verified_metadata.title: Towards generalizable energy forecasting: A cluster-based CNN-LSTM-Attention model for nation-wide and heterogeneous residential data
verified_metadata.abstract: Forecasting energy demand is essential to system operators or aggregators for informed decision making, such as balancing, where machine learning methods have shown appealing performance for single load points. However, the energy demand forecasting of nationwide households is complex and difficult to generalize due to diverse climatic conditions, socio-demographic and behavioral variations. This paper proposes a scalable and generalizable cluster-based forecasting framework that integrates a hybrid CNN-LSTM-Attention model to forecast nationwide large-scale demand. The proposed model combines LSTM for capturing long-term dependencies, CNN for extracting local patterns, and multi-head attention for refining feature selection, ensuring more precise forecasting. Given the high dimensionality of hyperparameters in such hybrid models, the Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA) is employed to efficiently optimize model configurations while reducing computational costs. To improve forecasting stability and generalizability across heterogeneous household groups, we introduce a k-means clustering approach that segments households based on electricity consumption behavior. This method reduces variability within groups, leading to significantly improved predictive accuracy. Additionally, comprehensive feature engineering enriches timestamped energy data with temporal attributes, further enhancing model performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed SSA-CNN-LSTM-Attention model achieves up to 86.4% reduction in RMSE compared to baseline models in single-step forecasting and maintains strong performance in multi-step scenarios. The cluster-based framework further enhances accuracy, reducing RMSE by an average of 32%, with some clusters exceeding 50% improvement. Moreover, SSA enables efficient hyperparameter tuning, achieving a low RMSE of 0.025 and SMAPE of 4.937 within 2166.5 s, significantly outperforming other optimization methods in both speed and consistency. This research provides a scalable and effective solution for real-world residential energy management.

verified_metadata.title: An AI-driven triaxial self-powered sensing system for attitude safety monitoring of aerial robots
verified_metadata.abstract: This study reports a triaxial self-powered sensing system for attitude safety monitoring (TSPS-AM) in aerial robots. The system uses a three-axis, four-channel architecture that couples triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) and electromagnetic generator (EMG) mechanisms, enabling its sensing units to detect triaxial acceleration, pitch, and roll without an external power supply. Validation confirms that TSPS-AM exhibits excellent linear fitting relationships within the horizontal acceleration range of 1–15 m/s2 and vertical acceleration range of 1–10 m/s2, and can monitor pitch and roll angles. Integrated with a lightweight CNN + GRU + Attention deep learning model, the system enables high-resolution multi-parameter identification, achieving resolutions of 0.1 Hz, 0.1 mm, and 2° for vibration frequency, amplitude, and excitation direction, and 0.1 Hz, 1°, and 2° for tilt frequency, tilt angle, and excitation direction. The identification accuracy of all parameters ranges from 93.34% to 99.33%. When used as an energy-harvesting unit, it delivered a peak output power of 0.0711 mW, corresponding to a power density of 273 mW m−3. After 60,000 cycles, the coefficient of variation of the output voltage for each channel remained below 5%, indicating good output stability. Finally, the trained model is deployed at the computer edge node with a Python-based terminal interface, and experimental tests confirm it effectively identifies and visualizes 9 typical aerial robot flight motions with 99.96% accuracy. In summary, TSPS-AM integrates self-powered sensing, data transmission, identification, and monitoring, laying a foundation for future attitude monitoring and collision-risk assessment in aerial robots.

verified_metadata.title: A generation method of meteorological year for photovoltaic buildings based on AR-LSTM with an improved diffuse estimation model
verified_metadata.abstract: In recent years, China's renewable energy has developed rapidly, and photovoltaic buildings are an important form of renewable energy utilization. In order to conduct better preliminary energy-saving design and assessment for photovoltaic buildings, it is necessary to establish the meteorological year for photovoltaic buildings. Firstly, regarding the research on the radiation meteorological years of existing photovoltaic buildings, most of the studies focus on the global solar radiation as a meteorological parameter, while ignoring the two components of the global solar radiation when it reaches the horizontal surface: direct radiation and diffuse radiation. These two components have significant impacts on photovoltaic power generation under different weather conditions. Although there are a large number of existing studies on diffuse radiation estimation models, the current research does not take into account the influence of various factors in the atmosphere and the transparency of clouds. The accuracy of the diffuse radiation estimation model still needs to be improved. Second, the meteorological parameters involved in constructing the meteorological year for photovoltaic buildings all have strong temporal characteristics. In particular, direct radiation and diffuse radiation have the characteristics of rapid changes and high volatility. The existing methods for generating the radiation meteorological years are unable to meet the requirements of accurately capturing the temporal characteristics, rapid changes, and high volatility of these meteorological parameters. Therefore, this paper has accomplished the following works: (1)Based on the model of the diffusion fraction and diffusion coefficient after adding precipitation. By introducing cloud transmittance and atmospheric quality coefficient as input parameters, the accuracy of the existing diffuse radiation estimation model was further improved. (2)The method combining the autoregressive model and the long short-term memory network model (AR-LSTM) is adopted. The AR-LSTM model uses AR model to capture the short-term variation patterns in the radiation data, and LSTM model to capture the long-term patterns of solar radiation changes. Selecting the typical months from the long-term data that can represent the long-term average characteristics of meteorological factors such as direct radiation and diffuse radiation, thereby constructing the meteorological year for photovoltaic buildings. This paper conducts verification experiments using four cities as examples in the solar radiation zoning: Golmud and Lhasa in Zone Ⅰ, and Kashgar and Urumqi in Zone Ⅱ. The results show:①The R2 (coefficient of determination) values of the improved diffuse radiation estimation models for the four cities ranged 0.96–0.99, showing a good fit with the actual values; the values of RMSE (root mean square error) and MABE (mean absolute deviation error) were 0.007–0.021, indicating good prediction accuracy; the value of MBE (mean deviation error) was close to the actual values for all four cities. ②The fitting degree R2 of the various main meteorological parameters (dry bulb temperature, relative humidity, direct radiation and diffuse radiation) of the meteorological year for photovoltaic buildings in the four cities to the long-term average values ranged 0.78–0.99, indicating a good fit to the long-term average values. The AR-LSTM model shows better performance in terms of direct and diffuse radiation compared to Bi-LSTM, LSTM, RF, and XGBoost model. For other meteorological parameters, the relative error range of the AR-LSTM model from the long-term average is 0.02%-4.94%. The AR-LSTM model demonstrates a stronger advantage in maintaining the long-term statistical characteristics of the key radiation input variables for photovoltaic buildings.

verified_metadata.title: Online adaptation via incremental clustering for cross-domain chiller fault diagnosis
verified_metadata.abstract: The chiller is a critical component of the heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems, and its fault diagnosis is essential for reducing building energy consumption. However, frequent working condition variations degrade the performance of traditional parametric models. Recently, cross-domain fault diagnosis methods have been used to address condition drift in chillers. However, traditional algorithms face two main limitations: (1) inefficiency in real-time prediction due to the need for iterative training on full target domain data, and (2) inability to cover all possible operating conditions. This paper proposes a real-time adaptive fault diagnosis algorithm based on cross-condition information fusion. Firstly, sensor data are fused into a mutual information matrix, and a predictive uncertainty separation algorithm divides the data into low-entropy and high-entropy samples. Low-entropy samples are labeled based on the previous time model, while high-entropy samples are processed through a memory buffer-based feature fusion space. Additionally, a prototype-based representation consistency method aligns online and historical data to fuse information across working conditions, enabling adaptation to changing conditions. Simultaneously, real-time incremental clustering ensures feature alignment for the same fault categories across batches. Experimental results demonstrate the model’s excellent real-time fault diagnosis performance in chillers.

verified_metadata.title: Comparative analysis of machine learning techniques for workplane illuminance estimation and photosensor placement assessment in DLCs
verified_metadata.abstract: Daylight-linked control systems (DLCs) can provide several advantages. Nonetheless, several variables (e.g. sensor location and commissioning configuration) have a substantial influence on the behaviour of the system. One way to find good correlations between the illuminance measured on one surface and the one on the workplane is to use artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, namely machine learning (ML) approaches. This study develops and compares seven ML models for workplane illuminance estimation in a DLCs context. The analysis explicitly evaluates the effect of photosensor location on estimation performance by considering two ceiling photosensor cases (C1 and C2). The ML algorithms, including XGBoost, gradient boosting, LSTM, FFANN, random forest, decision tree and KNN, are implemented and evaluated in terms of key performance metrics such as MAE, RMSE and R2. To align the comparison with DLCs operation, a range-based assessment has also been performed in the control-relevant 300–1000 lx band, and a setpoint-based dim/no-dim decision evaluation has been conducted at 500 lx. The results reveal that the XGBoost model provides the best full-range regression performance across the complete illuminance dataset, achieving test R2 greater than 0.97 for different test scenarios. Moreover, the setpoint-based analysis highlights that KNN achieves the highest dimming decision accuracy near the 500 lx threshold in both sensor cases, indicating that models with similar regression metrics can differ in control reliability. These findings support a control-oriented and deployment-relevant interpretation of model selection for DLCs, beyond generic algorithm benchmarking.

verified_metadata.title: Hybrid statistical and machine learning optimization of continuous pyrolysis to maximize bio-oil production
verified_metadata.abstract: Process optimization is a crucial step in biomass conversion to maximize product yield and control product properties, particularly for bio-oil production. In this study, a hybrid statistical and machine learning (HSML) approach, combining response surface methodology (RSM) with Gaussian process regression (GPR) and support vector regression (SVR), was applied to maximize bio-oil yield during continuous pyrolysis using local common reed as feedstock. Quadratic model fitting and statistical analysis via RSM were first discussed, followed by the hyperparameter tuning and interpretation of machine learning (ML) algorithms. Comparison of predicted and experimental yields confirmed the reliability and feasibility of the HSML approach. The optimal conditions were identified as temperature at 490 °C, carrier gas flow rate at 220 SCCM, and feeding rate at 10.8 RPM (1.5 g min−1), with predicted bio-oil yields of 39.82 wt% (RSM), 39.84 wt% (GPR), and 39.97 wt% (SVR), respectively. The validation experiments under optimal conditions also yielded a comparable result of 39.90 ± 0.35 wt%. The bio-oils, including light and heavy fractions, obtained from optimal conditions were characterized, including elemental composition, functional group, and chemical composition. Light bio-oil showed high oxygen content (72.36 wt%) and was rich in oxygenated compounds, especially acids (31.01 %) and aldehydes (16.97 %). Conversely, heavy bio-oil contained more carbon (61.70 wt%) with phenolic compounds (41.37 %) dominating. Besides, particle size was found to influence both yield and oil quality, where smaller particles (<250 μm) increased bio-oil yield (40.40 wt%) and reduced large oxygenates in the light fraction. Overall, the findings demonstrate HSML as a powerful tool for pyrolysis optimization and bio-oil maximization.

verified_metadata.title: Forecasting crude oil price volatility utilizing multivariate decomposition and deep learning approaches: Considering the role of influencing factors
verified_metadata.abstract: This paper attempts to identify the main influencing factors of the realized volatility (RV) for West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil spot price from three categories: commodity attribute factors, alternative energy factors, and macro uncertainty factors, so as to develop a multi-factor hybrid forecasting model. We integrated extremely randomized trees (ERT) with multivariate variational mode decomposition (MVMD) and temporal convolutional network (TCN) to construct an innovative ERT-MVMD-TCN model. Firstly, the ERT method is employed to select essential factors from candidate influencing variables as the main input features of the forecasting model. Secondly, MVMD is utilized to simultaneously decompose both the RV and the screened input variables into subsequences that reflect different scale features. Subsequently, the TCN with stable forecasting ability is applied to forecast each subsequence separately to effectively capture the time dependence. All individual forecasts are compiled to form the final prediction of RV. Finally, the forecasting performance of the model is evaluated through four loss functions: mean absolute error (MAE), mean square error (MSE), heteroscedastic adjusted MAE (HMAE), heteroscedastic adjusted MSE (HMSE) and modified Diebold and Mariano test (MDM). The empirical findings not only demonstrate the superior accuracy of the proposed ERT-MVMD-TCN model over the comparative single and hybrid models, but also maintain a robust predictive advantage across different forecast horizons and volatility periods. Hence, in the context of the current complex crude oil market, the proposed ERT-MVMD-TCN model presents a wide range of application prospects in crude oil price volatility prediction, which offers valuable insights for decision-making to both market participants and policymakers.

title: Simulation based validation of a reinforcement learning-based operation strategy for sector-coupled district heating system
abstract: Heating represents a major share of energy use in Germany, making it a critical sector in the energy transition. District heating systems (DHS) are key to decarbonising heat supply, particularly when integrating renewable energy sources and sector-coupled components. However, exploiting this flexibility requires advanced operational strategies. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly reinforcement learning (RL), offers a promising approach, but its performance must be validated under realistic operating conditions before deployment. This study presents a structured framework for evaluating AI-driven operational strategies using a physics-based dynamic simulation model of a real German DHS. A detailed digital twin was developed in MATLAB/Simulink using the Simscape toolbox, capturing thermo-hydraulic behaviour of heat pumps, stratified thermal energy storage, electric heating rods, a gas boiler, and the network. The AI model, based on reinforcement learning, determines generation dispatch with the objective of increasing renewable utilisation and reducing fossil backup operation. The simulation model is first validated against measured operation for four characteristic historical weeks, establishing a reliable physical reference. Baseline and AI-controlled operation are then compared under identical boundary conditions. Results show robust AI performance under moderate and warm conditions, while systematic underdelivery occurs during colder and highly dynamic periods, revealing limitations of the simplified training environment. The findings demonstrate that high-fidelity dynamic simulation provides a robust, risk-free environment for pre-deployment validation of AI-based control strategies in sector-coupled DHS.

verified_metadata.title: Multi-objective context-aware deep reinforcement learning for energy flexible control of a large multizone office building under extreme heatwave conditions
verified_metadata.abstract: The increasing frequency and severity of climate-driven heatwaves intensifies cooling demand in buildings, exacerbating peak electricity loads and threatening grid stability. Large multizone office buildings pose challenges with complex thermal dynamics, delayed HVAC responses and strict thermal comfort requirements. Reinforcement learning has shown promise for building energy management, but existing studies focus on nominal weather conditions, small scale buildings, dual-objective optimization and instantaneous state representations, limiting their performance under extreme heat events. To address these gaps, this research proposes a context-aware deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework based on Soft Actor-Critic to enhance energy flexibility in large multizone office building during heatwaves. The approach includes historical HVAC actions and zone temperatures to capture delayed thermal responses with instantaneous states. It also leverages exogenous weather and electricity price forecasts and dynamic occupancy context. A tri-objective optimization minimizes cooling energy cost, occupant discomfort and peak power demand. Photovoltaic and thermal energy storage are accommodated to support load shifting and grid-responsive operation. The framework is evaluated using EnergyPlus-Python co-simulation with real weather and electricity market data during the 2023 Cerberus heatwave in Italy. Compared to rule-based control, it achieves a 76.55% mean reduction in occupant discomfort, 17.15% reduction in energy costs, 16.45% reduction in total energy consumption and 15.28% reduction in peak power demand. Energy flexibility metrics indicate load shifting index of 20.55% and self-consumption ratio of 95.46%. These results demonstrate the potential of context-aware DRL as a robust and scalable strategy for grid-responsive buildings under increasingly frequent and severe heatwaves.

verified_metadata.title: Energy storage capacity optimization for dual-transformer highway service areas with cross-side photovoltaic–storage–charging coordination
verified_metadata.abstract: Highway service areas increasingly face the combined challenges of growing electric vehicle charging demand, photovoltaic generation variability, and separated power-supply infrastructures. In many practical service-area systems, commercial base loads and electric vehicle charging loads are supplied through independent transformers, which restricts the flexible sharing of photovoltaic generation and energy storage resources. To address this issue, this paper proposes a cross-side coordinated photovoltaic-storage-charging architecture for dual-side independent highway service areas, in which photovoltaic generation and the energy storage system can dynamically switch between the commercial/base-load side and the electric vehicle charging side. A bi-level collaborative optimization model is developed for energy storage capacity configuration. The upper level evaluates candidate storage capacities, while the lower level uses a Soft Actor–Critic-based scheduling strategy to optimize photovoltaic connection, energy storage connection, and charging/discharging decisions under coupled discrete switching and continuous power-control actions. A Capacity Optimization–Soft Actor–Critic framework, termed CO-SAC, is further developed with delayed update and fast warm-up mechanisms to improve training stability and convergence efficiency. Case studies using data from the Changxing Service Area on the G50 Shanghai–Chongqing Expressway show that the proposed dual-side coordinated switching mode achieves the lowest daily total cost of 3607.19 CNY, corresponding to reductions of 5.02%, 31.90%, 4.14%, 27.29%, 4.03%, and 4.70% compared with six benchmark operation modes. The CO-SAC framework identifies an optimal storage capacity of 1600 kWh. Compared with Deep Q-Network (DQN) and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), the daily total costs obtained by these two algorithms are 6.02% and 4.70% higher than that obtained by CO-SAC, respectively. The results demonstrate that cross-side PV–ESS coordination can improve economic performance, PV utilization, and operational flexibility in dual-transformer highway service area energy systems.

title: Mechanism-driven random forest adaptive discrete global search versus response surface methodology: A comparative study for multi-objective optimization of combined-cycle turbine startup
abstract: Optimizing the startup process of combined-cycle steam turbines poses a complex multi-objective, multivariate challenge. Despite the development of numerous optimization approaches, substantial inconsistencies often emerge due to variations in underlying optimization mechanisms and targeted objectives. To address this gap from a mechanistic perspective, this study developed two improved optimization strategies rooted in fundamentally distinct principles. The first, designated as the Mechanism-Driven Random Forest Adaptive Discrete Global Search (MD-RF-GS), is grounded in physical mechanism modeling and incorporates machine learning algorithms; the second, the Response Surface Methodology (RSM), is based on mathematical approximation techniques. Both approaches are applied to an identical standardized cold-start process to perform comprehensive global multi-objective optimization of the startup phase. A systematic comparative analysis is then conducted to assess the mechanisms and characteristics of the two methods across five critical dimensions: automation level, model interpretability, computational cost and response time, optimization accuracy and objectivity, and applicability scope. This work aims to provide actionable guidance for selecting appropriate startup optimization strategies under varying operating scenarios, and to improve the reliability and accuracy of optimization in practical engineering applications.

verified_metadata.title: Mechanism-driven random forest adaptive discrete global search versus response surface methodology: A comparative study for multi-objective optimization of combined-cycle turbine startup
verified_metadata.abstract: Optimizing combined-cycle steam turbine startups is a complex, multi-objective challenge. Existing optimization methods often yield inconsistent results due to differing underlying mechanisms. To address this, this study evaluates two fundamentally distinct strategies: a physical model-based Mechanism-Driven Random Forest Global Search and a mathematical approximation-based Response Surface Methodology. We apply both approaches to optimize a standardized cold-start process. The optimized trajectory significantly enhances performance, shortening the startup time by 12 min and reducing operational costs by 81,521 Yuan. Crucially, an operational power plant has successfully utilized this optimal trajectory for over a decade. Comprehensive macro- and micro-level physical inspections during scheduled teardowns—including exhaustive non-destructive testing (NDT) and metallographic analyses—revealed zero critical defects or thermal fatigue cracks in rotor components, definitively validating the long-term structural safety of the numerical models. Finally, a five-dimensional comparative analysis systematically assesses the mechanisms and trade-offs of both methods. This study offers field-proven guidance for selecting highly efficient and mechanically reliable startup optimization strategies under varying operational scenarios.

verified_metadata.title: Deep reinforcement learning-based switchable energy management strategy for hydrogen-electric hybrid power system in UAV applications considering uncertain operating conditions
verified_metadata.abstract: The proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) and lithium battery hybrid power system (HPS) can effectively improve endurance for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). However, UAVs often operate under uncertain operating conditions, where random and dynamic variations in load demand can significantly affect HPS performance. An effective energy management strategy (EMS) that achieves a balance between stability and adaptability is essential for the HPS. Herein, we propose a data-augmented rule-embedded double deep Q-network (DARE-DDQN) energy management approach for hydrogen-electric HPSs in UAV applications. By optimizing the switching rules of a rule-based EMS through DDQN, the proposed approach improves adaptability to uncertain operating conditions while maintaining control stability. First, an HPS model for the hydrogen-electric hybrid UAV is established as the training environment for deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Considering the uncertain operating conditions of UAVs, representative power demand modes are identified through a sliding-window operational clustering (SWOC) method. The DRL training environment is enriched with random operating conditions created by combining representative power demand modes and data augmentation. On this basis, a two-stage DDQN-assisted rule-based EMS is developed to optimize rule thresholds and adaptively switch the PEMFC output mode according to UAV operating conditions, enabling efficient and stable HPS operation. Finally, uncertain flight conditions of the UAV are used to validate the effectiveness of the DARE-DDQN energy management approach. Under unknown operating conditions, the proposed approach achieves superior performance over the baseline EMSs, reducing total hydrogen consumption by more than 3.91% and decreasing the PEMFC estimated degradation indicator by more than 2.91%.

verified_metadata.title: A multi-mode operational simulation and 4E analysis approach to ammonia production in a solar- and energy storage–driven system with LS-boosting machine learning for multi-criteria optimization and a case study
verified_metadata.abstract: The development of sustainable ammonia production through solar-driven integrated systems faces several critical challenges, including effective subsystem integration, validation under realistic operating conditions, and determination of the most suitable operational strategy. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an innovative solar-assisted ammonia production system based on parabolic trough solar collectors and performs a quasi-steady-state simulation that accounts for daily solar irradiance fluctuations under three operational modes. Afterward, a comprehensive 4E assessment framework is employed, encompassing energy, exergy, exergoeconomic, and exergoenvironmental analyses, with the latter based on life cycle assessment methodology. In addition, a hybrid optimization approach, integrating least-squares boosting machine learning and a multi-objective grey wolf optimizer (MOGWO), is applied to identify the optimum performance. The selected objective functions are ammonia production rate, total investment cost rate, and total exergoenvironmental impact rate. The optimization results yield optimal values of 1457 kg/day, 197.5 $/h, and 383.9 mPts/h, respectively. To evaluate practical applicability, the optimized system is investigated under the climatic conditions of Yazd and Bandar Abbas. Under optimal operating conditions, the above-mentioned objectives are found to be 1068.08 kg/day, 184.37 $/h, and 339.29 mPts/h for Yazd, respectively, while corresponding values for Bandar Abbas are 735.91 kg/day, 172.82 $/h, and 306.95 mPts/h.

verified_metadata.title: A rolling-regulated capacity market for mid-to-long-term inertia adequacy with machine learning forecasting
verified_metadata.abstract: In high-proportion renewable energy power systems, the declining share of synchronous generation reduces system inertia and seriously threatens frequency stability. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a rolling inertia-regulated capacity market mechanism that ensures mid-to-long-term inertia adequacy through market-based resource allocation. The mechanism treats inertia as a quantifiable service and uses price signals to incentivize investment in inertia-providing resources. A PLS-GBDT forecasting model is developed to evaluate mid-to-long-term inertia requirements, and a variable reliability requirement curve is formulated based on the forecasted inertia security level. A dynamic rolling update market mechanism is designed to periodically reassess inertia demand and adjust the capacity market clearing accordingly. An inertia-constrained capacity market clearing model is then constructed and solved using strong duality theory and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions. The proposed mechanism is validated on a modified IEEE 39-bus system. Simulation results demonstrate that the rolling inertia-regulated capacity market effectively maintains frequency stability under high renewable penetration, reduces the risk of inertia under-procurement, and provides a practical engineering solution for frequency security in future power systems.

verified_metadata.title: Transformer-based power forecasting and federated learning-driven fault detection with a quantum-inspired solar power optimization in smart grids
verified_metadata.abstract: This paper presents a unified smart-grid framework integrating solar forecasting, fault detection, and energy optimization using adaptive attention, federated learning, and quantum-inspired algorithms. The architecture combines TransDimNet with an Adaptive Multi-Resolution Attention Mechanism (AMRAM) to model temporal dependencies from solar irradiance, weather, and consumption data, improving solar prediction. A Bayesian Neural Network with Monte Carlo Dropout estimates Fourier-transformed features, while Federated Learning enables decentralized fault detection and predictive maintenance across grid components. Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning optimizes task prioritization, and Quantum-Inspired Neural Networks with a Decentralized Hierarchical Fuzzy Decision Framework perform dynamic load balancing and energy optimization. Validation on NREL, PVUSA, and GAN-generated datasets demonstrates superior performance. The framework achieves R2 of 0.92, per-panel MAE of 0.245 kW, RMSE of 0.312 kW, and MAPE of 4.5%, outperforming existing hybrid models by 15–20% (p < 0.05). Fault detection attains 99% precision, 98% recall, and 99% accuracy, surpassing baselines by 3–5%. The QINN–DHFD combination delivers 98% grid efficiency and 20% reduction in energy loss under fluctuating conditions. These results establish the proposed framework as a robust, scalable solution for enhancing sustainability and resilience in next-generation renewable energy systems.

verified_metadata.title: AI-assisted aerodynamic enhancement in low-speed wind energy harvesting: A case study on Archimedes spiral turbines
verified_metadata.abstract: The increasing demand for decentralized clean energy has increased interest in small-scale wind turbines that can operate efficiently in urban environments defined by weak wind conditions. Among these types of turbines, the Archimedes Spiral Wind Turbine (ASWT) has gained attention due to its structural simplicity and favorable aerodynamic behavior. In this study, data-driven methods used in conjunction with a genetic algorithm were implemented to enhance the aerodynamic design of this type of turbine. A dataset consisting of 1790 samples corresponding to different geometric and operational parameters was generated via computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations and used to develop predictive models for turbine performance. The predictive model demonstrated robust performance, achieving a coefficient of determination of R2 = 0.91. Furthermore, the subsequent data analysis revealed that the Tip Speed Ratio (TSR) is the most influential operational parameter governing the turbine's aerodynamic efficiency. Utilizing the validated predictive model, a genetic algorithm was deployed to fine-tune the structural parameters with the ultimate goal of maximizing energy capture. This optimization resulted in an average CP improvement of 9.24% across the tested wind velocity range compared to the baseline configuration, effectively shifting the turbine's peak performance to the upper bound of the designated low-speed urban wind regime. These outcomes suggest that strategic geometric alterations are capable of boosting energy extraction capabilities across the entire low-speed spectrum, thereby highlighting the efficacy of machine learning-assisted frameworks in refining ASWT performance.

verified_metadata.title: Optimized thermal management and power prediction of thermoelectric modules using diverse cooling designs and fluids with deep learning integration
verified_metadata.abstract: This paper presents a numerical study of a thermoelectric module using COMSOL to evaluate its performance under different cooling strategies. Thermal management is key to optimize thermoelectric generators (TEGs) performance, particularly, by maintaining a constant temperature gradient along the module. Four heat sink configurations were examined to improve heat dissipation on the cold side: a simple flat heat sink, a heat sink with longitudinal fins, a converging-diverging channel, and a zigzag channel. Furthermore, four cooling fluids (air, helium, water and oil) with different thermal characteristics were selected to compare their cooling performance. The simulation results were compared with the previously published experimental and computational results in order to verify the correctness of the simulation model. The model is capable of reliably predicting both thermal and electrical behavior of the TEG. The configuration with water as a coolant and the heat sink with longitudinal fins tested was the one that had the best performance, significantly improving the heat dissipation and boosting the power output. Further analysis was performed under different operational conditions including different hot-side temperatures (up to 300°C) and external load resistances. The maximum power of 7.92 W was achieved at 300°C, highlighting the importance of high temperature difference for effective power conversion. Moreover, deep learning models were used to predict electrical indices such as voltage, current and power with a high precision. This data-driven predictive approach based on machine learning enhances the system adaptability and provides insights for the future intelligent energy harvesting applications.

verified_metadata.title: LSTM-based weighted approach for TMY generation in extreme Antarctic climate
verified_metadata.abstract: Under Antarctica's highly complex climatic conditions, characterizing building-relevant meteorological variability and constructing typical meteorological year (TMY) datasets for distinct climate zones are essential for climate-adaptive research stations. However, existing TMY methods rely on fixed weighting schemes and cannot capture the nonstationary spatiotemporal variability of Antarctic meteorological parameters or the nonlinear coupling among climatic factors affecting building loads, leading to deviations in building performance simulations. To address this issue, a continuous meteorological dataset was developed from PANDA observations supplemented with satellite and reanalysis products. Three building climate zones are identified, including plateau extreme cold, steep-slope extreme wind, and coastal severe cold zones, and five representative stations are selected. A building-response-informed weighting scheme based on long short-term memory (LSTM) is introduced to replace the fixed empirical weights in the Sandia method. Results show that temperature is the most influential meteorological parameter. Compared with the fixed temperature weight of 0.2 in the conventional Sandia method, its weight increases to approximately 0.6 in the plateau extreme cold zone, reducing the mean absolute error (MAE) of building energy simulation by 0.2 kWh/m2. Compared with conventional methods used in low- and mid-latitude regions, the proposed approach yields TMY results that better match long-term meteorological records and multi-year average building energy consumption, with maximum root mean square error (RMSE) reductions of 3.08 °C and 0.96 kWh/m2. The Sandia-LSTM method provides a building-response-informed approach to weighting-factor determination for TMY generation in extreme climates and supplies representative annual weather inputs for Antarctic building-energy assessment.

title: Preference-conditioned reinforcement learning for balancing occupant comfort and energy efficiency in adaptive residential HVAC control under changing preferences
abstract: In the context of carbon neutrality, enhancing energy efficiency in residential buildings is pivotal for achieving emission reduction targets. Although improving thermal insulation effectively reduces thermal loads, the performance of Air Source Heat Pumps (ASHPs) often degrades under low-load conditions. While conventional Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) can optimize equipment operation, its reliance on pre-defined and static reward functions makes it difficult to adapt to the dynamic and subjective comfort preferences of occupants. To address this limitation, this study proposes a preference-conditioned DRL framework for adaptive HVAC control and implements a large-language-model-based natural language interface for preference input. The framework translates short occupant feedback into explicit preference constraints, enabling flexible and personalized adjustment of comfort–energy trade-offs. To verify the practical feasibility of the proposed method, a hardware integration platform based on Raspberry Pi was developed and deployed in a real-world residential setting. In the field tests, the proposed system achieved a 21% reduction in daily energy consumption under fixed-preference control and a 14% reduction under time-varying preference control compared with the corresponding baseline methods, while maintaining personalized occupant comfort. These findings highlight the potential of adaptive preference-aware HVAC control for improving residential energy efficiency while supporting personalized comfort requirements.

verified_metadata.title: Full-scale thermal modeling enabled by interpretable deep learning for energy-efficient in-row cooling data center
verified_metadata.abstract: This study establishes a full-scale coupled thermal-fluid-humidity model and an interpretable deep learning framework to achieve accurate temperature prediction and optimized cooling control across room, rack, server, and chip levels in data centers. Experimental measurements under raised-floor cooling validate the accuracy of the model. CFD based comparative analyses are performed between raised-floor cooling and in-row cooling systems. The full-scale model reveals strong coupling between internal server airflow and rack-level external airflow. Multiscale mappings under varying supply air parameters and spatial locations are studied. The results show that the CPU temperature is primarily governed by the supply air temperature and exhibits a uniform thermal response to temperature variation, whereas the GPU temperature is highly sensitive to spatial nonuniformity. An interpretable convolutional neural network-long short-term memory model with a custom attention module, incorporating a random sliding-window sampling mechanism, is developed to achieve rapid and accurate temperature prediction. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis the contributions of local and global features, indicating that the local temperature at the server inlet is the dominant driver of hotspot formation. Finally, a coupled optimization strategy based on supply air temperature and workload difference is proposed, and a supply air energy saving curve is established. At a supply air temperature of 23 °C, the maximum temperature at the chip level is reduced from 86.70 °C to 66.02 °C. The proposed full-scale temperature prediction and energy saving control strategy eliminates hotspots and over-cooling, enabling precise supply air temperature control and energy-efficient operation in data centers.

verified_metadata.title: Photon flux uniformity-oriented design and machine learning prediction of CPC-based low-concentration PV/T systems
verified_metadata.abstract: Due to its cost-effectiveness and comparatively more uniform irradiance distribution than many high-concentration solar concentrators, the Compound Parabolic Concentrator (CPC) is regarded as a promising technology for low-concentration photovoltaic/thermal (LCPV/T) applications. While existing literature recognizes the significance of concentrator design—such as employing height truncation to achieve the dual benefits of reduced manufacturing cost and optimized optical concentration—a comprehensive investigation into the underlying mechanism by which design parameters influence the output characteristics of PV/T systems and the spatial uniformity of the photovoltaic surface remains absent. This work presents a systematic investigation into concentrator design parameters, including horizontal shift, vertical shift, truncation ratio, and rotation angle. By integrating Monte Carlo ray-tracing (MCRT) simulations with experimental validation, the influence of these individual and coupled factors on flux uniformity and PV/T performance was elucidated. Furthermore, a single neural network and a Genetic Algorithm-optimized Backpropagation (GA-BP) neural network were developed to predict photon distribution under complex concentrator designs. Finally, the generalization capabilities of three modeling approaches—RSM, BP, and GA-BP—were evaluated and validated through comparative analysis. The established optimization framework might support rational and low-cost structural design of CPCs with verified stable prediction performance. Furthermore, this work provides theoretical support for optimizing machine learning models to realize targeted parameter adjustment.

verified_metadata.title: An evidence-integrated explainable AI approach to eco-suitability zoning and geographical potential assessment for large-scale wind power construction
verified_metadata.abstract: The development of frameworks for large-scale energy construction zoning, considering geographical potential, is pivotal for achieving carbon neutrality goals. Existing wind power development environmental impact studies have predominantly focused on microscale analyses, lacking the incorporation of eco-environment factors into wind power development planning at a macro level. This study presented a hybrid evidence-integrated explainable AI framework for eco-suitability zoning prediction, combining a rule-based indicator prior with documented real-world anchors and four nonlinear learners. It introduced SHapley additive explanations and feature importance analysis to quantitatively elucidate the relationships between eco-environment factors and wind power suitability zoning and served as a link between mitigation and adaptation measures in the context of global climate change. Twenty suitability indicators were incorporated, and a quantitative evaluation method generated twenty raster data layers as inputs for subsequent models. Prediction accuracies for suitability zoning reached 93.36%, 96.50%, 97.17%, and 97.46% for XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and CNN, respectively. Notably, CatBoost demonstrated consistent performance across all scores, while CNN excelled in accurately identifying very unsuitable and very suitable zones. The explainable artificial intelligence revealed that desertification sensitivity and road proximity are the most influential factors in suitability zoning, whereas socio-economic indicators exert minimal impact. Applying the framework to the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau revealed that 71.4% of the area is very unsuitable for wind farm construction, but the total geographical potential remains substantial at 1.90 × 106 GWh. These findings suggest prioritizing the development of the 11.32% highly suitable areas, following detailed micro-site assessments, to meet nationally determined contributions targets and effectively mitigate global warming.

verified_metadata.title: An experimental and deep neural network-based analysis of the combustion and emission characteristics of an ammonia-diesel dual-fuel engine under a lean condition with various ammonia energy fractions
verified_metadata.abstract: Ammonia is a promising carbon-free fuel for engines in response to the era of carbon neutrality. This study investigates the combustion and emission characteristics of an ammonia–diesel dual-fuel engine operated under lean and relatively low medium-speed conditions, with diesel injection timing and ammonia energy fractions as the primary parameters. Based on this, a deep neural network model was developed to predict critical parameters of the ammonia–diesel dual-fuel engine. The results indicate that applying delayed diesel injection timing enhanced the efficiency of the ammonia–diesel dual-fuel engine, including brake thermal efficiency. However, for ammonia energy fractions exceeding A50, the highest efficiency was observed at an earlier diesel injection timing of 12°CA BTDC rather than at the most delayed timing of 9°CA BTDC. Delayed diesel injection timing and higher ammonia energy fractions extended ignition delay, yet the shortening of the late combustion phase contributed significantly to reducing total combustion duration, thereby improving efficiency. While delayed diesel injection timing lowered NO, NOx, and CO emissions at the same ammonia energy fractions, it deteriorated N2O and NH3 emissions. NO2 and CO2 emissions displayed either pronounced nonlinearity or minimal sensitivity to diesel injection timing. The optimized deep neural network model achieved R2 values of 0.999, 0.996, 0.9733, 0.9635, 0.9471, and 0.934 for in-cylinder pressure, heat release rate, brake thermal efficiency, indicated mean effective pressure, NOx, and NH3, respectively, demonstrating exceptional predictive accuracy. These outcomes provide valuable guidance for advancing experimental and AI-driven approaches to optimize combustion, efficiency, and emission control in ammonia–diesel dual-fuel engines.

verified_metadata.title: Machine Learning-Assisted Multi-Objective Optimization of a COG-Based CHP–Methanol Polygeneration System with Exergo-Environmental Assessment
verified_metadata.abstract: Coke oven gas (COG) serves as a high-energy density feedstock for integrated industrial processes. The present study suggests a new plant involving a combined heat and power (CHP) plant coupled with COG based methanol synthesis process. The method used is multi-stage thermal integration and flue gas recirculation to reduce carbon emissions and increase product output. It consists of fuel burner, methanol synthesis unit, organic Rankine cycle and ammonia Rankine cycle. The suggested system is simulated and examined from the perspectives of thermo-enviro-economic analysis using Aspen HYSYS. The baseline analysis results show that the overall exergy efficiency is 41.81% and the overall energy efficiency is 56.59%. The environmental analysis gives a CO_{2} footprint of 0.182 tons/MWh while the economic analysis results in a levelized cost of energy (LCOE) of 0.165 $/kWh and a net present value (NPV) of 50.03 M$. To surpass the baseline performance, a machine-learning framework was utilized to create an accurate surrogate model to perform faster analysis, and then, using the Non-dominated Sorting Whale Optimization Algorithm, a four-objective optimization was performed. By presenting an optimal-compromise solution, the optimization indicates a significant performance improvement, resulting in a lower CO_{2} footprint of 0.151 tons/MWh, LCOE of 0.11 $/kWh, NPV of 74.75 M$, and exergy efficiency of 43.79%. Sensitivity and uncertainty analyses also showed that o-Xylene pressure fuel rate, and reactor pressure were the most crucial factor in the system's performance. The results indicate that the proposed COG-based polygeneration process, which has been refined with the aid of the advanced framework, is a low-emission, efficient, and economical procedure to generate heat, power, and methanol.

title: Attitudes toward climate change to demand-driven energy mitigation: A machine-learning approach
abstract: Promoting mitigation behaviors among the public is a fundamental step in addressing climate change, yet such efforts have achieved uneven success across demographic groups. This paper surveys the literature on the relationship between personal attitudes toward climate change and mitigation behaviors, with a particular focus on demand-side energy consumption reductions. An interpretative framework for understanding the key drivers of and barriers to common mitigation strategies is provided. Applying a machine-learning approach to survey data from 23 European countries to disentangle the relative importance of attitudinal predictors, the analysis finds that perceived personal responsibility for climate change is the single most powerful predictor of energy-conscious behavior. This paper thus offers a useful guide to understanding successful approaches to incentivizing climate-friendly action within this regional context.

verified_metadata.title: Cooperative optimization of energy and thermal management in PHEV using a time-correlated Laplacian noise-based reinforcement learning framework
verified_metadata.abstract: Plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) are a key force driving the low-carbon energy transition in the 21st century, and their performance is closely tied to the energy management strategy (EMS). However, focusing solely on EMS may cause thermal safety issues in PHEVs. To address this problem, this paper proposes an intelligent control method based on time-correlated Laplacian noise, termed TLP-TD3, for the cooperative optimization of thermal management in PHEV electric drive systems and vehicle energy management. The method innovatively introduces TLP exploration noise, which, by virtue of its time correlation and the peaked, heavy-tailed characteristics of the Laplacian distribution, exhibits superior exploration and regulation capabilities. By innovatively integrating TLP noise with the TD3 reinforcement learning (RL) agent, the exploration of optimal policies is enhanced, achieving cooperative optimization between thermal management and energy management. Experimental results under multiple driving cycles show that TLP-TD3 achieves a converged average reward of −3.11, at least 51.41% higher than other methods. Under two unseen cycles (HWFET and China_City + JN1015), while maintaining state-of-charge (SOC) within 0.6–0.3 and battery/motor temperatures within 40 °C and 85 °C, TLP-TD3 attains low equivalent fuel consumptions (EFCs) of 5.85 L/100 km and 3.43 L/100 km. Compared with baseline ECMS-RULE, it trades modest EFC increases of about 3.21% (China_City + JN1015) and 26.32% (HWFET) for better SOC maintenance and thermal safety, demonstrating good comprehensive performance under constraints. This work offers an efficient and stable RL solution for cooperative thermal-energy management of intelligent PHEVs.

verified_metadata.title: Multi-objective parameter optimization of a methanol-mediated carbon-closed power system assisted by a neural network prediction model
verified_metadata.abstract: A novel methanol-mediated carbon-closed power system integrating green methanol synthesis, carbon capture and utilization, and high-efficiency power generation is proposed to address the challenges of renewable energy intermittency and carbon emission reduction. The system couples alkaline electrolysis, methanol synthesis, methanol reforming, gas turbine combined cycle, and carbon capture into a highly integrated energy conversion framework. To efficiently optimize this complex system under strict operating constraints, a novel staged optimization framework combining a neural-network surrogate model with the NSGA-II algorithm is developed. High-efficiency energy utilization is achieved by employing extraction steam for reforming and carbon capture, facilitating a carbon-closed cycle by recycling captured CO2 for methanol synthesis. During the methanol synthesis system optimization phase, the NSGA-II algorithm identified optimal parameters that reduced the unit exergy cost and unit exergy carbon intensity of methanol by 3.5% and 2.01%, respectively, compared to the base case. For the methanol utilization system, a neural network surrogate model was introduced to achieve effective prediction of turbine inlet temperature and flue gas temperature constraints. This approach, validated against simulated values, eliminated over 90% of invalid operating cases and significantly accelerated the search process. Optimization results reveal that the unit exergy cost and unit exergy carbon intensity of power decreased by 1.4% and 6.2%, respectively. Ultimately, the system efficiency increased to 32.9%, reaching peak operational performance within the defined flue gas temperature constraints. The results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating neural-network-assisted optimization with carbon-closed energy systems and provide a scalable framework for future low-carbon energy system design.

verified_metadata.title: Artificial intelligence-based optimization of HVAC systems: Advances in thermal comfort, energy efficiency, energy consumption, challenges, and research gaps
verified_metadata.abstract: As buildings consume roughly a third of all the energy used in the world, improving their energy efficiency and environment-friendliness is essential. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods, especially machine learning and deep learning, have been gradually adopted over the last decade to handle the complexity of built-environment systems. This review summarizes the recent research on AI-driven integrated and holistic frameworks for building management. Functions such as occupancy detection and behavior modeling, energy consumption forecasting and optimization, indoor air quality and thermal comfort assessment, and fault detection and diagnosis must be examined to streamline the management of buildings and address interrelated heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning issues. While studies have evaluated the performance, modeling approaches, and methodological structures of AI-based techniques, identifying viable AI models remains challenging due to the rapid proliferation of algorithms across spatial scales, including system components, urban-level studies, temporal resolutions, and assessment metrics. Because of this methodological diversity, drawing direct comparisons and selecting optimal techniques for specific applications is difficult. Although AI techniques can improve the energy efficiency of buildings, most studies have focused on controlled laboratory settings or simulations, with few post-occupancy evaluations and real-world deployments. Standardized evaluation frameworks and practical guidelines are required to implement AI solutions in operational buildings. Based on the current study, from 2000 to 2026, the application of AI techniques and thermal comfort models has enabled energy saving on average 21.91 and 44.76% and comfort improvement on average between 21.77 and 85.95%. Finally, this paper discusses the challenges faced in the use of AI for energy productivity and comfort improvement and opens main future directions in relation with AI-based HVAC control systems for human comfort and energy-efficiency management.

verified_metadata.title: Unveiling multi-scenario land use-carbon nexus: Crested Porcupine Optimizer-enhanced deep learning model with attention mechanisms for predicting carbon emissions
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate projection of land-use-related carbon emissions is essential for regional low-carbon planning, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions where land conversion, energy consumption, and socio-economic development are closely intertwined. This study develops a multi-scenario modelling framework integrating energy-consumption forecasting, deep-learning-based carbon-emission prediction, and land-use simulation. City-specific grey forecasting models are used to project energy consumption associated with building land, whereas emissions from other land-use types are estimated using emission coefficients. A Crested Porcupine Optimizer (CPO)-enhanced CNN-GRU-Attention model integrates land-use, energy-consumption, socio-economic, environmental, and spatial-accessibility variables to represent nonlinear relationships and feature interactions in regional carbon-emission prediction. Opti-LEAS is used to estimate land-expansion probabilities, and a cellular-automata-based CARS module with multiple stochastic seeds simulates land-use changes under natural development, urban development, and ecological protection scenarios. The framework is applied to the Fenwei Plain, China. Most city-level energy-consumption sequences satisfy the suitability requirements of grey forecasting, and city-specific model variants are selected according to validation errors. Under the primary training-testing partition, the proposed model achieves a testing R2 of 0.9574 and outperforms the benchmark models. Across ten repeated random partitions using 70% of the samples for training and 30% for testing, the mean testing R2 was 0.9798 ± 0.0267 and the mean WAPE was 7.31% ± 2.80%, although performance declined under individual partitions. Under the specified literature-informed transition rules, the ecological protection scenario produces the lowest regional net carbon-emission level among the three scenarios by 2030. The framework provides quantitative support for low-carbon land-use planning and regional carbon-mitigation policymaking.

verified_metadata.title: An autoencoder-integrated extended Long Short-Term Memory model for long-sequence energy consumption prediction across climate zones
verified_metadata.abstract: Building carbon emissions account for 37% of the global total, with early design decisions locking in approximately 80% of lifecycle energy load. Accurate long-sequence energy prediction across climate zones is therefore critical. However, standard recurrent networks encounter gradient collapse in long sequences, and cross-climate methods lack effective mechanisms for extracting climate-invariant features. This study proposes an autoencoder-integrated extended Long Short-Term Memory (xLSTM_AE), which utilizes xLSTM to mitigate gradient issues and integrates Sinusoidal Position Encoding (SPE) to provide a deterministic temporal reference. An Autoencoder (AE) performs task-integrated nonlinear compression, where the bottleneck is jointly optimized with the prediction objective through end-to-end training. This represents the first systematic application of xLSTM_AE for cross-climate-zone long-sequence building energy prediction, with ablation experiments delineating each component's contribution. Evaluations across five climate zones indicate that xLSTM_AE achieves consistent performance (R2 = 0.97, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) = 3.95, Coefficient of Variation of Root Mean Square Error (CVRMSE) = 14.67%, Normalized Mean Bias Error (NMBE) = −2.88%), outperforming Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN), and Transformer. Ablation analysis shows the AE bottleneck recovers xLSTM's capability in complex climate zones (R2 from 0.63 to 0.73 to 0.94–0.97), while CVRMSE by load quantile reveals lower calibration error than Principal Component Analysis (PCA) + xLSTM in the high-load regime in three of five cities. Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) shows SPE mitigates positional drift in recursive memory, with structurally divergent representations. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) reveals adaptive heating and cooling mode switching across climate zones, offering retrofit prioritization guidance.

title: A preference-aware reinforcement learning framework for cost-effective and comfort-driven coordinated building energy management
abstract: Building energy consumption accounts for up to 40% of global energy use, contributing substantially to greenhouse gas emissions. Although demand-side management (DSM) and intelligent control systems have been extensively studied for residential buildings, smart buildings still face critical challenges due to their complex energy consumption profiles and lack of flexible, multi-energy management frameworks. This paper presents a novel multi-objective coordinated energy management system (EMS) that integrates a preference-aware reinforcement-learning framework to balance energy cost and indoor thermal comfort by dynamically coordinating multiple building systems, including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), energy storage systems (ESS), and hydrogen storage tanks (HST). To support day-ahead operation under uncertain renewable generation, the proposed EMS incorporates an AI-based extreme learning machine (ELM) model enhanced by a historical data correlation evaluation (HDCE) method, which improves the accuracy of short-term photovoltaic (PV) generation predictions. Simulation results show that the proposed framework can achieve approximately 13.4% energy cost reduction while maintaining nearly negligible user discomfort. In addition, the integrated PV forecasting module achieves a prediction error of 3.33%, which provides reliable renewable input for the coordinated EMS.

verified_metadata.title: An interpretable GRU–Transformer hybrid model for multi-target time-series prediction and thermal management of proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer systems
verified_metadata.abstract: Renewable-coupled proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) requires short-horizon prediction of coupled electrical and thermal states for proactive temperature regulation. This study develops an interpretable gated recurrent unit (GRU)–Transformer model to predict inlet temperature, outlet temperature, stack voltage, and stack temperature. A zero-dimensional multiphysics model, calibrated against a custom-built 3 kW PEMWE system, generates a 60 h dynamic dataset spanning prescribed ranges of current, heating power, and water flow for training and internal testing. Bidirectional GRU layers extract local transient features, whereas a Transformer encoder captures temporal dependencies within the input window. Target-specific feature weighting and temporal attention provide indicators of feature importance and temporal relevance, respectively. The model achieves a normalized multi-target mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.016 on the model-derived test set and 0.080 against measured dynamic responses. For normalized stack-temperature prediction, the model achieves an MAE of 0.0384 and an R2 of 0.9833, outperforming the evaluated GRU, long short-term memory (LSTM), and Transformer baselines. A separately trained voltage-prediction configuration achieves an MAE of 0.0119 V and an R2 of 0.9837 on a public PEMWE dataset spanning 961 h. The learned attributions recover the dominant thermal and electrochemical dependencies represented in the training data. In the simulated MPC scenario, incorporating attribution-weighted control penalties reduces the peak stack temperature by more than 4 °C relative to the default experimental control settings under a scaled wind-power profile.

verified_metadata.title: Spatiotemporal deep learning for wind turbine blade root load prediction via physics-guided GCN-GRU modelling
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate blade-root load estimation is important for structural monitoring of operating wind turbines, but direct load measurements are not routinely available. This study proposes a physics-guided spatiotemporal GCN-GRU framework for one-step-ahead blade-root load prediction using commonly available SCADA variables. Historical wind speed-power curves are used to construct a static graph representing quasi-static operational similarity among turbines, while graph convolution and gated recurrent units capture cross-turbine relational information and temporal dependencies, respectively. With the 1 Hz sampling rate used in this study, the prediction horizon is 1 s. The framework is evaluated using SCADA and measured blade-root load data from five 4 MW turbines in an industrial wind farm. Three turbines are used for model development, whereas two turbines are completely held out for within-farm, same-type cross-turbine evaluation. The proposed model achieves R2 values of 0.98-0.99 on the chronological test segments of the model-development turbines. For the held-out turbines, the average R2 values reach 0.815 for flapwise load prediction and 0.95 for edgewise load prediction. Ablation results further show that graph-based relational aggregation improves prediction performance over a GRU using only turbine-identity information, while the power-curve-based graph provides an interpretable, reproducible, and competitive relational prior. The results support the proposed framework as a near-real-time virtual-sensing approach for blade-root load monitoring.

title: A heat exchanger network retrofit method for non-continuous processes based on reinforcement learning
abstract: Non-continuous industrial processes exhibit irregular operating behaviour, characterised by frequent transitions and poorly defined operating regimes. To facilitate systematic analysis and optimisation, such processes are therefore commonly approximated as a set of representative discrete operating states. This study proposes an integrated reinforcement learning framework for heat exchanger network retrofitting under multiple operation states of non-continuous process. The reinforcement learning framework then optimises exchanger areas and network structure while respecting practical retrofit constraints. Unlike conventional machine learning approaches that rely on surrogate models or direct prediction of optimal designs, the proposed framework embeds learning within the optimisation process to adaptively explore retrofit decisions under non-continuous operation. Compared with traditional deterministic optimisation algorithms that require explicit enumeration of all structural constraints and may become infeasible for complex networks, the reinforcement learning approach employs trial-and-error learning on simplified models with fixed exchanger areas, enabling robust optimisation of the overall retrofit problem. Case study results show that the proposed approach reproduces optimisation trends comparable to those obtained using the full dataset and achieves a reduction in total annual cost, with exchanger reassignment and minor retrofit modifications alone delivering savings of approximately $300,000–500,000 and permitting additional heat exchangers increasing the benefit to over $1,000,000.

verified_metadata.title: Ultrahigh-heat-flux inclined jet-impingement layered-manifold liquid cooling synergized by machine learning for high energy efficiency
verified_metadata.abstract: Thermal management presents growing challenges for advanced electronics as the devices become more compact and powerful, which also leads to substantial energy consumption. To this end, we propose an inclined jet-impingement layered-manifold microchannel (IJMC) that delivers ultrahigh heat flux removal with high energy efficiency through a parametric multi-objective optimization framework. Analysis of variance reveals that all four key geometric parameters exert statistically significant impacts on the thermo-hydraulic performance. Specifically, the microchannel width is the most influential factor on thermal performance (57.05%), followed by the jet inlet and outlet widths, while the jet inlet and outlet widths dominate hydraulic performance (43.50% and 36.11%, respectively). Physical mechanism analysis demonstrates that introducing an inclined jet creates a pre-diffusion zone, effectively reducing the friction factor by 12.76%. Through machine learning-assisted multi-objective optimization, three distinct solutions tailored for balanced-priority, thermal-priority, and hydraulic-priority scenarios are derived, achieving COP increments of 1500, 589, and 1898 over the baseline, respectively. The thermal-priority solution is capable of dissipating a maximum heat flux of 1629 W/cm2. Importantly, at a heat flux of 1000 W/cm2 and a 60 °C maximum temperature rise, the thermal-priority solution can exhibit a thermal resistance as low as 0.075 K cm2/W and achieve a COP of up to 19349, enabled by an extremely low pumping power of only 0.47 mW.

verified_metadata.title: Toward deployment-ready Deep Learning for energy-efficient power plants: A critical survey of forecasting, control, and operational gaps
verified_metadata.abstract: Improving energy efficiency in power plants has become increasingly important due to increasing demand, fluctuating renewable generation, environmental pressures, and grid complexity. However, most Deep Learning studies still focus on accuracy and forecasting metrics and do not clearly demonstrate their relationship with measurable improvements in power plant operational indicators. This study, using a PRISMA-Guided Review Protocol, reviewed studies published between 2019 and May 2026 and selected 41 studies from 512 records for final analysis after Screening, Quality Assessment, and Standardized Data Extraction. The main innovation of the paper is to provide a Problem-Oriented, Deployment-Focused, and Power-Plant-Centered Taxonomy in four axes: Renewable Output Forecasting, Network Energy Coordination, Asset Condition Monitoring, and Cross-Domain Hybrid Efficiency. The results showed that Forecast Savings with 27% and Control Savings with 21% are the dominant research objectives. In comparison, Validation Debt with 25% and Context Lock-In with 23% are the most important barriers to transferring models to the real environment. Also, evidence related to the direct reduction of Fuel Consumption, Heat Rate, Energy Loss, and the increase in Equipment Availability is still limited. Therefore, progress in Model Accuracy has been faster than proving Operational Energy-Efficiency Impact. Future research should focus on Multi-Site Validation, Before–After KPI Assessment, Uncertainty Quantification, Explainable AI, MLOps, Techno-Economic Assessment, and Cybersecurity to develop Deployment-Ready and reliable models.

verified_metadata.title: A novel multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework based on scene clustering for dynamic scheduling of integrated energy systems
verified_metadata.abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy and the unpredictable nature of load demand pose challenges to traditional single-agent reinforcement learning. Therefore, a decentralized learning decentralized execution framework based on deep reinforcement learning is proposed, focusing on an electricity-hydrogen-heat system with electric energy as the central component. Firstly, due to the lack of exploration scenes within a single system, a novel multi-environment multi-agent interaction learning framework is proposed based on the K-means clustering algorithm. By training specialized agents for distinct scenes or environments, this framework partially mitigates the impact of uncertainties on agent decisions. Therefore, a prediction module combining a convolutional neural network and a gated recurrent unit is introduced to forecast environmental features for scheduling periods. This enables the clustering algorithm to match similar environments and corresponding agents based on these features. Subsequently, addressing the issue of goal preference in the multi-objective deep reinforcement learning, an economy-deep deterministic policy gradient model is proposed, which enhances the economic weight of decisions by integrating an economy-guided network into the deep deterministic policy gradient. Finally, the stability and superiority of the proposed method are validated, through comparisons with advanced deep reinforcement learning methods and traditional optimization approaches.

verified_metadata.title: Predictive modeling of a 100 MJ cascaded packed-bed thermal energy storage system with macro-encapsulated PCMs using XGBoost machine learning: Experimental data integration and performance analysis
verified_metadata.abstract: Addressing the imbalance in energy supply and demand, particularly for intermittent renewable sources, necessitates efficient thermal energy storage systems. Conventional modeling approaches struggle with the complex, nonlinear interactions within packed-bed thermal energy storage systems utilizing phase change materials. This study tackles this problem by developing advanced XGBoost machine learning models to predict the thermal dynamics of a 100 MJ cascaded packed-bed thermal energy storage system, uniquely trained and validated using comprehensive, real-world experimental data. The models' performance was rigorously assessed using six statistical metrics. The developed models demonstrated high predictive accuracy for the thermal energy storage system's performance. For both charging and discharging processes, predictions for Heat Transfer Fluid Outlet Temperature, Charging Energy, and Discharging Power showed excellent agreement with experimental data. Specifically, Coefficients of Determination were consistently high, between 0.99459 and 0.99979. Furthermore, all predictions consistently achieved an Index of Agreement of 0.99 and very low Margin of Deviation. These results affirm the XGBoost model's accuracy, precision, and reliability in predicting critical operational parameters. This work offers a significant step by validating machine learning performance with comprehensive, industrial-scale experimental data, providing a robust, computationally efficient proxy tool that can support the preliminary design optimization and control strategy development for future high-capacity thermal energy storage solutions.

verified_metadata.title: Thermodynamic analysis and deep learning-based prediction for curved-channel printed circuit heat exchangers with rectangular cross-section
verified_metadata.abstract: Printed Circuit Heat Exchangers (PCHEs) offer compact structure and high-efficiency heat transfer for advanced energy systems, with liquid working medium enabling low-pressure operation and high reliability. To elucidate the internal flow and heat transfer mechanisms in PCHEs and develop a reliable predictive model for thermodynamic performance, this study systematically evaluates and optimizes serrated and zigzag channels with varying geometric parameters (bending angle and curvature radius) through a comprehensive approach combining experiments, numerical simulation, and deep learning methods. The flow and heat transfer experiment of liquid lead-bismuth eutectic in a rectangular single channel provides a reliable reference for the validation of the numerical model. The thermodynamic performance of Serrated and Zigzag channels (SRPEs and ZZPEs) with bending angle (η) of 15°, 30°, 45° and curvature radius (R) of 0 mm, 5 mm, 10 mm is comprehensively evaluated using numerical methods. When the bending angle is fixed, extending the return length of the SRPEs to form a ZZPEs configuration effectively decreases the internal frictional losses. At a bending angle of 30°, introducing curvature enhances the PEC performance of both SRPEs and ZZPEs compared with the straight configuration; however, further increasing the curvature radius weakens the geometric disturbance, leading to a diminished enhancement at 10.0 mm relative to 5.0 mm. A similar tendency is observed for the SRPEs at 45°, whereas the ZZPEs exhibits the opposite response, with its average ΔPEC rising by approximately 1.2% as the curvature radius increases from 5.0 mm to 10.0 mm. With a nonzero curvature radius, the SRPEs exhibits superior PEC performance by maintaining a favorable balance between effective flow perturbation and reduced frictional loss. At a bending angle of 30°, the ΔPEC of SRPEs ranges from 17.9% to 21.7%, exceeding that of ZZPEs (15.3%–17.0%). At 45°, SRPEs achieves 30.6%–38.7%, compared with 24.8%–26.0% for ZZPEs. These findings highlight the advantage of integrating moderate curvature with serrated periodic disturbances in the structural design of CCPEs. With the support of data augmentation techniques, multiple neural networks are trained using multilayer perceptron (MLP) and convolutional neural network (CNN) methods. The results show that the CNN enhanced with cubic spline interpolation achieves the best predictive performance. Across TPUA, f *, Nu * and PEC, the model attains an average MSE of 0.14, RMSE of 0.29, MAE of 0.18, and R2 of 0.94. Curvature radius, inlet velocity and bending angle are the three most sensitive input parameters. Based on this dataset, a predictive model for SRPEs and ZZPEs thermodynamic parameters is developed, accounting for variations in bending angle and curvature radius.
