verified_metadata.title: Intelligent structural optimization of composite mini-channel heat exchangers using reinforcement learning algorithms
verified_metadata.abstract: Structural optimization of compact heat exchangers involves high-dimensional design spaces where thermal, hydraulic, and structural constraints are tightly coupled. This paper develops a reinforcement learning (RL) framework that couples three tabular algorithms (Sarsa, Q-learning, Dyna-Q) and one deep RL algorithm (Proximal Policy Optimization, PPO) with a physics-informed environment based on segmented LMTD methodology and ASME structural verification, simultaneously optimizing the cross-sectional channel geometries and spatial layouts of a composite mini-channel heat exchanger. The model-based Dyna-Q algorithm reduces the training episodes required for convergence by 75% relative to Sarsa and maintains the lowest post-convergence reward fluctuation. PPO achieves a peak ECO of 329.17 at γ = 0.5, exceeding the genetic algorithm (GA) baseline by 14.4%, but suffers a 32.5% degradation through catastrophic forgetting at γ = 0.9, confirming the robustness advantage of tabular methods in low-dimensional discrete optimization. The RL-optimized design attains a volumetric power density of 223 MW/m3, which is a 32.7% improvement over the GA baseline. This work provides a methodology for intelligent design of mini-channel heat exchangers with application potential in aerospace thermal management systems.

verified_metadata.title: Deep neural network observer for energy system monitoring with nuclear application
verified_metadata.abstract: To improve the safety, stability, flexibility and efficiency for the operation of complex energy mix comprising renewables, fossil fuels, nuclear power, storage, and load, it is urgently necessary to develop advanced monitoring methods for anomaly detection. A key challenge in system monitoring is the observation of unmeasurable internal states that indicates system's healthy condition, which is complicated by high nonlinearity and uncertainty. Given the powerful approximationability of neural networks (NNs), it is promising to integrate data-driven NNs with model-based state-observers for enhanced state-observation. To this end, a deep neural network observer (DNNO) is proposed by embedding a deep neural network (DNN) into a Luenberger observer within deterministic framework. The DNNO, essentially a recurrent neural network (RNN), provides globally bounded state-observation and features parameter-free, online learning, and globally bounded convergence. Driven exclusively by the output observation error, the online learning laws guarantee globally asymptotic convergence of the state-observation error to a bounded set, independent of any prior knowledge of system's physical parameters. The effectiveness of the DNNO is validated through its application to a modular high temperature gas-cooled reactor (mHTGR), a representative small modular reactor (SMR). Simulation results in multiple scenarios verify the theoretical findings, confirm the satisfactory performance of the DNNO, and highlight the advantages of its deep structure.

verified_metadata.title: AI-enabled real-time hybrid model testing of floating wind turbines: An asynchronous aerodynamic load prediction framework validated on a 16 MW TLP turbine
verified_metadata.abstract: High-fidelity wave-basin testing of floating wind turbines requires real-time reproduction of motion-dependent aerodynamic loads, but existing real-time hybrid model testing (RTHM) systems remain constrained by online aerodynamic-solver blocking and limited multi-axis load actuation. This study proposes an AI-enabled RTHM framework in which an OpenFAST-informed aerodynamic surrogate is embedded as an active numerical substructure and integrated with asynchronous command execution and multi-channel physical loading. A CNN-BiLSTM-Attention surrogate is trained using fully coupled OpenFAST data to predict one-step-ahead rotor thrust Fx and aerodynamic moments Mx, My, and Mz from turbulent wind input, turbine operating states, and real-time six-degree-of-freedom platform-motion feedback. A prediction–cache–release strategy decouples command release from AI inference, load scaling, and command generation, with the measured cache-release latency below 1 ms. The predicted loads are scaled and physically reproduced by a six-rotor aerodynamic loading device in a 1:85 wave-basin test of a 16 MW tension-leg platform floating wind turbine. The AI-predicted loads agree closely with OpenFAST references, with the minimum Q-Q coefficient of determination reaching 0.997. The corresponding measured thrust and moment channels achieve minimum Q-Q coefficients of 0.988 and 0.927, respectively. At the system-response level, the main statistical errors of platform surge, heave, pitch, and upwind center tendon tension remain below 9.6%. The proposed framework establishes a motion-feedback-in-the-loop AI numerical-substructure approach for real-time hybrid testing of the investigated 16 MW TLP floating wind turbine.

verified_metadata.title: Multi-objective parameter performance optimization of a novel ultrasonic oscillation falling film generator based on machine learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Ammonia-water absorption refrigeration and heat pump systems are restricted by low thermodynamic coefficient of performance, meanwhile the generator component suffers from unsatisfactory heat and mass transfer efficiency. To solve this bottleneck, this work innovatively introduces ultrasonic oscillation technology into a newly developed falling film generator. A one-dimensional theoretical model is established to characterize ammonia-water falling film desorption under ultrasonic excitation, covering five key operating variables: ultrasonic power, inlet solution concentration and flow rate, hot water inlet temperature, and generation pressure. Multi-parameter coupling impacts on average mass transfer rate and degassing range (Δω) are systematically analyzed. A histogram-based gradient boosting regressor is constructed as an efficient surrogate of the physics-based model for high-dimensional screening and optimization. Accumulated local effects analysis quantifies each parameter's marginal contribution to Δω variation, and a differential evolution algorithm performs multi-variable performance optimization. The results demonstrate that inlet flow rate dominates Δω variation with a 61.66% contribution. The predicted maximum Δω has a relative error of only 3.2% against numerical simulation, and the optimized Δω is 33.3% higher than the conventional generator without ultrasonic reinforcement. Although this study verifies the remarkable performance improvement brought by ultrasonic intensification, it should be noted that these quantitative values are theoretical predictions derived from the first-order acoustic streaming intensification model, without considering the boiling nucleation effect induced by cavitation. Since cavitation phase change can produce additional enhancement effects, the actual intensification performance will be higher. Further experimental verification is required before all these results can be applied to practical engineering scenarios.

verified_metadata.title: Physics-consistent reinforcement learning for temperature control in delayed thermal energy systems
verified_metadata.abstract: Delayed flow heat transfer control is challenging because outlet temperature is governed by fluid transport delay, solid heat storage, and hidden wall–fluid thermal states. Under limited measurements, the control task becomes partially observable, making reinforcement learning based only on instantaneous observations prone to delayed actions, excessive overshoot, and closed-loop oscillations. To address this problem, this study proposes a physics-consistent state-augmented reinforcement learning framework for overshoot-suppressed temperature control in delayed thermal energy systems. First, the delayed input–output relationship of the flow-heating process is analyzed to clarify why instantaneous observations are insufficient for policy learning. A fast reduced-order physical model is then developed to predict steady-state thermal–hydraulic features, including outlet temperature, pressure, velocity, and characteristic settling time. To reduce model bias caused by dimensional reduction and uncertain heat-transfer conditions, an ensemble Kalman filter is introduced to update the equivalent heat-source correction parameter online. The corrected physical predictions are incorporated into the policy state, and a PPO-based policy is trained for continuous control using this augmented state representation. At the 80 °C benchmark, the proposed method achieved a maximum temperature overshoot of 0.291±0.201°C across five independently trained seeds, representing an 86.4% reduction relative to Standard PPO. Across the 70, 75, and 80 °C targets, the mean maximum overshoot remained between 0.148 and 0.291 °C, demonstrating repeatable overshoot-suppressed regulation at the tested setpoints. These results show that online-corrected physical state augmentation improves reinforcement-learning state representation and provides a control reference for delayed thermal energy systems.

title: Energy flow analysis and control strategy optimization for a hybrid wheeled all-terrain vehicle under complex driving scenarios
abstract: The energy management of Hybrid Wheeled All-Terrain Vehicles (HWATVs) operating in unstructured environments faces significant challenges due to stochastic power demands and the lack of representative standard driving cycles. Existing strategies often fail to balance dynamic performance and fuel economy under such extreme conditions. This study proposes a systematic optimization framework integrating energy flow analysis with adaptive control. First, a high-fidelity powertrain test bench is established using the Design of Experiments (DOE) method to precisely quantify the multi-physical energy loss characteristics of the engine, motors, and battery. Subsequently, a driving cycle reconstruction method based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA), K-means clustering, and Markov chains is developed to extract four typical off-road patterns and synthesize stochastic validation cycles from real-vehicle data. On this basis, the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) is employed to optimize mode-switching thresholds and battery State of Charge (SOC) maintenance ranges for each identified typical driving cycle. Incorporating these optimized parameter sets, an adaptive Energy Management Strategy (EMS) is established featuring online driving condition recognition to dynamically apply the optimal control logic. Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) validation under typical driving conditions and comprehensive driving cycles demonstrates that, compared to traditional rule-based strategies, the proposed approach exhibits superior robustness in stochastic environments. Specifically, it reduces fuel consumption by 0.99%–7.01% and decreases battery charge/discharge cycling frequency by 2.14%–15.30%. This research elucidates the energy-saving mechanism of coupling high-efficiency engine operation with minimized transmission path losses, providing a theoretical foundation for the efficient control of special vehicles in complex terrains.

verified_metadata.title: Energy flow analysis and control strategy optimization for a hybrid wheeled all-terrain vehicle under complex driving scenarios
verified_metadata.abstract: The energy management of Hybrid Wheeled All-Terrain Vehicles (HWATVs) operating in unstructured environments faces significant challenges due to stochastic power demands, the scarcity of real off-road data, and the absence of representative standard driving cycles. To address these intertwined constraints, this study establishes a physics-informed, data-driven optimization framework that bridges full-spectrum energy flow testing with adaptive control. Specifically, a high-fidelity powertrain test bench is first established using the Design of Experiments (DOE) method to precisely quantify the multi-physical energy loss characteristics of the engine, motors, and battery. Using the measured loss maps as physical anchors, four typical off-road patterns are then directly extracted from 23,559 s of real-vehicle data via Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and K-means clustering, and stochastic validation cycles are synthesized via Markov chains. For each identified pattern, the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) is adopted to calibrate the mode-switching thresholds and SOC bounds. These calibrated parameter sets are subsequently deployed through an online driving condition recognition mechanism that enables real-time adaptive switching. Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) validation under both typical and stochastic driving cycles demonstrates that, compared with traditional rule-based strategies, the proposed approach exhibits improved robustness in stochastic environments, reducing fuel consumption by 0.99%–7.01% and decreasing battery charge/discharge cycling frequency by 2.14%–15.30%. The energy-flow post-analysis reveals that the savings originate from the coupling of high-efficiency engine operation with minimized series-path conversion losses, providing a practical foundation for special-purpose off-road vehicles in GPS-denied environments.

verified_metadata.title: Comprehensive solvent evaluation for post-combustion carbon capture in cement decarbonization: 4E analysis, machine learning, life cycle assessment and sensitivity analysis
verified_metadata.abstract: Global warming and climate change have intensified the need for effective carbon mitigation strategies to achieve net-zero emissions. The cement industry is among the largest industrial sources of CO2 emissions, making post-combustion carbon capture (PCC) a key technology for decarbonization. However, the performance of PCC systems strongly depends on solvent selection.This study provides a comprehensive multi-criteria evaluation of commercial amine-based solvents, including monoethanolamine (MEA), diethanolamine (DEA), diglycolamine (DGA), methyldiethanolamine (MDEA), piperazine (PZ), triethanolamine (TEA), and other blends. Steady-state simulations were combined with an integrated 4E framework (energy, exergy, exergoeconomic, and exergoenvironmental analyses), together with life cycle assessment and sensitivity analysis, to evaluate thermodynamic, economic, and environmental performance. In addition, machine learning models, including K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Tree, Random Forest, Artificial Neural Network, Support Vector Classifier (SVC), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), were optimized using GridSearchCV for predictive solvent classification.The results show that no single solvent is optimal across all evaluation criteria. DGA performs best in terms of energy consumption, exergy destruction, exergoeconomic performance, economic cost, life cycle assessment, and sensitivity analysis. MDEA achieves the highest exergy efficiency (60.5%), while Disopropanolamine exhibits the lowest environmental impact. From a data-driven perspective, the Random Forest model achieved the highest predictive performance, with an Area Under Curve (AUC) of 0.94, and identified TEA as the optimal solvent. Overall, the proposed integrated thermodynamic and machine learning framework provides a robust decision-support tool for sustainable solvent selection and supports the broader decarbonization of the cement industry.

verified_metadata.title: Intelligent setpoint decision-making for PWR automatic startup based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning
verified_metadata.abstract: The automatic startup of a pressurized water reactor exhibits strong coupling, wide-range transients, and stringent safety constraints. Existing setpoint decision-making methods typically treat each control loop independently and rely on fixed offline trajectories, leaving inter-loop couplings unaddressed and lacking adaptability to real-time disturbances. Consequently, even with well-tuned bottom-layer controllers, the startup performance remains constrained by oscillations and potential safety violations. To overcome these limitations without modifying existing safety-certified controllers, this study proposes a non-intrusive deep reinforcement learning strategy for intelligent setpoint decision-making. A two-stage “offline training – online decision-making” architecture integrates an intelligent module above the existing automatic startup system. Three independent deep deterministic policy gradient agents are developed for pressure, temperature, and water level control, each with a low-dimensional state space and incremental actions. An indirect multi-agent coordination mechanism based on shared environmental feedback enables emergent inter-agent collaboration. Simulation verification on a high-fidelity Hua-long pressurized water reactor simulation platform demonstrates robust single-agent generalization, active disturbance rejection, and effective multi-agent coordination under load transients. Compared with conventional fixed setpoints, the multi-agent intelligent setpoints reduce the integral of time-weighted squared error by 95.0%, 27.3%, and 78.5% for pressure, temperature, and water level, respectively. These results confirm that the proposed strategy achieves adaptive, disturbance-rejecting, and coordinated automatic startup.

verified_metadata.title: Predicting energy efficiency and carbon footprint in livestock farms using artificial neural networks: A case study in Turkey
verified_metadata.abstract: On dairy farms, the increasing number of operational processes over time, along with rising energy costs and environmental issues, has made managing energy and its carbon footprint (CF) a necessity for farm sustainability. Thus, energy efficiency and energy-related CF were calculated for 93 dairy cattle farms in Türkiye, with capacities ranging from 1 to 225 heads, using conventional production methods and semi-open free-stall systems. Within the scope of the study, average energy consumption and output amounts, as well as energy efficiencies were determined using six parameters (feed, electricity, labor, machinery, young dairy cattle, fuel) and three output parameters (manure, milk, meat) obtained from field studies conducted on 93 farms. Additionally, average CF calculations based on energy sources have been carried out using the directly consumed energy inputs (electricity, fuel) and the inputs that drive energy consumption in production processes (feed and manure) for all farms. Finally, the energy efficiency and CF amounts for these farms were predicted using an artificial neural network (ANN). The average energy consumption of all farms was determined to be 78737.94 MJ/LSU. The average energy output from the farms was 13082.23 MJ/LSU. Accordingly, only 17% of the energy consumed in farms can be met. The average CF per liter of milk was 0.558 kg CO2-eq. On farms, the highest energy-related CO2-eq was fuel, while the lowest was manure. Using ANN, energy efficiency and energy-related CF have been successfully predicted, with R2 scores over 90% and low error rates. This will inform farms by providing a practical decision-support tool.

verified_metadata.title: Hot helium temperature optimization in modular high-temperature gas-cooled reactors using supervisory LSTM-MPC
verified_metadata.abstract: Flexible operation of modular high-temperature gas-cooled reactors (MHTGRs) requires effective regulation of the delayed and oscillatory hot helium temperature during load changes. This study develops a supervisory long short-term memory-based model predictive control (LSTM-MPC) strategy that reshapes the thermal power setpoint online while retaining the existing coordinated control system. A unified closed-loop LSTM surrogate was trained using data collected within 50%–75% rated full power (RFP) and applied without retraining to bidirectional transients extending to 100% RFP. The model predicts the hot helium temperature increment and is embedded in a differentiable receding-horizon optimizer to generate bounded setpoint compensation. Hard constraints, control penalties, and baseline fallback limit the supervisory authority and preserve plant-side stabilization and actuator coordination. The strategy was implemented through Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture (OPC UA) on an MHTGR engineering simulator and evaluated under two load-reduction scenarios and one power-increase scenario, with baseline coordinated control and dynamic matrix control used as benchmarks. LSTM-MPC improved all evaluated temperature-response indices and representative extrema, with integral of squared error reductions of 40.9%–64.3% relative to the baseline. These results demonstrate that data-driven predictive setpoint reshaping can improve MHTGR load-changing performance through a bounded and non-intrusive supervisory implementation.

verified_metadata.title: Strategic day-ahead bidding for hydropower producers under heterogeneous competitor behavior: A clustering-based boundedly rational behavioral modeling and bilevel optimization framework
verified_metadata.abstract: In day-ahead electricity markets, hydropower producers face the challenge of optimizing bids while anticipating the reactions of heterogeneous, boundedly rational competitors. This study proposes an integrated framework combining data-driven competitor typology identification, behavioral modeling, and bilevel optimization. First, a multi-view spectral clustering approach fuses statistical features and dynamic time warping-based temporal patterns to identify representative competitor types from historical data. Second, an improved Barberis–Shleifer–Vishny (BSV) model is developed, incorporating a psychological confidence index, a diurnal seasonal anchor, and a shock overreaction mechanism to predict each competitor's boundedly rational bidding adjustments in a self-feeding multi-step manner. Third, these behavioral predictions are embedded into the lower-level market clearing of a bilevel model, where the upper level maximizes the hydropower producer's profit under hydraulic constraints. Validated with real data from the Hubei electricity market, the improved BSV model achieves R2 above 0.94 and MAPE below 5% over a 24-h horizon. The resulting bidding strategy yields profit improvements of 7.5%–18.1% over traditional BSV, game-theoretic, and greedy benchmarks, with independent validation discrepancies below 1%. The framework demonstrates that explicitly modeling heterogeneous bounded rationality significantly enhances hydropower bidding performance.

title: A time-series clustering framework for sector-coupled capacity expansion models
abstract: The growing importance of hydrogen and sector coupling increases the complexity of Capacity Expansion Models (CEMs) and underscores the need for time-series aggregation methods that balance accuracy with computational efficiency. While previous studies have focused on developing methods for small-scale power sector CEM, this work compares three traditional clustering approaches with a novel DTW-based method (DTW-VD) in terms of statistical accuracy and applies them in a single-node and a multi-node sector-coupled CEMs with seasonal storage. DTW-VD achieves the highest statistical accuracy and best approximates the full-resolution objective function in the single-node case for up to 125 representative days. In the multi-node model, where the true solution is not available, investment decisions based on DTW-VD achieve the best operational performance in 2050. Overall, using two different models and three different weather years, the findings indicate that the performance of time-series aggregation methods depends on the characteristics of the optimization problem, the underlying dataset, and the chosen temporal resolution. The proposed method performs particularly well in complex systems and when a low number of representative periods is used.

verified_metadata.title: A time-series clustering framework for sector-coupled capacity expansion models
verified_metadata.abstract: The increasing complexity of capacity expansion models underscores the need for time-series aggregation methods that balance accuracy with computational efficiency. While previous studies have focused on developing methods for small-scale power sector capacity expansion models, this work compares three traditional clustering approaches with a novel dynamic time warping based methodology using a single-node and a multi-node sector-coupled capacity expansion model with seasonal storage. All methods are evaluated in terms of statistical accuracy, objective function approximation, and operational performance across three weather years. The proposed methodology achieves the highest statistical accuracy and best approximates the full-hourly objective function in the single-node case. In the multi-node model, where a full-hourly benchmark is computationally infeasible, proxy-based operational metrics indicate that the proposed methodology most closely approximates the full-hourly solution among the evaluated methods. Overall, the findings suggest that the proposed method performs particularly well in complex systems and when a low number of representative periods is used.

verified_metadata.title: A scalable BIM-machine learning-evolutionary framework for multi-objective building performance optimization
verified_metadata.abstract: In sustainable design, optimizing building performance to simultaneously achieve energy efficiency, low environmental impact, and indoor comfort remains a significant challenge, mainly due to the complexity of the calculations involved in simulating and optimizing numerous design parameters. Although traditional methods mainly rely on physical simulations or simplified models, they often have limitations in terms of computational efficiency, the ability to optimize high-dimensional objectives, and the predictive accuracy in resolving the complex nonlinear relationships between building parameters and performance indicators. This study proposes a comprehensive framework that systematically integrates three key technologies: Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for hyperparameter adjustment, Machine Learning (ML) for performance prediction, and Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm (NSGA)-III for multi-objective optimization. First, orthogonal experiments are conducted using the Building Information Model (BIM) with DesignBuilder (DB), and a comprehensive sample dataset is generated. Secondly, the particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to optimize the hyperparameters of four machine learning models (including Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and Support Vector Machine (SVM)), thereby establishing an accurate prediction model. Finally, the optimal model obtained is used to construct the fitness function of NSGA-III and to obtain the Pareto optimal solution. A study was conducted using an office building in Wuhan. The results show that: (1) Compared with PSO-GBDT, PSO-ANN, and PSO-SVM, the PSO-RF model has prediction R2 values of 0.999, 0.998, and 0.957 respectively for energy consumption, carbon emissions, and thermal comfort. (2) The optimization results are remarkable, with life-cycle energy consumption and carbon emissions reduced by 23.49% and 5.58%, and thermal comfort (PMV) approaching a neutral state. (3) Parameter importance analysis indicates that the cooling setpoint temperature and building airtightness are the primary factors affecting the design. Our study provides a robust and intelligent framework that enables designers and policymakers to make informed decisions toward the development of high-performance sustainable buildings.

verified_metadata.title: Real-time adaptive energy management with acceleration-consistency-regularized trend-enhanced transformer-based speed prediction for hybrid electric amphibious vehicles
verified_metadata.abstract: Hybrid electric amphibious vehicles (HEAVs) are characterized by highly dynamic speed profiles and speed-dependent transient load variations, posing challenges to fuel economy, SOC regulation, and powertrain stability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a real-time adaptive energy management framework integrating an acceleration-consistency-regularized Trend-Enhanced Transformer (TE-Transformer) with a prediction-guided load-splitting adaptive equivalent consumption minimization strategy (PLS-AECMS). Firstly, a stop-constrained method is developed to segment a 10314s real-world waterborne dataset into low-speed maneuver, mid-speed fluctuation, and high-speed cruise profiles. To capture the evolution characteristics of waterborne speed, the TE-Transformer jointly learns point-wise temporal dependencies and segment-level trends, achieving average MAE, RMSE, and R2 values of 0.1107, 0.1993, and 0.9951 on an EAORA07 controller. Based on the predicted speed sequence, PLS-AECMS assigns baseline load to the engine and transient demand to the battery. Across nine scenarios, it maintains final SOC within 59.19%-59.90%, reduces total SOC-corrected fuel consumption by 1.27% and 2.93% compared to prediction-based MPC (P-MPC) and AECMS, and decreases the average maximum engine power change rate by 88.26% and 90.18%, respectively. Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) tests further verify the real-time performance and deployment potential of PLS-AECMS, with an average solving time of 15.3 ms and a maximum solving time below 20 ms. Overall, this study provides an effective solution for real-time energy management of HEAVs, and offers valuable insights for hybrid marine propulsion systems.

title: Cross-building reinforcement learning for zero-shot HVAC control in residential buildings
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise for residential Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) control, but conventional approaches require target-building data, model construction, and policy training, limiting scalability in newly constructed houses. Although transfer learning reduces this burden, scalable zero-shot RL control that avoids target-building data collection, model calibration, and policy retraining remains insufficiently investigated. This study therefore has two objectives: (1) to develop a Cross-building Trust Region Policy Optimization (TRPO) framework for zero-shot residential air-conditioning control, and (2) to determine whether it can achieve performance comparable to room-specific RL in unseen rooms without retraining. EnergyPlus generated residential rooms with diverse thermal characteristics, and thermal-performance indicators were incorporated into the state space to condition the policy on room-specific responses. A single TRPO policy was trained across these tasks and tested in resistance-capacitance (RC) simulation environments constructed from data for two unseen target rooms; these data were used only for evaluation. For the small-design-load room, Cross-building TRPO reduced energy consumption to 64.57% of the fixed-setpoint baseline while maintaining a 100% comfort ratio. For the large-design-load room, where the baseline operated at a high coefficient of performance (COP), both room-specific TRPO and Cross-building TRPO yielded limited additional improvement. Overall, Cross-building TRPO achieved performance close to room-specific TRPO without target-room retraining, demonstrating the feasibility of building-performance-conditioned zero-shot HVAC control. In practice, pre-trained HVAC controllers could be deployed in newly constructed residential buildings using available thermal-performance information, reducing on-site data collection and policy retraining requirements and supporting large-scale deployment.

verified_metadata.title: Balancing energy-comfort-carbon trade-offs for traditional Sanheyuan building retrofit: A decision support framework integrating two-stage SHAP analysis and pareto clustering
verified_metadata.abstract: Traditional Sanheyuan buildings in the Hot Summer and Cold Winter (HSCW) zone face a critical trilemma under heritage conservation constraints: balancing operational energy use intensity (EUI), thermal comfort hours (TCH), and embodied carbon (CE). This study develops a decision support framework integrating two-stage SHAP analysis and Pareto clustering to address this challenge. A validated EnergyPlus model generated 2000 design scenarios. Among seven machine learning models, XGBoost achieved the highest predictive accuracy and was selected as the surrogate model. Global SHAP analysis reveals that active measures dominate EUI (outdoor air flow rate contributes 71.0%), while passive measures dominate CE (wall insulation material and its thickness collectively contribute 62.5%), with TCH exhibiting synergistic active-passive control. The NSGA-III algorithm generated 129 Pareto optimal solutions. Entropy-weighted TOPSIS selected a comprehensive optimal solution from the Pareto front. Local SHAP analysis on this solution identifies cooling setpoint and outdoor air flow rate as key TCH drivers, and material selection as the primary CE reducer. Finally, K-means clustering condensed the 129 Pareto solutions into four retrofit archetypes: energy-prioritized, comfort-oriented, low-carbon balanced, and robust-balanced. Key contributions include the two-stage SHAP interpretation bridging global sensitivity and local attribution, an integrated NSGA-III–TOPSIS–K-means decision pipeline producing actionable archetypes, and quantification of the carbon penalty and energy-comfort trade-off under conservation constraints.

verified_metadata.title: Thermodynamically consistent feature representation for machine learning-based HHV prediction of municipal solid waste
verified_metadata.abstract: Higher heating value (HHV) is a key property for evaluating municipal solid waste (MSW) feedstocks in waste-to-energy systems. However, the as-received HHV of MSW reflects the combined effects of combustible composition and physical dilution associated with moisture and ash. This coupling requires a direct machine-learning model to simultaneously fit combustible-composition effects and moisture/ash dilution effects within a single regression mapping, which increases the complexity of the learning task and may reduce the stability and physical interpretability of the fitted relationship. To address this issue, this study developed a thermodynamically consistent feature-representation framework that separates dry ash-free combustible-fraction HHV prediction from physical dilution reconstruction. Three strategies were evaluated under the same modeling and validation protocol: a direct model using as-received elemental composition, moisture, and ash to predict as-received HHV; a partially converted model using dry ash-free elemental composition together with moisture and ash to predict as-received HHV; and a fully converted model using dry ash-free elemental composition to predict dry ash-free HHV, which was then converted back to the as-received basis by multiplying it by the combustible mass fraction calculated from moisture and ash contents. The results show that converting elemental features to a dry ash-free basis alone is insufficient when as-received HHV remains the direct learning target. Among the three evaluated frameworks, the fully basis-converted framework achieved the lowest overall prediction errors for as-received HHV and provided a more stable residual structure for directly learned dry ash-free HHV. Its R2, RMSE, and MAE were 0.9845, 1.202 MJ/kg, and 0.713 MJ/kg for HHVar, respectively, whereas the corresponding values for directly predicted HHVdaf were 0.8970, 2.182 MJ/kg, and 1.375 MJ/kg. It also showed more stable sample-wise error behavior across different moisture and ash dilution levels. However, the improved as-received metrics partly reflect the error-scaling effect introduced by deterministic reconstruction. This framework also provides a clearer physical allocation of model components, in which dry ash-free elemental features are used to represent the combustible fraction, while moisture and ash are introduced through mass-based reconstruction. These findings suggest that thermodynamically consistent basis conversion is an effective representation strategy for improving prediction accuracy, residual stability, and interpretability in the present small and highly heterogeneous MSW dataset.

verified_metadata.title: Eco-engineered multi-product sustainable energy system by utilization waste-heat recovery from flue-gas and CO2 capture: Integrated 6E analysis and convolutional neural network assisted multi-objective moth-flame optimization
verified_metadata.abstract: This study proposes an eco-engineered multi-product system that utilizes post-combustion flue-gas streams from cement kilns as a primary thermal resource to improve energy recovery and reduce environmental impacts. To maximize the utilization of high- and medium-grade thermal energy, a small fraction of the exhaust gas is directed to Rankine-based modules, while the majority is supplied to a Kalina cycle unit. The system integrates a two-stage organic Rankine cycle with a steam Rankine cycle to simultaneously generate electricity and hot water from different temperature levels. To ensure complete cascade utilization of the remaining low-temperature thermal energy, the exhaust stream leaving the Kalina unit is further recovered in a desalination subsystem. An integrated CO2 capture unit is also incorporated to recover carbon dioxide from cement-kiln flue gas and support emission reduction objectives. The proposed configuration is evaluated using energy, exergy, and emergy analyses, complemented by sensitivity and parametric investigations. Results indicate an exergy efficiency of 34.02%, an exergy-based product cost of 6.76 $/GJ, and a sustainability index of 1.516. Emergo-economic assessment reveals the lowest factors for the Kalina and desalination units because of their significant exergy-destruction contributions. Neural-network-assisted moth-flame optimization identifies an optimal design with 45.228% exergy efficiency, 0.036 $/kWh levelized cost, a sustainability index of 1.824, and a net present value of 27.088 M$.

verified_metadata.title: Integrated neural-network modeling and improved discrete-time RL-EADRC control for flexible operation of ultra-supercritical units
verified_metadata.abstract: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy and its inherent intermittency, ultra-supercritical (USC) units are required to operate flexibly across different load levels to accommodate fluctuating grid demands. However, accurately modeling the USC unit under such load-varying conditions remains challenging due to large inertia, strong nonlinearity, and multivariable coupling. Meanwhile, in practical implementations, the performance of error-based active disturbance rejection control (EADRC) is influenced by discrete-time realization and parameter tuning. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a flexible operation scheme integrating neural-network modeling and discrete-time reinforcement learning (RL)-EADRC control. Firstly, an improved Titans model featuring a long-term memory module (LMM) and trend-aware attention mechanism is designed to characterize the dynamic behavior of USC units. Secondly, a control strategy based on discrete-time EADRC with a current-form observer is developed to reduce observation lag and improve control performance. Furthermore, an RL agent is introduced to adaptively tune key EADRC parameters online under varying operating conditions. Experimental results based on field operating data from a 1000 MW USC unit show that the improved Titans model achieves a modeling accuracy of 99.3%. Based on this high-accuracy model, tracking and disturbance rejection tests are conducted to evaluate the proposed RL-EADRC. The results show that it achieves stable and accurate peak-shaving performance over the 57%-87% rated load range and maintains robustness at two representative operating points. These results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method for flexible operation of USC units.

verified_metadata.title: Enhancing Energy Management in Microgrids with Renewable Sources and Electric Vehicles using Hybrid Red Panda Optimization and Multi-fidelity Bayesian Neural Networks
verified_metadata.abstract: The increasing integration of Renewable Energy Sources (RESs) and Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEVs) into microgrids (MGs) presents significant energy management (EM) challenges due to renewable generation intermittency, fluctuating load demand, and uncertain vehicle charging requirements. Efficient MG operation requires intelligent prediction and optimization to maintain energy balance while minimizing Total Operating Costs (TOC). To address these challenges, this study proposes a hybrid Red Panda Optimization and Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Neural Network (RPO-MFBNN) framework for intelligent EM in RES- and PHEV-integrated MGs. The Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Neural Network (MFBNN) utilizes multi-fidelity information to accurately predict future renewable generation, load demand, and PHEV charging requirements, while the Red Panda Optimization (RPO) algorithm optimally allocates energy among renewable sources, battery energy storage systems, PHEVs, local loads, and the utility grid to minimize TOC and maintain reliable operation. The framework is implemented in MATLAB and evaluated under two MG operating scenarios with different storage and PHEV conditions. Comparative analysis with ANN-PSO, COA-CANN, LSO-DADRCNN, ANN-FLC, and BESO demonstrates the superiority of the proposed approach. The RPO-MFBNN framework achieves TOC values of 333.28 €ct and 321.63 €ct, compared with 385.45 €ct and 385.44 €ct for controlled operation and 671.42 €ct and 660.71 €ct for uncontrolled operation, demonstrating accurate prediction, optimized energy allocation, reduced operating costs, improved energy utilization, and efficient EM for renewable- and PHEV-integrated MGs under varying operating conditions.

verified_metadata.title: Comparison and optimization of advanced machine learning methods for performance prediction of the hydrogen-enriched Wankel engine under multiple engineering constraints
verified_metadata.abstract: This study proposes a data-driven multi-objective optimization framework for a hydrogen-blended gasoline Wankel rotary engine. All experiments and GT-Power simulations were conducted at 4200 r/min and a manifold absolute pressure of 35 kPa. A fused dataset of 54 experimental samples and 250 simulated samples was established at three hydrogen volume fractions across the investigated ranges of excess-air coefficient and spark timing. A KDE-weighted kernel stacking model combining random forest, support vector regression, and Gaussian process regression with a ridge meta-learner was used to predict effective thermal efficiency, indicated mean effective pressure, source-specific NOx responses, peak in-cylinder pressure, and peak temperature. The model delivered the best overall predictive performance among the evaluated approaches. Feature-attribution analysis showed that the excess-air coefficient dominated peak temperature, while spark timing mainly affected effective thermal efficiency through combustion phasing; hydrogen volume fraction and excess-air coefficient jointly influenced simulated NOx. The frozen surrogate was then coupled with constrained hypervolume-improvement-based multi-objective Bayesian optimization to identify Pareto trade-offs. The selected compromise solution balanced efficiency, simulated NOx, and thermal load while satisfying the adopted screening criteria. GT-Power recalculation of five representative solutions supported the internal consistency of the surrogate predictions and screening results, but did not constitute independent validation. The proposed framework provides an efficient calibration strategy for the investigated condition, although its applicability to other speed-load conditions requires further investigation.

verified_metadata.title: Data-driven sensitivity analysis and dominant factor identification for coal and gas outburst: An explainable machine learning approach fusing multi-source monitoring data
verified_metadata.abstract: The precise prevention and control of coal and gas outburst is crucial for achieving safe and efficient mine production. Addressing the limitations of existing big data analysis methods, which often focus on constructing high-precision black-box early warning models while lacking interpretability for decision-making, and have not yet systematically leveraged multi-source data for dynamic sensitivity analysis, this study proposes and develops a research methodology that integrates multi-source monitoring data, multi-level feature engineering, and explainable machine learning. Firstly, a feature engineering framework incorporating static geological data, dynamic gas and acoustic emission time-series data, and mining disturbance data is constructed, achieving a multi-dimensional characterization of the outburst triggering process. Secondly, by integrating the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) explainable framework with the XGBoost model, a three-dimensional sensitivity quantification analysis method is established, encompassing global importance, local triggering mechanisms, and feature interaction effects. This enables a multi-level quantitative analysis of the nonlinear coupled contributions of multiple factors. Through a typical mine case study, the abrupt variation patterns of key sensitivity indicators immediately prior to an outburst are dynamically captured, and highly sensitive data features are mapped to the physical process of stress concentration-fracture evolution-gas emission, thereby constructing a linkage from data correlations to disaster-causing mechanisms. The research outcomes provide a solution with both theoretical value and engineering applicability, facilitating a transition in outburst risk warning from static single-indicator thresholds to dynamic multi-indicator collaborative early warning.

verified_metadata.title: Energy Markets, AI-Driven Demand, Electric Vehicles, and Smart Grids under Geopolitical Risk: Implications for the Energy Transition
verified_metadata.abstract:
This study examines the evolving interactions among energy and carbon systems, green finance, and technology-driven assets in the context of geopolitical risk and energy transition. The analysis incorporates key energy-related variables, including crude oil (WTI), carbon prices (ETS), green finance, smart-grid infrastructure, artificial intelligence, semiconductors, electric vehicles (EVs), copper, and geopolitical risk, capturing recent structural shifts associated with the post-2022 AI expansion and the 2026 Middle East geopolitical escalation. Using daily data from 18 September 2018 to 19 March 2026, the study applies TVP-VAR, generalized variance decomposition of forecast errors, quantile connectedness, and network analysis. Spillovers are identified through order-invariant generalized variance shares that measure the direction and magnitude of shock transmission across markets.

The findings reveal that the global energy system has become increasingly interconnected, particularly during periods of geopolitical tension and energy market disruptions, including those in 2026. Oil markets remain the central node in the estimated spillover network, linking conventional energy dynamics to carbon pricing, green finance, and technology-driven demand. The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure is a major market-based indicator associated with expected energy demand, reinforcing the link between technology markets and electricity consumption. At the same time, the growing adoption of electric vehicles is associated with changes in energy-demand patterns by reducing dependence on fossil fuels while increasing electricity consumption and pressure on grid systems. Smart grids play a key role in this transition by facilitating the integration of renewable energy, improving grid flexibility, and supporting the rising electricity demand associated with digitalization and electrification. Energy price fluctuations closely tie carbon markets to fossil fuel dynamics, highlighting their continued dependence.

These findings suggest integrated energy policies that jointly address energy security, AI-driven demand, EV expansion, smart-grid development, and carbon market stability to ensure a resilient and sustainable energy transition.

verified_metadata.title: AI-enabled optimization of integrated photovoltaic-latent heat thermal energy storage systems for sustainable building energy management
verified_metadata.abstract: Global energy transition and building decarbonization have increased interest in photovoltaic and latent heat thermal energy storage (PV-LHTES) systems for zero energy buildings. This review focuses on building integrated PV-LHTES systems, including building envelopes containing PCMs and latent heat storage units coupled with photovoltaic generation, HVAC systems, and domestic hot water supply. Sensible and thermochemical storage are discussed only briefly to distinguish their functions from those of LHTES in building energy management. Recent studies on the use of AI to optimize integrated PV-LHTES systems are reviewed within a common technical framework. Physical integration of PV and LHTES enables solar energy conversion, thermal buffering, and load shifting, while AI supports system prediction, optimization, and operational control. Data based prediction and adaptive control can improve system design and operation under changing building conditions. Current building applications of PCMs include macroencapsulated panels, microencapsulated PCMs incorporated into cement or gypsum, and phase change Trombe walls. Dynamically movable PCM layers have also been investigated to make better use of natural heat and cold sources, thereby reducing summer heat gain and winter heat loss. Important limitations remain, including cycling stability, leakage, declining thermal response, high energy use during production, environmental impacts, and long payback periods. Further development of AI based PV-LHTES optimization requires better handling of heterogeneous data, improved transfer of models across building types, and greater interpretability and reliability of AI methods. Progress in materials, control methods, data management, and building energy policy will further support the application of PV-LHTES systems in low carbon buildings.

verified_metadata.title: Multimodal unsupervised early warning of thermal runaway in traction batteries incorporating target-cell-aware relative-voltage pseudo-heatmap
verified_metadata.abstract: To address the scarcity of labeled fault samples prior to thermal runaway, the complexity of real-world operating conditions, and the difficulty in identifying weak cell-level anomalies, this study proposes a multimodal feature construction method incorporating target-cell-aware relative-voltage pseudo-heatmaps (RVPHs) and develops an unsupervised anomaly detection model with multimodal feature fusion for early thermal-runaway warning. The method integrates statistical features, time–frequency spectrograms, and target-cell-aware RVPHs to provide multidimensional representations of each target cell. The model uses modality-specific branches to encode and fuse heterogeneous inputs and locates potential faulty cells based on cell-level reconstruction errors. Validation using real-world vehicle operating data shows that, for vehicles that experienced thermal runaway, the model can identify anomalous cells several hours to several days in advance. Fixed-threshold tests on normal vehicles across different SOC ranges and cumulative mileage levels trigger no alarms. In cross-model validation, the model can still capture persistent deviations of anomalous cells from the remaining cells in the battery pack. The full multimodal model achieves the best overall performance, with Top-1 and Top-3 localization rates of 91.03% and 94.24%, respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method for early thermal-runaway warning.

verified_metadata.title: Economical, reliable, and deployable operation of integrated energy systems for communities: a hierarchical multi-timescale constrained reinforcement learning approach
verified_metadata.abstract: Integrated energy systems (IES) for communities are key building blocks of urban energy management, yet reliable operation is challenged by multi-energy coupling, multiple operational constraints, and significantly different device response speeds. Existing deep reinforcement learning methods typically operate on a single timescale and rely on penalty functions for constraint handling, where manually tuned coefficients are scenario-sensitive and often yield unstable constraint satisfaction, undermining the reliability required for real-world deployment. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a hierarchical multi-timescale dispatch method that combines constrained reinforcement learning with mathematical programming, in which a cross-timescale constraint propagation mechanism feeds residual constraint information from the inner layer back to the outer-layer policy, transforming one-way hierarchical scheduling into closed loop coordination across timescales. The method is validated on a community-scale system in Beijing, China, under typical winter and summer scenarios against six benchmark strategies. Results show that the proposed method reduces total operating cost by 3.01% and 1.10% relative to mixed-integer linear programming under the multi-timescale framework, and by 5.06% and 6.86% relative to single-timescale deep reinforcement learning, while reducing constraint violations by over 98% compared with penalty-function-based reinforcement learning and maintaining a daily cumulative online computation time below 0.1 s. Further evaluations confirm the reliability and robustness of the proposed method under different parameter settings and operating uncertainties. These findings provide a theoretical basis and practical foundation for the economical, reliable, and deployable multi-timescale dispatch optimisation of IES.

verified_metadata.title: Towards sustainable aviation: aircraft fuel flow estimation using an improved iTransformer for pollutant emission calculations
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurate estimation of aircraft fuel consumption and emissions is essential for sustainable aviation but is constrained by the lack of publicly available fuel flow data and the limited accuracy of existing methods. This study proposes an improved iTransformer-based approach for aircraft fuel flow estimation using ADS-B data. First, key variables influencing fuel flow are identified through Spearman correlation analysis. An LSTM network and a multi-head differential attention mechanism are then incorporated into the iTransformer architecture to improve temporal feature extraction, estimation accuracy, and model generalization. QAR and ADS-B data are preprocessed and analyzed, with the model trained using QAR data and subsequently applied to ADS-B data for fuel flow estimation. The fuel flow estimation yields an average accuracy of 93.7% based on 4968 flights covering 11 aircraft types. Further estimation of fuel consumption and pollutant emissions was performed on a dataset of 23,756 flights with the same 11 aircraft types, and the overall average accuracy of all estimation results is higher than 90%. The resulting emission estimates are consistent with observed operational characteristics. Furthermore, the proposed method is applied to a large-scale dataset of 855,000 flight movements across mainland China in October 2024, enabling nationwide quantification of aviation fuel consumption and emissions. The results demonstrate the robustness and scalability of the proposed approach and highlight its potential to support aviation energy management, emissions monitoring, and sustainable aviation development.

verified_metadata.title: Integrated PEM electrolyzer–fuel cell polygeneration system powered by photovoltaic–thermal solar energy: Exergoeconomic analysis and artificial intelligence optimization
verified_metadata.abstract: Growing requirements for low-carbon energy, freshwater, and thermal services have made the development of efficient, integrated systems based on renewable resources increasingly necessary. Accordingly, this study proposes a novel poly-generation configuration powered by a concentrated photovoltaic thermal unit for the simultaneous production of electricity, freshwater, heating, and cooling. The proposed system combines a proton exchange membrane electrolyzer for hydrogen generation, a proton exchange membrane fuel cell for electricity production, a humidification–dehumidification desalination unit, an organic Rankine cycle for recovering waste heat, and liquefied natural gas–trans-critical CO2 compression refrigeration subsystems to provide cooling. A detailed assessment encompassing energy, exergy, and economic (3E) performance is performed, after which a tri-objective optimization is applied to improve both operational efficiency and overall cost metrics. The optimization outputs reveal that the system attains an overall exergy efficiency of 3.08%, a poly-generation unit cost of 44.65/GJ, and a total cost rate of 13.48/GJ. When compared with the baseline configuration, these optimized operating conditions yield substantial gains in thermodynamic performance and economic viability, thereby validating the practicality and promise of the concentrated photovoltaic thermal-based poly-generation arrangement for low-carbon multi-energy utilization.

verified_metadata.title: Data-driven energy consumption prediction for electric vehicles considering differentiated driving behavior: A hybrid machine learning model
verified_metadata.abstract: To address the significant impacts of heterogeneous driving behaviors on electric vehicle energy consumption, as well as the limited performance of conventional data-driven models that ignore differentiated driving features and long-term temporal dependencies, this paper constructs a data-driven hybrid machine learning prediction framework that fully considers differentiated driving behaviors throughout speed sequence generation and energy consumption forecasting. Based on 10,170 real-world kinematic segments, hierarchical K-means clustering is adopted to separate driving conditions and classify styles, while a LightGBM-based model is established for online driving style recognition. Style-specific Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) speed prediction method is further employed to generate speed sequences, and a dual-layer LSTM-Transformer (DLLT) architecture is designed to capture both local dynamics and long-term dependencies of energy consumption. Results show that the recognition model achieves 96.07% accuracy, and the DLLT model yields a weighted-average R2 of 0.9412, significantly outperforming baseline methods. The proposed data-driven hybrid machine learning framework accurately captures heterogeneous energy consumption patterns under different driving behaviors, achieving superior accuracy and generalization under low-frequency sampling compared with undifferentiated generic models.

verified_metadata.title: A machine learning-based framework for electric carsharing service and energy optimization via V2G interactions
verified_metadata.abstract: One-way station-based electric carsharing (ECS) improves shared mobility convenience and sustainability, but encounters supply-demand imbalance issue affects ECS promotions. Regional supply-demand attributes and real-time distributions are vague to identify. Supply-demand imbalance status further affects ECS utilization, charging efficiency and service revenue. Therefore, we propose a machine learning-based framework for ECS service and energy optimization, focusing on spatiotemporal supply-demand identification, prediction, and rebalancing. Initially, a multi-category data collection and analysis pattern is formulated, involving land-using forms, ECS trajectory, user orders and station energy operations information. Then, Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) and Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) are integrated to predict user time-varying demands and station-based supply capacity within the divided ECS hot and cold regions. Group-aware splitting mechanism (GASM) and time-grouped validation mechanism (TGVM) are further introduced to enhance prediction accuracy. Finally, a user-oriented allocation model is developed for ECS supply-demand rebalancing and energy optimization. Based on dynamic price incentive mode (DPIM), an improved immune genetic algorithm (IIGA) is applied to maximize service allocation and energy operation profits. Flow-Conservative Integer Mapping Mechanism (FCIMM) and adaptive crossover and mutation factors are utilized in IIGA to enhance model convergence and robustness. Case study proves that DBSCAN and CatBoost models show higher supply-demand identification and prediction accuracy than benchmark methods. Sensitivity analysis results demonstrate that DPIM improves ECS service balance in multi-scale scenarios and enhances energy efficiency and profitability by vehicle-to-grid (V2G) interactions. To conclude, our research contributes to more efficient ECS service and energy optimization in urban transportation systems.

verified_metadata.title: LiDAR-informed transformer framework for spatiotemporal estimation of rotor-effective wind speed beyond Taylor’s frozen turbulence hypothesis
verified_metadata.abstract: The accurate estimation of rotor effective wind speed (REWS) is crucial in terms of improving feedforward control and enabling the effective optimization of wind turbine performance. Currently, upstream measurements provided by light detection and ranging (LiDAR) technology have been employed for REWS estimation; however, Taylor’s frozen turbulence hypothesis is commonly assumed. Furthermore, effects present in real atmospheric boundary layer flow, e.g., turbulence evolution, are neglected; thus, estimation accuracy is limited. This paper proposes a data-driven approach that utilizes a transformer model to estimate REWS directly from LiDAR measurements. Through its attention mechanism, the transformer model understands the spatiotemporal information of the wind, effectively bypassing Taylor’s hypothesis. LiDAR measurements are obtained from high-fidelity large eddy simulations of the atmospheric boundary layer across different wind speeds and preview distances to train and evaluate the proposed framework. The obtained results demonstrate that the transformer estimation exhibits good agreement with the target REWS values, significantly outperforming the REWS estimated with Taylor’s hypothesis. The proposed model improved both the time lag and wind speed overestimation present in the LiDAR measurements. At the closest measurement gate, the root mean squared error of the estimation was reduced by 68%, 56%, and 37% for mean wind speeds of 12, 14, and 16 m/s. The findings of this study highlight the application prospects of the proposed framework in real-world wind turbine control.

verified_metadata.title: Establishment and verification of a predictive model for the startup strategy of turbine mode of the pumped storage unit based on machine learning
verified_metadata.abstract: With the global energy transition accelerating and large-scale integration of intermittent renewable energy sources—primarily wind and photovoltaics—grid frequency regulation and peak-shaving demands have intensified significantly. Pumped storage units, owing to their fast response and multi-functional regulation capabilities, serve as key supporting equipment for modern power systems. However, the strong coupling of runner speed, guide vane opening, flow rate, and pressure during the startup transient makes accurate prediction and intelligent control extremely challenging. This study investigates the pump-turbine of a high-head pumped storage power station. 15 transient CFD simulations are conducted across three typical startup strategies: Linear, 2Slopes, and BEP. A full-dimensional time-series dataset is constructed, covering hydraulic performance, hydraulic losses, runner force characteristics, and pressure pulsations. Three deep learning models—LSTM, TCN, and Informer—are trained with startup control parameters as inputs for multi-target prediction. Model performance is systematically evaluated using R2, MAE, and RMSE. Key findings are as follows. For temporally regular signals such as flow rate, output power, and guide vane pressure pulsations, all three models achieve high accuracy (R2 > 0.90). Under complex nonlinear BEP conditions with coupled multi-physics dynamics, Informer—leveraging ProbSparse self-attention and generative decoding—achieves the lowest overall error and best comprehensive performance. TCN excels in local feature fitting but struggles with long-range temporal dependencies. LSTM performs well under steady conditions but degrades significantly under strong nonlinear and abrupt-change scenarios. This work presents an efficient, data-driven prediction framework for rapid optimization of pumped storage startup strategies, effectively avoiding the high computational cost of repeated multi-scheme CFD simulations.

verified_metadata.title: Machine learning prediction of hydrochar and bio-oil properties during biomass hydrothermal conversion with aqueous phase recirculation
verified_metadata.abstract: Hydrothermal conversion coupled with aqueous phase (AP) recirculation has emerged as a promising strategy for enhancing biomass valorization by improving product yields and energy recovery (ER). For the first time, AP recirculation was explicitly incorporated as a specific input variable into ML models (Model 1 and Model 2) for predicting hydrochar and bio-oil properties during hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) and hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL), respectively. Four ML algorithms were systematically compared and optimized, with Gradient Boosting Regression (GBR) showing a slight performance advantage. Model 1 (GBR) delivered the best performance for hydrochar properties, with testing R2 of 0.98 for hydrochar yield (HY) and 0.95 for energy recovery of hydrochar (ER_HC). Model 2 (GBR) achieved the most robust performance, with testing R2 of 0.83 for bio-oil yield (BY) and 0.85 for energy recovery of bio-oil (ER_BO). Feature importance analysis revealed that AP recirculation ranked among the top one or two most influential variables for both HTC and HTL. Increasing AP recirculation initially led to significant improvements in hydrochar and bio-oil yields as well as ER, whereas further increases resulted in diminishing benefits due to the gradual saturation of organic compounds in the AP. Furthermore, donut chart analysis demonstrated that biomass elemental composition contributed more significantly to product properties than hydrothermal conditions. Finally, the integrated software enables rapid prediction of hydrothermal products, facilitating biomass screening, AP recirculation-assisted hydrothermal conversion process route selection, and optimization.

title: Data-driven digital twin for Solar Power Towers: Achieving experimental accuracy via sim2real deep-learning transfer
abstract: Concentrating solar technologies (CST) have shown a wide potential for power generation at highly-irradiated locations and for thermochemical processes and industrial heat production. In particular, solar power tower (SPT) systems are especially effective for high temperature applications. However, a techno-economical gap in terms of operation and maintenance, flux and meteorological conditions’ monitoring, and plant control still hinders the serial industrial adoption of this energy source. In order to tailor an embedded solution for flux prediction and control, this work presents the simulation-to-reality learning step of an Attention-Gated U-Net (AttU-Net) model especially tailored for flux density prediction. This neural network, previously trained with a purely synthetic dataset, has been re-trained with an experimental dataset composed of 562 samples, which was obtained between May 2025, and July 2025. The training results show solid accuracies above 95%, structural similarity indexes (SSIM) up to 97% and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) metrics over 30 dB, which is consistent with model robustness and accuracy. Inference ability and times were tested with 10 held-out samples, reaching accuracies above 96%, SSIMs above 92%, as well as PSNRs above 30 dB. These results suggest the algorithm’s suitability for future integration within flux density control loops to improve plant operability and safety.

verified_metadata.title: Selective expert-guided reinforcement learning for vehicle cabin thermal management
verified_metadata.abstract: Model-free reinforcement learning for vehicle cabin thermal management requires extensive environment interaction, as early exploration can generate ineffective or energy-intensive actuator commands. Expert demonstrations can reduce this burden, but their utility and reliability depend on how expert information is used during learning. We propose Selective Expert-Guided Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (SEG-TD3), which selectively allocates expert-derived information across value learning, exploration, and actor regularization. Genuine expert transitions and one-step counterfactual probes jointly support critic learning, whereas only genuine expert actions provide residual guidance for exploration. For actor learning, a detached positive-advantage Soft Q-filter admits only critic-supported candidate actions for actor regularization. Expert influence decays with accumulated experience and is removed at deployment. SEG-TD3 and five learned baselines were trained for 100 episodes with five matched random seeds on a physics-based vehicle thermal management system and evaluated using deterministic controllers, mechanism ablations, and 12 operating conditions. Under the same interaction budget, SEG-TD3 reached high training returns earlier than standard TD3 and reduced mean cabin-temperature MAE at episode 100 by 13.1% with similar TMS energy use. Across the 12-condition suite, SEG-TD3 reduced mean MAE and TMS energy use by 18.8% and 9.7%, respectively, relative to TD3; both reductions were statistically significant after Holm correction. SEG-TD3 also required 87.7% less measured reinforcement-learning update time than SPReD-E in the same software and hardware environment. These results show that role-selective allocation of expert information can improve interaction efficiency and closed-loop performance without retaining expert guidance at deployment.

verified_metadata.title: Semantic-mask-enhanced deep reinforcement learning for energy storage scheduling in virtual building-cluster microgrids with vehicle-to-building flexibility
verified_metadata.abstract: To address the optimal operation of building-cluster microgrids integrating multiple distributed energy resources and vehicle-to-building (V2B) flexibility, this study constructs a 30-day virtual environment using adapted multi-source building load data and public electric vehicle (EV) charging records. Vehicle arrival, charging, discharge eligibility, and departure are modeled under time-of-use prices. A state-dependent semantic action masking mechanism is developed for deep reinforcement learning (DRL) based stationary energy storage system (ESS) scheduling. The mechanism integrates ESS physical constraints and operational information to dynamically construct a state-dependent candidate action set. Deep Q-Network (DQN), Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (D3QN), and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) select the final ESS action. Under the V2B-enabled condition, EVs supply 141.5 MWh to buildings, and the average net electricity cost per unit charging energy decreases by 24.2%. Across six paired comparisons, semantic action masking reduces operating cost and total grid purchase by averages of 1.27% and 3.77%, respectively. The action modification rate decreases by an average of 56.18 percentage points, and the variability of total episode returns during late-stage training decreases by an average of 51.05%. Among the evaluated configurations, PPO with semantic action masking and V2B achieves the lowest operating cost, reducing operating cost, total grid purchase, and peak-period grid purchase by 18.5%, 13.2%, and 44.7%, respectively, compared with the baseline configuration without ESS or V2B. These findings provide a methodological reference for the intelligent operation and coordinated utilization of flexible energy resources in building-cluster microgrids.

verified_metadata.title: A dual-driven framework for low-carbon dispatch in the steel enterprise: Integrating deep learning forecasting and distributionally robust optimization under carbon price uncertainty
verified_metadata.abstract: The steel industry remains one of the largest industrial carbon emitters worldwide and is exposed to increasingly stringent carbon market regulations. The operation of Renewable Integrated Energy Systems (RIES) in steel enterprises is complicated by multi-dimensional uncertainties, including intermittent renewable generation, strongly coupled multi-energy loads, and volatile carbon prices. To address these challenges, this study develops a dual-driven framework that combines high-precision forecasting with a two-stage distributionally robust optimization model (TSDROM) for day-ahead and real-time low-carbon dispatch of a steel enterprise RIES. First, a chaos game optimization-enhanced hybrid forecasting architecture, integrating Transformer, bidirectional long short-term memory, and XGBoost, is constructed to predict renewable generation, multi-energy loads, and carbon trading prices with hourly resolution. The prediction errors are then used to build a Wasserstein distance-based ambiguity set, enabling data-driven uncertainty characterization without assuming a specific probability distribution. On this basis, a TSDROM with a linear affine recourse policy coordinates electricity, thermal, gas, hydrogen, and cooling subsystems under worst-case uncertainty realizations. A case study shows that carbon capture reduces daily physical emissions by 76.0% relative to pre-capture direct emissions and yields a 90.13 t/day Emissions Trading System (ETS) allowance surplus under the adopted capacity configuration. Under the largest resampling configuration considered, explicitly modeling carbon price uncertainty reduces the total system cost by CNY 1.105 million relative to the corresponding case without carbon-price uncertainty. The proposed framework provides an operationally tractable “prediction–optimization” paradigm for robust and cost-effective low-carbon dispatch in steel and other energy-intensive industries.

verified_metadata.title: Unveiling nonlinear thresholds and synergistic effects in continuous supercritical water gasification of biomass via interpretable machine learning
verified_metadata.abstract: Driven by the global imperative for green hydrogen transition, supercritical water gasification (SCWG) of biomass waste has gained attention for its high conversion efficiency. Developing an interpretable and generalizable model to predict hydrogen yield is essential for accelerating industrial deployment of biomass-based SCWG, yet related studies remain scarce. Herein, experimental data from a continuous SCWG reactor are used to identify key parameters, including biomass elemental and proximate analyses, as well as operating temperature, pressure, residence time, and biomass concentration. These parameters are then used to develop XGBoost, CatBoost, and RF models for hydrogen yield prediction. The results indicate that the XGBoost model demonstrated superior predictive accuracy, with an R2 of 0.975, an RMSE of 0.944, and an MAE of 0.626. Furthermore, based on interpretable machine learning analysis, this study elucidated the synergistic regulatory mechanism of multivariate nonlinear interactions on the hydrogen production performance of continuous-flow SCWG. Three key coupling effects in the process were quantitatively analyzed, including the thermodynamic competition between steam reforming and decarboxylation reactions, the time-temperature compensation effect of temperature-residence time, and mass-transfer limitations imposed by ash and high-concentration feed. The results provide a direct mechanistic basis for delineating the reactor's optimal operating window and guiding process amplification.

verified_metadata.title: Neural Network Enhanced Digital Twin Based Carbon Oriented Planning of Distributed Generation and Hydrogen Microgrids in Prosumer-Centric Energy hub
verified_metadata.abstract: Carbon-aware distribution planning requires investment decisions that account for how storage, hydrogen-based microgrids, and network carbon flows interact over time. Existing planning and scheduling models usually treat these elements separately, leaving weak representation of storage-induced emission shifting and hydrogen-microgrid carbon responsibility. This paper develops an integrated planning framework for a power distribution network coupled with hydrogen-based microgrids under emission targets and chronological carbon-flow effects. The framework formulates distributed generation, electrical storage, and hydrogen storage decisions within a two-stage stochastic structure, transfers carbon burden across charging and discharging periods. The resulting nonlinear formulation is converted into a mixed-integer nonconvex quadratically constrained programming structure and solved through a penalty-based proximal-distance scheme. Tests on a modified network show that coordinated hydrogen flexibility reduces total annual cost by about 20.5% compared with an electrical-storage-dominant compliance case while preserving the same emission target. Hydrogen-specific carbon-flow guidance reduces system emissions by about 18.5% relative to the unrestricted operating trial and lowers the carbon intensity of hydrogen-related electricity use from 0.317 to 0.114 Ton/MWh. Annual hydrogen-storage complementarity also decreases operating cost by nearly 5.9% and increases renewable utilization by about 1.7 percentage points. The results indicate that chronological carbon tracing can materially alter storage valuation and coordinated low-carbon planning.
