title: Content-Aware Image Compression Model for Macromolecular Crystallography Data.
abstract: The structural biology community faces the challenge of managing massive data volumes from macromolecular crystallography (MX) experiments, motivating the development of efficient lossy compression methods for permanent data archival. In this paper, we introduce a novel content-aware deep image compression model specifically designed for MX data. Bragg reflections (also called spots) position information derived from a spot finder is incorporated during training to guide the compression preserving content-relevant regions, while inference remains fully independent of Bragg spot information. We further investigate different mask generation strategies to balance the trade-off between compression ratio and diffraction pattern preservation. Additionally, we propose novel content-aware loss functions to better preserve Bragg spot information. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves both higher spot detection performance and superior compression ratio compared to other methods, enabling scientifically reliable compression for crystallographic data archiving and analysis. Our code is available at https://github.com/DJX1995/BNL-ImageCompression.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Cardiac Output Prediction From Echocardiograms: Self-Supervised Learning with Limited Data.
abstract: Cardiac Output (CO) is a key parameter in the diagnosis and management of cardiovascular diseases. However, its accurate measurement requires right-heart catheterization, an invasive and time-consuming procedure, motivating the development of reliable non-invasive alternatives using echocardiography. In this work, we propose a self-supervised learning (SSL) pretraining strategy based on SimCLR to improve CO prediction from apical four-chamber echocardiographic videos. The pretraining is performed using the same limited dataset available for the downstream task, demonstrating the potential of SSL even under data scarcity. Our results show that SSL mitigates overfitting and improves representation learning, achieving an average Pearson correlation of 0.41 on the test set and outperforming PanEcho, a model trained on over one million echocardiographic exams.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Improving Segmentation of Retinal Arteries and Veins Using Cardiac Signal in Doppler Holograms.
abstract: Doppler holography is an emerging retinal imaging technique that captures the dynamic behavior of blood flow with high temporal resolution, enabling quantitative assessment of retinal hemodynamics. This requires accurate segmentation of retinal arteries and veins, but traditional segmentation methods focus solely on spatial information and overlook the temporal richness of holographic data. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective approach for artery-vein segmentation in temporal Doppler holograms using standard segmentation architectures. By incorporating features derived from a dedicated pulse analysis pipeline, our method allows conventional U-Nets to exploit temporal dynamics and achieve performance comparable to more complex attention- or iteration-based models. These findings demonstrate that time-resolved preprocessing can unlock the full potential of deep learning for Doppler holography, opening new perspectives for quantitative exploration of retinal hemodynamics. The dataset is publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/DigitalHolography/
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Harmonic-Fused Dual-Domain Network for Low-Concentration Magnetic Particle Imaging Reconstruction.
abstract: Reconstruction of low-concentration magnetic particle imaging (MPI) is a critical challenge for clinical translation, due to low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), severe artifacts, and blurred details in the reconstructed harmonic images. The ISBI-2026 LCR-MPI Challenge is focused on achieving high-fidelity fifth-harmonic reconstruction from low-concentration data. The network takes normalized third- and fifth-harmonic images as dual-channel input and integrates a spatially adaptive denormalization-based fusion module to leverage the structural prior of the third harmonic for guiding the restoration of noisy fifth-harmonic images. To further improve the signal-to-noise ratio, a spatial-frequency dual-domain fusion scheme based on a symmetric encoder-decoder architecture with fast Fourier convolution is adopted. Additionally, a learnable gated skip connection is incorporated to adaptively regulate network information flow and enhance feature representation capability. Experiments on the challenge dataset demonstrate that DuLCR-Net outperforms the baselines, providing an effective solution for low-concentration MPI reconstruction and advancing its clinical applicability.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Self-Supervised Vision Transformer for Surgical Phase Recognition in Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection.
abstract: Surgical phase recognition is critical for context-aware interventions, but deep learning models require large, costly annotated datasets. This work presents DINO-Endo, an efficient framework pairing a self-supervised DINOv2 Vision Transformer (ViT-S/14) backbone with lightweight temporal models. Through sequential domain adaptation—pretraining on unannotated porcine videos followed by human endoscopic videos—our approach produces highly discriminative features that enable simple temporal decoders to achieve state-of-the-art performance. We demonstrate 89.5% accuracy on patient dataset and 90.0% on complex porcine dataset, outperforming existing methods while using 14-times fewer parameters than foundation models like V-JEPA2. Our comprehensive evaluation reveals that powerful SSL features reduce temporal modeling complexity, with dataset characteristics determining optimal decoder architecture. This work establishes that domain-specific self-supervised pretraining combined with efficient temporal heads achieves state-of-the-art results while reducing annotation dependency and computational requirements for clinical deployment.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: A Multi-Scale Linear-Time Encoder for Whole-Slide Image Analysis.
abstract: We introduce Multi-scale Adaptive Recurrent Biomedical Linear-time Encoder (MARBLE), the first purely Mamba-based multi-state multiple instance learning (MIL) framework for whole-slide image (WSI) analysis. MARBLE processes multiple magnification levels in parallel and integrates coarse-to-fine reasoning within a linear-time state-space model, efficiently capturing cross-scale dependencies with minimal parameter overhead. WSI analysis remains challenging due to gigapixel resolutions and hierarchical magnifications, while existing MIL methods typically operate at a single scale and transformer-based approaches suffer from quadratic attention costs. By coupling parallel multi-scale processing with linear-time sequence modeling, MARBLE provides a scalable and modular alternative to attention-based architectures. Experiments on five public datasets show improvements of up to$\mathbf{6. 9 \%}$in AUC,$\mathbf{2 0. 3 \%}$in accuracy, and$\mathbf{2. 3 \%}$in C-index, establishing MARBLE as an efficient and generalizable framework for multi-scale WSI analysis.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Beer-Lambert Autoencoder for Unsupervised Stain Representation Learning and Deconvolution in Multi-Immunohistochemical Brightfield Histology Images.
abstract: Separating the contributions of individual chromogenic stains in RGB histology whole slide images (WSIs) is essential for stain normalization, quantitative assessment of marker expression, and cell-level readouts in immunohistochemistry (IHC). Classical Beer-Lambert (BL) color deconvolution is well-established for two- or three-stain settings, but becomes under-determined and unstable for multiplex IHC (mIHC) with$K>3$chromogens. We present a simple, data-driven encoder-decoder architecture that learns cohortspecific stain characteristics for mIHC RGB WSIs and yields crisp, well-separated per-stain concentration maps. The encoder is a compact U-Net that predicts$K$nonnegative concentration channels; the decoder is a differentiable BL forward model with a learnable stain matrix initialized from typical chromogen hues. Training is unsupervised with a perceptual reconstruction objective augmented by loss terms that discourage unnecessary stain mixing. On a colorectal mIHC panel comprising 5 stains (H, CDX2, MUC2, MUC5, CD8) we show excellent RGB reconstruction, and significantly reduced inter-channel bleed-through compared with matrix-based deconvolution. Code and model are available at https://github.com/measty/StainQuant.git.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: A Temporally Aware Transformer Model for Predicting Personalized Head Growth and Surgical Outcomes in Craniosynostosis.
abstract: Craniosynostosis is the premature fusion of the cranial sutures, often requiring corrective surgery. However, treatment selection remains subjective due to the lack of longitudinal image datasets, hindering the creation of tools that can predict pathologic development and treatment outcomes. In this work, we introduce a temporally aware transformer to predict personalized cranial development before and after treatment using a unique longitudinal 3D craniofacial photogrammetry dataset. We combine a geometric autoencoder to create low-dimensional encodings of each photogram and a dual-branch transformer guided by developmental context embeddings for independent modeling of natural growth and anatomical changes introduced by surgery. Trained on 1,493 pre- and postsurgical 3D photograms, our method outperformed state-of-the-art models with a point-to-point prediction error of 2.09$\pm 1.51 ~\text{mm}$evaluated on an independent longitudinal dataset. This is the first method for predicting both pre- and postsurgical development in children with craniosynostosis, offering a foundation for objective treatment planning.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Protostage-NET: A Clinically Guided Foundation Model With Prototypical Learning for Automated Amd Grading From Oct Images.
abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a major cause of vision loss, where accurate staging is essential for treatment. However, most recent approaches for OCT images remain limited to binary classification and do not capture the full clinical spectrum of the disease. To address this gap, we propose ProtoStage-Net, an explainable foundation model framework for fine-grained AMD staging. Our method leverages the DINOv2 vision foundation model as a backbone, fully fine-tuned for OCT data, and introduces two clinically inspired attention mechanisms: the Clinically Guided Channel Attention (CGCA) module, which emphasizes diseaserelevant feature channels, and the Lesion Localization Module (LLM), which highlights pathological retinal regions. Classification is performed through a hierarchical prototypical learning strategy at binary, ternary, and detailed six-class levels, providing transparent similarity-based decisions. In addition, we incorporate temporal ordinal constraints to enforce clinically valid AMD progression pathways. We evaluate ProtoStage-Net on a cohort of 954 OCT B-scans acquired from three different imaging devices. Our framework achieves a macro F1-score of 93.49 %, surpassing the baseline foundation model by more than 2 % and outperforming recent state-of-the-art methods. Extensive experiments further demonstrate the clinical explainability of our approach, with saliency maps confirming that ProtoStage-Net accurately localizes lesion regions across different AMD grades.

verified_metadata.conference_title: 2026 IEEE 23rd International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
verified_metadata.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a major cause of vision loss, where accurate staging is essential for treatment. However, most recent approaches for OCT images remain limited to binary classification and do not capture the full clinical spectrum of the disease. To address this gap, we propose ProtoStage-Net, an explainable foundation model framework for fine-grained AMD staging. Our method leverages the DINOv2 vision foundation model as a backbone, fully fine-tuned for OCT data, and introduces two clinically inspired attention mechanisms: the Clinically Guided Channel Attention (CGCA) module, which emphasizes diseaserelevant feature channels, and the Lesion Localization Module (LLM), which highlights pathological retinal regions. Classification is performed through a hierarchical prototypical learning strategy at binary, ternary, and detailed six-class levels, providing transparent similarity-based decisions. In addition, we incorporate temporal ordinal constraints to enforce clinically valid AMD progression pathways. We evaluate ProtoStage-Net on a cohort of 954 OCT B-scans acquired from three different imaging devices. Our framework achieves a macro F1-score of 93.49 %, surpassing the baseline foundation model by more than 2 % and outperforming recent state-of-the-art methods. Extensive experiments further demonstrate the clinical explainability of our approach, with saliency maps confirming that ProtoStage-Net accurately localizes lesion regions across different AMD grades.

title: Semi-Supervised Fetal Echocardiography Segmentation and CHD Classification.
abstract: Automated analysis of fetal cardiac ultrasound requires simultaneous segmentation of anatomical structures and classification of congenital heart disease (CHD), yet expert annotation is scarce in clinical practice. We present a semisupervised dual-task framework that jointly optimizes pixel-level segmentation of 14 cardiac structures (plus background) and multi-label CHD classification across 7 pathological categories from four standard cardiac imaging planes. The framework builds on a shared DINOv2 ViT-B/14 backbone with partial fine-tuning, where the lower six transformer blocks are frozen to preserve generic visual representations while the upper six are fully updated for cardiac domain adaptation. A dual-bottleneck design isolates the segmentation and classification gradient flows, preventing destructive task interference. Semi-supervised training follows a UniMatch-style paradigm with an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) teacher, CutMix augmentation, and view-aware pseudo-label filtering, complemented by label smoothing and a pseudo-label ramp-up schedule. On a dataset of 2,800 fetal cardiac ultrasound slices with only 391 annotated cases$(\sim 15.6 {\%})$, our method achieves a mean Dice of 82.40%, NSD of 60.22%, and macro-F1{@}0.5 of 0.539, substantially outperforming the supervised-only baseline and a prior Swin-UNETR-based semi-supervised approach.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: LUMOS: Universal Semi-Supervised Oct Retinal Layer Segmentation with Hierarchical Reliable Mutual Learning.
abstract: Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) layer segmentation faces challenges due to annotation scarcity and heterogeneous label granularities across datasets. While semi-supervised learning helps alleviate label scarcity, existing methods typically assume a fixed granularity, failing to fully exploit cross-granularity supervision. This paper presents LUMOS, a semi-supervised universal OCT retinal layer segmentation framework based on a Dual-Decoder Network with a Hierarchical Prompting Strategy (DDN-HPS) and Reliable Progressive Multi-granularity Learning (RPML). DDN-HPS combines a dual-branch architecture with a multi-granularity prompting strategy to effectively suppress pseudo-label noise propagation. Meanwhile, RPML introduces region-level reliability weighing and a progressive training approach that guides the model from easier to more difficult tasks, ensuring the reliable selection of cross-granularity consistency targets, thereby achieving stable cross-granularity alignment. Experiments on six OCT datasets demonstrate that LUMOS largely outperforms existing methods and exhibits exceptional crossdomain and cross-granularity generalization capability.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Enhancing Renal Tumor Malignancy Prediction: Deep Learning with Automatic 3D CT Organ Focused Attention.
abstract: Accurate prediction of malignancy in renal tumors is crucial for informing clinical decisions and optimizing treatment strategies. However, existing imaging modalities lack the necessary accuracy to reliably predict malignancy before surgical intervention. While deep learning has shown promise in malignancy prediction using 3D CT images, traditional approaches often rely on manual segmentation to isolate the tumor region and reduce noise, which enhances predictive performance. Manual segmentation, however, is labor-intensive, costly, and dependent on expert knowledge. In this study, a deep learning framework was developed utilizing an Organ Focused Attention (OFA) loss function to modify the attention of image patches so that organ patches attend only to other organ patches. Hence, no segmentation of 3D renal CT images is required at deployment time for malignancy prediction. The proposed framework achieved an AUC of 0.685 and an F1-score of 0.872 on a private dataset from the UF Integrated Data Repository (IDR), and an AUC of 0.760 and an F1-score of 0.852 on the publicly available KiTS21 dataset. These results surpass the performance of conventional models that rely on segmentation-based cropping for noise reduction, demonstrating the framework's ability to enhance predictive accuracy without explicit segmentation input. The findings suggest that this approach offers a more efficient and reliable method for malignancy prediction, thereby enhancing clinical decision-making in renal cancer diagnosis.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Uncertainty-Guided Generation of Dark-Field Radiographs.
abstract: X-ray dark-field radiography provides complementary diagnostic information to conventional attenuation imaging by visualizing microstructural tissue changes through small-angle scattering. However, the limited availability of such data poses challenges for developing robust deep learning models. In this work, we present the first framework for generating dark-field images directly from standard attenuation chest X-rays using an Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Generative Adversarial Network. The model incorporates both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty to improve interpretability and reliability. Experiments demonstrate high structural fidelity of the generated images, with consistent improvement of quantitative metrics across stages. Furthermore, out-of-distribution evaluation confirms that the proposed model generalizes well. Our results indicate that uncertainty-guided generative modeling enables realistic dark-field image synthesis and provides a reliable foundation for future clinical applications.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: DERMAE: Improving Skin Lesion Classification Through Conditioned Latent Diffusion and MAE Distillation.
abstract: Skin lesion classification datasets often suffer from severe class imbalance, with malignant cases significantly underrepresented, leading to biased decision boundaries during deep learning training. We address this challenge using classconditioned diffusion models to generate synthetic dermatological images, followed by self-supervised MAE pretraining to enable huge ViT models to learn robust, domain-relevant features. To support deployment in practical clinical settings, where lightweight models are required, we apply knowledge distillation to transfer these representations to a smaller ViT student suitable for mobile devices. Our results show that MAE pretraining on synthetic data, combined with distillation, improves classification performance while enabling efficient on-device inference for practical clinical use.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Latent Space Modelling of a Biomedical Multimodal Dataset.
abstract: Clinical decision-making is rarely based on a single data source or modality. However, contemporary machine learning applications are mostly tailored to one specific modality. In this work, multimodal data integration, including histologic images and surgery-related texts, is tested for creating patient-level vector representations with information density comparable to that of pathologic analysis for Head and Neck (HNC) patients. Here, we rely on the multimodal HNCfocusing HANCOCK dataset. First, we transform individual modalities into vector representations using proven expert models tailored to their data types. Next, these are aligned into a joint latent space. Finally, the modality-specific vectors are recombined into a single patient-level embedding. With this approach, a mean AUC score of 0.67 for cancer-specific survival and 0.66 for 3 -year recurrence was achieved using only text and image data, compared to 0.79 when including structured pathologic data.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Classifying Breast Composition by Applying Deep Learning to Microwave Images: A Feasibility Study.
abstract: Breast density (BD) is a recognized risk factor for breast cancer. For mammograms, BD is described with four categories (A to D) according to the Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BIRADS), based on the increasing proportion of glandular tissue in the breast. For risk assessment, new approaches to quantifying the composition of the breast are of interest. This study explores identifying breast composition in 292 microwave images (MWI) from 81 patients with a pretrained ResNet50 convolutional neural network (CNN). Image normalization, weighted stochastic oversampling, and focal loss techniques were used to address the small dataset size and class imbalance, and repeated stratified cross-validation enabled statistically robust performance estimates. Compared to mammography (used as baseline in this study), the MWI-based density classification with$68 {\%}, 75 {\%}$, and 81% accuracy was achieved in 4-, 3 - and 2-class models, respectively.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Unsupervised Confidence Calibration for Active Learning.
abstract: In active learning, training data to be annotated is generally selected based on the confidence scores output by a classifier. However, the selection of the initial training data pool typically relies on random sampling since the classifier has not yet been trained. To address this issue, it is necessary to obtain a classifier that can appropriately assess confidence without supervised learning at the initial pool selection stage. In this study, we propose an unsupervised confidence calibration method based on domain adaptation. The proposed framework integrates a variational autoencoder into an unsupervised domain adaptation method and trains them simultaneously, thereby allowing the estimation of the joint distribution of input data and class labels. The proposed framework enables the classifier to compute reliable confidence scores for the target domain in a completely unsupervised manner. We conducted experiments on medical image datasets to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed unsupervised confidence calibration method and its impact on active learning. Experimental results showed that the proposed method consistently outperforms the baseline in all six transfer settings, achieving an average improvement of$1.0-1.5$points in classification accuracy across domains.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: A View-Specific Dual-Task Framework for Fetal Heart Ultrasound Analysis.
abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is the leading cause of fetal morbidity and mortality worldwide. The accuracy of prenatal ultrasound screening heavily depends on expert interpretation of standard views, including the four-chamber (4 CH), left and right ventricular outflow tracts (LVOT/RVOT), and threevessel trachea (3VT) views. However, clinical practice faces critical challenges including a shortage of domain experts, insufficient multi-view annotated data, and difficulty in identifying subtle anatomical features. To address the limitations of the official baseline (lightweight UNet)-namely insufficient model capacity, multi-task feature conflicts, inadequate handling of class imbalance, and underutilization of multiscale information-this study proposes a deep learning optimization framework built upon a large-scale multi-view fetal ultrasound dataset. Systematic improvements are introduced across four dimensions: backbone network upgrade with transfer learning, decoupled multi-task learning, multi-scale feature fusion, and robust loss function design. Specifically, Xception and MiT-B5 are adopted as backbone networks, a separated multi-task optimization strategy is employed, an FPN mechanism is integrated, and pos_weight adjustment is combined with Dice Loss. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a Dice coefficient (DSC) of 38.95% and a Macro F1-Score of 67.16% on the official validation set, and a DSC of 23.68% and a Macro F1-Score of 57.2% on the test set, with both metrics significantly outperforming the baseline model. The complete implementation is available at the following GitHub repository: https://github.com/linghs/fetal-ultrasound-chd-segmentation.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Dual-Network Semi-Supervised Framework for Carotid Plaque Ultrasound Analysis.
abstract: Accurately identifying carotid artery plaques and determining how dangerous they are is very important for preventing strokes and helping doctors make decisions. To address problems like limited labeled data and errors caused by combining segmentation and classification in existing methods, this paper presents a two-stage approach. In the first stage, a segmentation model using EfficientNet-B4 and feature pyramid network is applied, along with a semi-supervised learning method that uses pseudo-labels. With a small amount of labeled data, the model generates labels for a large amount of unlabeled data and trains on both, reducing the need for extensive labeling. In the second stage, a region-guided four-branch classification structure is introduced. Using the segmentation results, images from multiple views and anatomical regions are built, and separate encoders extract features and combine them for classification, which separates the tasks and prevents errors from spreading. In the final CSV challenge ranking, the method achieved an F1-Score of 37.91 and a seg-score of 62.8, with the seg-score reaching state-of-the-art (SOTA) level in the competition. This provides a reliable and efficient technical solution for automated ultrasound assessment of carotid artery plaques. verified_metadata.conference_title: 2026 IEEE 23rd International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurately identifying carotid artery plaques and determining how dangerous they are is very important for preventing strokes and helping doctors make decisions. To address problems like limited labeled data and errors caused by combining segmentation and classification in existing methods, this paper presents a two-stage approach. In the first stage, a segmentation model using EfficientNet-B4 and feature pyramid network is applied, along with a semi-supervised learning method that uses pseudo-labels. With a small amount of labeled data, the model generates labels for a large amount of unlabeled data and trains on both, reducing the need for extensive labeling. In the second stage, a region-guided four-branch classification structure is introduced. Using the segmentation results, images from multiple views and anatomical regions are built, and separate encoders extract features and combine them for classification, which separates the tasks and prevents errors from spreading. In the final CSV challenge ranking, the method achieved an F1-Score of 37.91 and a seg-score of 62.8, with the seg-score reaching state-of-the-art (SOTA) level in the competition. This provides a reliable and efficient technical solution for automated ultrasound assessment of carotid artery plaques. The complete implementation is available at the following GitHub repository:https://github.com/linghs/Carotid-Plaque-Assessment-CSV-Chanellge.

title: View-Conditioned Semi-Supervised Learning for Fetal Cardiac Ultrasound Analysis.
abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) screening from fetal cardiac ultrasound is challenged by view-specific label validity, longtailed small structures, and scarce expert annotations. We study a semi-supervised framework with dataset-provided view information, a LoRA-adapted SwinUNETR, viewconditioned masking, weak-to-strong consistency, invalidmass suppression on unmasked segmentation logits, and anatomy-constrained stage-wise checkpoint selection. On our internal split of 311 labeled images, 2409 unlabeled images, and 80 validation images, the final fixed-threshold model achieved Dice 76.98, NSD 57.85, and view-masked MacroF1@0.5 0.513. Relative to the direct joint-training baseline, diagnosis improved substantially while high-quality anatomy was preserved. These findings support anatomy-protected semi-supervised optimization and provide a reference for official evaluation.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Human-Aligned Learning of Interpretable Biomarkers for Lung Ultrasound Diagnosis.
abstract: Lung ultrasound (LUS) offers rapid, radiation-free bedside imaging, yet automated interpretation remains constrained by the opacity of end-to-end deep learning models. We propose a framework that explicitly aligns learned representations with human clinical reasoning by supervising models to predict interpretable visual biomarkers - clinician-recognized patterns such as A-lines, B-lines, and pleural irregularities - prior to diagnostic inference. This biomarker-aligned representation serves as a compact, semantically meaningful intermediate space for downstream tasks including lungseverity scoring, S/F ratio estimation, and disease classification. On a dataset of 189 patients (718 LUS videos), models trained via biomarker alignment outperform conventional task-specific networks while maintaining interpretability. A complementary user study demonstrates that decision tree explanations derived from biomarker features enhance clinicians' ability to identify incorrect model predictions compared to conventional saliency maps, underscoring the value of human-aligned representations in achieving both accuracy and transparency in diagnostic AI.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Protomsnet: A Prototypical Network for Interpretable Detection of Mitral Stenosis in Echocardiography.
abstract: Mitral stenosis (MS), a pathological narrowing of the mitral valve, is primarily evaluated using echocardiography, a modality that relies heavily on operator expertise for both image acquisition and interpretation. To reduce this dependency, machine learning (ML) methods have been developed to automate valvular disease detection. However, the rarity of MS limits the availability of labeled data for model training, and the poor interpretability of many ML models hinders clinical adoption. We propose ProtoMSNet, a prototypical network for MS detection from easily acquired echocardiographic views. ProtoMSNet enhances interpretability by offering explainable decisions through the use of informative visual prototypes. To address data scarcity, we introduce an etiology-based transfer learning approach that leverages pretraining on valve leaflet thickness and annular calcification, features associated with the rheumatic and calcific etiologies of MS. Experimental results demonstrate that ProtoMSNet accurately detects MS while generating clinically meaningful prototypes that capture the pathological diversity of MS.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Dual Cross-Attention Siamese Transformer for Rectal Tumor Regrowth Assessment in Watch-and-Wait Endoscopy.
abstract: Increasing evidence supports watch-and-wait (WW) surveillance for patients with rectal cancer who show clinical complete response (cCR) at restaging following total neoadjuvant treatment (TNT). However, accurate methods to early detect local regrowth (LR) from follow-up endoscopy images during WW are essential to manage care and prevent distant metastases. Hence, we developed a Siamese Swin Transformer with Dual Cross-Attention (SSDCA) to combine longitudinal endoscopic images at restaging and follow-up and distinguish cCR from LR. SSDCA leverages pretrained Swin Transformers to extract domain agnostic features and enhance robustness to imaging variations. Dual cross attention is implemented to emphasize features from the paired scans without requiring any spatial alignment to predict response. SSDCA as well as Swin-based baselines were trained using image pairs from 135 patients and evaluated on a held-out set of image pairs from 62 patients. SSDCA produced the best balanced accuracy (81.76% ± 0.04), sensitivity (90.07% ± 0.08), and specificity (72.86% ± 0.05). Robustness analysis showed stable performance irrespective of artifacts including blood, stool, telangiectasia, and poor image quality. UMAP clustering of extracted features showed maximal inter-cluster separation (1.45 ± 0.18) and minimal intra-cluster dispersion (1.07 ± 0.19) with SSDCA, confirming discriminative representation learning. All code and trained model checkpoints will be shared through GitHub upon manuscript acceptance.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

verified_metadata.title: ADAPT: Multibeamformer with Tunable Weight Fusion and Patch-Wise Learning for Ultrasound Imaging
verified_metadata.conference_title: 2026 IEEE 23rd International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
verified_metadata.abstract: In the recent past, deep learning (DL)-based beamformers have been employed to accelerate adaptive beamforming for ultrasound imaging. However, most of these approaches are trained to mimic a particular beamformer type for a predefined depth of imaging and require complete retraining to adapt to a new beamformer and depth. In this work, we propose a novel deep learning framework, ADAPT (Adaptive Depth-Agnostic Patch-wise Tunable-multibeamformer), that employs a depth-wise patching strategy for computational efficiency and depth-independent learning. In order to develop a beamformer agnostic framework, the proposed approach first trains identical neural networks separately to derive the individual beamforming algorithm model weights, which are then fused via a tunable weighted averaging mechanism. This provides clinicians with dynamic and adaptable diagnostic perspectives, blending the acceptability of delay and sum (DAS) beamformer with the contrast of filtered delay multiply and sum (FDMAS) beamformer and the resolution of minimum variance (MV) beamformer simultaneously at very low complexity. ADAPT achieves 73 % speedup in training, 94 % reduction in computations and 94 % reduction in activation memory over a model trained over full depth.

title: Deep Learning Based Landmarks Detection for Positioning Assessment in Mammography.
abstract: Proper breast positioning is critical for reliable mammographic screening, yet remains a major source of diagnostic variability and exam failure. This study proposes an interpretable, landmark-based framework for the automated evaluation of the Adequate amount of pectoral muscle criterion in mediolateral oblique mammograms. Our approach combines a DeepLabv3+ model for pectoral muscle segmentation with a Gaussian U-Net for nipple localization, followed by a geometric decision algorithm assessing positioning adequacy from the relative locations of the predicted landmarks. The method was trained and evaluated on 2274 annotated MLO images derived from a multicenter audit, with a test subset independently labeled by three expert radiographers to account for inter-rater variability. The proposed system achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.88 (specificity of 0.92, sensitivity of 0.84), outperforming both classification-based CNN baselines and previous landmark detection models. Mean localization errors were within expert variability ($1.5-3.0 ~\text{mm}$for pectoral landmarks, 2.0 mm for nipple). These results highlight that anatomically grounded, explainable models can deliver robust and clinically meaningful positioning assessments even in imbalanced and subjective datasets.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: SA-UNetv2: Rethinking Spatial Attention U-Net for Retinal Vessel Segmentation.
abstract: Retinal vessel segmentation is a crucial yet challenging task for early diagnosis of diseases such as diabetes and hypertension. SA-UNet achieves promising performance by introducing spatial attention in the bottleneck, but it underuses attention in skip connections and fails to address the severe foreground-background imbalance. We propose SA-UNetv2, a lightweight model that injects cross-scale spatial attention into all skip connections to strengthen multi-scale feature fusion and adopts a weighted Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE) + Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) loss to improve robustness to class imbalance. On the public DRIVE and STARE datasets, SA-UNetv2 achieves state-of-the-art performance with only$\mathbf{1. 2 M B}$memory and$\mathbf{0. 2 6 M}$parameters (less than 50% of SA-UNet), and$\mathbf{1}$second CPU inference on$592 \times 592 \times 3$images, demonstrating strong efficiency and deployability in resource-constrained, CPU-only settings. The code is available at github.com/clguo/SA-UNetv2.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Follow Your Heart: Landmark-Guided Transducer Pose Scoring for Point-of-Care Echocardiography.
abstract: Point-of-care transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) makes it possible to assess a patient's cardiac function in almost any setting. A critical step in the TTE exam is acquisition of the apical 4-chamber (A4CH) view, which is used to evaluate clinically impactful measurements such as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). However, optimizing transducer pose for high-quality image acquisition and subsequent measurement is a challenging task, particularly for novice users. In this work, we present a multi-task network that provides feedback cues for A4CH view acquisition and automatically estimates LVEF in high-quality A4CH images. The network cascades a transducer pose scoring module and an uncertainty-aware LV landmark detector with automated LVEF estimation. A strength is that network training and inference do not require cumbersome or costly setups for transducer position tracking. We evaluate performance on point-of-care TTE data acquired with a spatially dense “sweep” protocol around the optimal A4CH view. The results demonstrate the network's ability to determine when the transducer pose is on target, close to target, or far from target based on the images alone, while generating visual landmark cues that guide anatomical interpretation and orientation. In conclusion, we demonstrate a promising strategy to provide guidance for A 4 CH view acquisition, which may be useful when deploying point-of-care TTE in limited resource settings.

title: Cross-Domain Vessel Segmentation via Latent Similarity Mining and Iterative Co-Optimization.
abstract: Retinal vessel segmentation serves as a critical prerequisite for automated diagnosis of retinal pathologies. While recent advances in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have demonstrated promising performance in this task, significant performance degradation occurs when domain shifts exist between training and testing data. To address these limitations, we propose a novel domain transfer framework that leverages latent vascular similarity across domains and iterative co-optimization of generation and segmentation networks. Specifically, we first pre-train generation networks for source and target domains. Subsequently, the pretrained sourcedomain conditional diffusion model performs deterministic inversion to establish intermediate latent representations of vascular images, creating domain-agnostic prototypes for target synthesis. Finally, we develop an iterative refinement strategy where segmentation network and generative model undergo mutual optimization through cyclic parameter updating. This co-evolution process enables simultaneous enhancement of cross-domain image synthesis quality and segmentation accuracy. Experiments demonstrate that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in crossdomain retinal vessel segmentation, particularly in challenging clinical scenarios with significant modality discrepancies.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

verified_metadata.conference_title: 2026 IEEE 23rd International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
verified_metadata.abstract: Acquiring high-quality synthetic computed tomography (sCT) images from cone-beam CT is crucial for accurate dose calculation in the field of adaptive radiotherapy. However, existing sCT generation methods based on diffusion models often struggle to preserve anatomical structures, especially when the anatomical structure of the input CBCT and ground-truth CT differs in shape. To address this, we propose a Hierarchical Anatomical-Guided Diffusion (HAGD) framework that captures both global semantic information and local textural details for anatomical-aware sCT generation. We first introduce a dual-branch encoder to simultaneously extract features from coarse structural masks and fine segmentation maps. Secondly, a hierarchical fusion module is proposed to integrate these multiscale features into the conditional diffusion model, using concatenation or attention-gated fusion. Experiments on the SynthRAD2023 dataset show that HAGD achieves superior performance, with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 56.51 for concatenation fusion and 54.62 for attention-gated fusion improves performance over existing image translation models. These results highlight the effectiveness of structured anatomical guidance in enhancing fidelity and structural consistency of sCT images, thus supporting accurate and robust image translation in clinical radiotherapy workflows.

title: A Dual-View U-Net Framework for Carotid Ultra-Sound Plaque Segmentation and Vulnerability Classification.
abstract: Automated analysis of carotid ultrasound is important for stroke risk assessment, yet remains challenging due to speckle noise, low plaque contrast, limited annotations, and high inter-observer variability. This paper presents a compact dualview U-Net framework for joint carotid plaque segmentation and binary vulnerability classification in the ISBI 2026 Carotid Plaque Segmentation and Vulnerability Assessment in UltraSound (CSV 2026) challenge. The method jointly processes paired longitudinal and transverse ultrasound views using a shared ResNet-34 encoder, lightweight cross-view feature interaction, and two view-specific decoders with attention-gated skip connections. An auxiliary case-level classification branch regularizes the shared representation during training. Using only 200 labeled cases, our submission achieves a total leaderboard score of 58.87 on the released validation phase, outperforming the released baseline score of 50.92, while also improving runtime from 308.90 s to 160.98 s for 200 cases. Detailed validation metrics of the final model show plaque Dice around 0.65, vessel Dice around 0.90, and a classification F1-score of 0.58. These results indicate that a compact fully supervised dual-view design can provide a practical balance between segmentation quality, vulnerability assessment, and inference efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Unsupervised Ultrasound Image Denoising with Monte Carlo Risk Estimation.
abstract: Speckle noise is a fundamental artifact in ultrasound imaging that severely degrades spatial resolution and contrast, affecting both manual and automated diagnostic tasks. While deep learning methods have shown great promise for image denoising, their application to ultrasound is critically constrained by the absence of noise-free images for supervised training. To overcome this limitation, we introduce MC-MURE, a novel framework for training any deep neural network for ultrasound image despeckling using only noisy scan data. Our approach is centered on a computationally efficient Monte Carlo (MC) method to approximate a modified Multiplicative Unbiased Risk Estimation (MURE) loss function. This enables robust, end-to-end training without access to ground-truth images, thus breaking the dependency on noise-free images for supervision. We validate our framework on synthetically corrupted breast ultrasound data, using three common despeckling network architectures. Quantitative evaluation demonstrates that models trained with our unsupervised MC-MURE framework achieve performance remarkably close to their fully supervised Oracle counterparts trained with clean ground truth on both image fidelity metrics and downstream segmentation accuracy.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Assessing AI Polyp Detection Delay Using Tracklets.
abstract: This study introduces a tracklet-based approach for estimating the polyp detection delay for a colon CADe system as part of overall standalone performance testing. We propose using detection delay as a benchmarking metric that is agnostic to processing time and dataset modifications. Our study addresses how polyps frequently come in and out of frame, creating distinct tracklets, and examines the impact this behavior can have on detection delay calculations. Lastly, we introduce detection delay curves to compare model performance over a range of sensitivities and use detection window curves to measure how sensitivity improves the longer a model observes a polyp.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Domain-Expert-Guided Hybrid Mixture-of-Experts for Medical AI: Integrating Data-Driven Learning With Clinical Priors.
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models increase representational capacity with modest computational cost, but their effectiveness in specialized domains such as medicine is limited by small datasets. In contrast, clinical practice offers rich expert knowledge, such as physician gaze patterns and diagnostic heuristics, that models cannot reliably learn from limited data. Combining data-driven experts, which capture novel patterns, with domain-expert-guided experts, which encode accumulated clinical insights, provides complementary strengths for robust and clinically meaningful learning. To this end, we propose Domain-Knowledge-Guided Hybrid MoE (DKGHMoE), a plug-and-play and interpretable module that unifies data-driven learning with domain expertise. DKGH-MoE integrates a data-driven MoE to extract novel features from raw imaging data, and a domain-expert-guided MoE incorporates clinical priors, specifically clinician eye-gaze cues, to emphasize regions of high diagnostic relevance. By integrating domain expert insights with data-driven features, DKGH-MoE improves both performance and interpretability. (Code: https://github.com/BrainX-Lab/Domain-Expert-Guided-Hybrid-MoE)
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Multimodal Optical Imaging Platform for Quantitative Burn Assessment.
abstract: Accurate assessment of burn severity at injury onset remains a major clinical challenge due to the lack of objective methods for detecting subsurface tissue damage. This limitation is critical in battlefield and mass-casualty settings, where rapid and reliable evaluation of burn depth is essential for triage and surgical decision-making. We present a multimodal optical imaging framework that establishes the foundation for a compact, low-size, weight, and power (low-SWaP) field-deployable device for quantitative burn assessment. The system integrates broadband hyperspectral imaging (VSWIR,$400-2100 ~\text{nm}$) with laser speckle contrast imaging to jointly evaluate biochemical composition and microvascular perfusion. Using short-wave infrared (SWIR,$>1000 ~\text{nm}$) wavelengths, we developed and validated novel deep-tissue parameters linked to water, lipid, and collagen absorption features that enhance burn-tissue separability and burn severity classification. We implemented and validated unsupervised learning methods for spectral feature extraction, band down-selection, and clustering against histology, establishing a foundation for a rugged, data-driven device for early quantitative burn evaluation in austere environments.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: All-Subtype Cataract Classification and Grading in AS-OCT via a Unified Multi-Task Framework.
abstract: Automated cataract grading based on Anterior Segment Optical Coherence Tomography (AS-OCT) plays a key role in objective diagnosis. However, current approaches are restricted to single-subtype analysis, limiting their clinical applicability. We propose a unified multitask framework that concurrently performs lens subregion segmentation and severity grading for cortical, nuclear, and posterior subcapsular cataracts. The framework integrates three modules: an Implicit Boundary Rendering (IBR) module for sub-pixel boundary refinement, a Laplacian Feature Masking (LFM) module for subregion-specific feature separation, and a Multi-Granularity Experts Fusion (MGEF) module for adaptive feature integration. Experiments on 2,088 AS-OCT images demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving IoU by up to 4 % and grading accuracy by 3-10 % compared with existing models. This study presents the first unified framework capable of simultaneous segmentation and grading of all cataract subtypes, advancing automated ophthalmic diagnosis toward clinical application.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: SplineSplat: 3D Ray Tracing for Higher-Quality Tomography.
abstract: We propose a method to efficiently compute tomographic projections of a 3D volume represented by a linear combination of shifted B-splines. To do so, we propose a ray-tracing algorithm that computes 3D line integrals with arbitrary projection geometries. One of the components of our algorithm is a neural network that computes the contribution of the basis functions efficiently. In our experiments, we consider well-posed cases where the data are sufficient for accurate reconstruction without the need for regularization. We achieve higher reconstruction quality than traditional voxel-based methods.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Ranking-Guided Semi-Supervised Domain Adaptation for Severity Classification.
abstract: Semi-supervised domain adaptation leverages a few labeled and many unlabeled target samples, making it promising for addressing domain shifts in medical image analysis. However, existing methods struggle with severity classification due to unclear class boundaries. Severity classification involves naturally ordered class labels, complicating adaptation. We propose a novel method that aligns source and target domains using rank scores learned via ranking with class order. Specifically, Cross-Domain Ranking ranks sample pairs across domains, while Continuous Distribution Alignment aligns rank score distributions. Experiments on ulcerative colitis and diabetic retinopathy classification validate the effectiveness of our approach, demonstrating successful alignment of class-specific rank score distributions.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: A Dirichlet Distribution-Based Trust-Adaptive Ensemble Approach for Pneumonia Classification from Chest X-Ray Images.
abstract: Pneumonia diagnosis from chest radiographs is hindered by AI model variability and limited decision transparency. We present a deployment-ready, abstaining Dirichlet-evidence ensemble for paediatric CXR triage that elevates “Indeterminate” to a first-class outcome and implements dynamic, trust-adaptive weighting. Eight diverse pre-trained models each provide binary predictions, which are converted to three-way CXR supports, scaled by ongoing trust scores, and fused using a Dirichlet-evidence mechanism. Selective gates on class separation and pooled evidence allow the ensemble to defer, with auditable reasoning, when the decision is uncertain. On a 200-image paediatric hold-out, simple majority voting achieved 94.5% accuracy but dropped to 83.0% when two training models were intentionally inverted. At a fixed operating point, the proposed ensemble maintained zero errors (100% accuracy) on decided cases in both settings, abstaining on only 1-2% of studies instead of issuing incorrect labels. Unlike prior work, our system tightly integrates uncertainty, selective prediction, and per-case logging for clinical governance. This framework advances safe, interpretable automation for paediatric pneumonia assessment.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Uncertainty Analysis in Intravascular Oct Segmentation.
authors: Ruben G. A. van der Waerden
abstract: Integrating uncertainty quantification (UQ) into optical coherence tomography (OCT) segmentation could enhance model reliability and clinical interpretability. Using an ensemble-based model, we estimated pixelwise entropy as a measure of uncertainty and compared it to segmentation accuracy and inter-observer variability. Higher entropy was associated with lower accuracy: uncertain predictions had lower Dice scores and larger measurement errors, particularly in complex structures. Regions of annotator disagreement coincided with elevated model uncertainty. Entropy-based UQ thus provides an interpretable confidence measure, supporting selective human review and more trustworthy AI-assisted OCT analysis.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: REAF: a Region-Enhanced Volume-Slice Hierarchical Attention Fusion Vision-Language Model for CT-Report Retrieval.
abstract: Cross-modal retrieval between 3D medical images and radiological reports is crucial for clinical decision support. However, existing Vision-Language Models (VLMs) struggle to adequately represent complex volumetric data, failing to capture complementary global and local features simultaneously. Moreover, they often lack mechanisms to weigh clinically salient features across these distinct granularities adaptively. To alleviate these limitations, we propose a Region-Enhanced volume-slice hierarchical Attention Fusion (REAF) method that includes two core modules: (1) Layer-wise Hierarchical Attention Fusion (LHAF), which effectively extracts and fuses data features across the volume-level (global) and slice-level (local) hierarchy, and (2) the 3D Regional Saliency Enhancer (3D-RSE), which ensures the fusion process is content-aware by dynamically concentrating on the most informative regions at each level. This dual-module approach generates more focused visual representations that are better aligned with radiology reports. Trained end-to-end on the CT-RATE dataset, REAF outperforms previous methods on image-text retrieval, with improvements of 5.15 percentage points (p.p.) and 7.32 p.p. in Recall@50 (R@50) and Recall@100 (R@100) for report-to-volume retrieval, and 4.61 p.p. and 7.05 p.p. in R@50 and$\mathrm{R} @ 100$for volume-to-report retrieval. The code is available at https://github.com/HiLab-git/REAF.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

To alleviate these limitations, we propose a Region-Enhanced volume-slice hierarchical Attention Fusion (REAF) method that includes two core modules: (1) Layer-wise Hierarchical Attention Fusion (LHAF), which effectively extracts and fuses data features across the volume-level (global) and slice-level (local) hierarchy, and (2) the 3D Regional Saliency Enhancer (3D-RSE), which ensures the fusion process is content-aware by dynamically concentrating on the most informative regions at each level. This dual-module approach generates more focused visual representations that are better aligned with radiology reports. Trained end-to-end on the CT-RATE dataset, REAF outperforms previous methods on image-text retrieval, with improvements of 5.15 percentage points (p.p.) and 7.32 p.p. in Recall@50 (R@50) and Recall@100 (R@100) for report-to-volume retrieval, and 4.61 p.p. and 7.05 p.p. in R@50 and$\mathrm{R} @ 100$for volume-to-report retrieval. The code is available at https://github.com/HiLab-git/REAF.

title: Unpaired Semantic-Preserving Virtual Perls Generation via Conditional Generative Models.
abstract: Virtual staining has emerged as a promising approach to reduce laboratory workload and enhance digital hematopathology workflows. However, stain-to-stain translation in hematology remains largely unexplored, mainly due to the absence of paired data. In this study, we propose a modified CycleGAN framework to virtually generate Perls-stained images from morphologically stained bone marrow smears. The model introduces a class-conditioned pairing strategy and a classification consistency loss guided by an external DenseNet-based sideroblast classifier to preserve diagnostic semantics. Trained on 12,738 unpaired cell images from 44 patients, the proposed approach achieved substantial improvements in both label preservation and image realism. Results highlight the potential of virtual Perls generation to complement morphological analysis and pave the way toward multimodal generative models for comprehensive hematological characterization.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: PIVM: Diffusion-Based Prior-Integrated Variation Modeling for Anatomically Precise Abdominal CT Synthesis.
abstract: Abdominal CT data are limited by high annotation costs and privacy constraints, which hinder the development of robust segmentation and diagnostic models. We present a Prior-Integrated Variation Modeling (PIVM) framework, a diffusion-based method for anatomically accurate CT image synthesis. Instead of generating full images from noise, PIVM predicts voxel-wise intensity variations relative to organ-specific intensity priors derived from segmentation labels. These priors and labels jointly guide the diffusion process, ensuring spatial alignment and realistic organ boundaries. Unlike latent-space diffusion models, our approach operates directly in image space while preserving the full Hounsfield Unit (HU) range, capturing fine anatomical textures without smoothing.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Dihedral-Invariant LBP Co-Occurrence for Cellular Texture Analysis.
abstract: Co-occurring Local Binary Patterns (LBPs) capture spatial relationships between adjacent intensity transitions and are effective for texture-based biomedical image analysis. Existing rotation-invariant formulations, such as RIC-LBP, still treat mirror-reflected configurations as distinct, introducing redundant orientation variability. We analyze how the cyclic group$C_{2}$and dihedral group$D_{2}$partition the 256 adjacent 4-bit LBP pairs, identifying the cases where reflection merges rotation-generated bins. We propose a compact reflectionand rotation-invariant descriptor (RRIC-LBP) based on$D_{2}$orbits, reducing the histogram dimensionality from 136 to 88. Evaluations on fluorescence microscopy of mitochondrial networks show statistically equivalent classification performance, demonstrating that the reduced representation maintains discriminative power.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: LOCBAM: Advancing 3D Patch-Based Image Segmentation by Integrating Location Context.
abstract: Patch-based methods are widely used in 3D medical image segmentation to address memory constraints in processing highresolution volumetric data. However, these approaches often neglect the patch's location within the global volume, which can limit segmentation performance when anatomical context is important. In this paper, we investigate the role of location context in patch-based 3D segmentation and propose a novel attention mechanism, LocBAM, that explicitly processes spatial information. Experiments on BTCV, AMOS22, and KiTS23 demonstrate that incorporating location context stabilizes training and improves segmentation performance, particularly under low patch-to-volume coverage where global context is missing. Furthermore, LocBAM consistently outperforms classical coordinate encoding via CoordConv. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/compai-lab/2026-ISBI-hooft.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Learnable Descent Algorithm for Cardiac Transmembrane Potential Imaging.
abstract: Myocardial transmembrane potential (TMP) offers greater clinical value than body surface potential (BSP) or heart-surface reconstructions. In this work, we propose a TMP reconstruction method based on a convergent learned descent-type algorithm (LDA) and its induced deep neural network. Specifically, we propose a variational model where the data fidelity term links BSP measurements to the TMP via a heart-torso geometric matrix. The regularization term combines an$L_{2,1}$norm to enhance sparsity with a feature extractor parameterized as a deep convolutional neural network. We applied the LDA, which leverages Nesterov's smoothing technique, the idea of residual learning, and an iteration selection policy as the safeguard for convergence, to solve the proposed non-smooth non-convex minimization model. We generate a neural network whose architecture follows the algorithm. This network inherits the convergence property of the algorithm and is highly interpretable and parameter efficient. Experiments on simulated data demonstrate our method's superior accuracy and robustness over traditional approaches.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: 3D Lung Reconstruction from X-Rays: Implicit Single-View Occupancy Vs. Explicit Voxel-Based Biplanar Methods.
abstract: Deep learning has enabled 3D anatomical reconstruction from 2D radiographs through two main paradigms: image-to-segmentation and image-to-mesh methods. Yet, their relative performance remains poorly understood for the same anatomy. This study compares KVNet, a biplanar segmentation-based network, with the occupancybased model X2V, the state-of-the-art single-view implicit image-to-mesh model for lung reconstruction, on the same dataset of 646 cases. KV-Net achieves higher volumetric and surface accuracy, while X2V produces plausible global shapes with lower computational costs. Beyond whole-organ metrics, a regional analysis highlights distinct challenges across lung zones: occupancy-based models struggle to capture thin lower regions, whereas segmentation networks achieve a twofold reduction in average surface error across all regions. These results provide the first region-aware comparison between image-to-segmentation and image-to-mesh approaches for 3D lung reconstruction from X-rays.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: High-Fidelity 3D CT Super-Resolution on Real-Paired Datasets with Adaptive Interpolation and Feature Consistency.
abstract: High-resolution thin-slice Computed Tomography (CT) imaging is critical for accurate diagnosis, yet clinical scans are often acquired with thick slices to reduce radiation dose and scanning time. This leads to anisotropic volumes that obscure fine anatomical details and hinder 3D analysis. While deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) methods have made progress in reconstructing high-resolution volumes from thick-slice inputs, they remain limited by challenges in slice generation, feature enhancement, and structural refinement. In this work, we present a unified framework that systematically addresses these three aspects. An adaptive slice interpolation module enables content-driven and positionaware generation of intermediate features for anatomically consistent upsampling. A frequency-enhanced throughplane attention block enriches multi-view representations by integrating spatial and frequency cues. Furthermore, an EMA-based feature consistency strategy refines latent representations to ensure structural coherence and perceptual fidelity. Experiments on real paired CT datasets demonstrate that our method achieves superior quantitative accuracy and visual realism compared to state-of-the-art approaches. Code available at: https://github.com/bigcl/AIFC-SR
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Introducing Curvature Trajectory Information into Boundary Corner Point Distribution to Guide Colorectal Polyp Segmentation.
abstract: Achieving accurate segmentation of polyps remains a challenging task due to various uncertainties regarding polyp boundaries. To enhance the perception of boundary details, this paper introduces a boundary corner point distribution mapping method called CDCT, which incorporates curvature trajectory structure information. Our method transforms the boundary ground truth into a discrete corner point distribution and supplements the trajectory distribution of the corner points along the boundary curve to provide essential boundary curvature information. Consequently, we propose a straightforward boundary-guided network named BCTNet to guide polyp segmentation. Experiments conducted on multiple datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of CDCT method and BCTNet model.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Abdominal Cone-Beam CT Visual Quality Enhancement Using 2.5D Conditional Diffusion Model.
abstract: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is crucial for accurate patient positioning in image-guided radiotherapy. However, CBCT is often compromised by scatter, beam hardening, and limited projection angles, which result in increased noise and degraded image quality. These limitations hinder its application in quantitative clinical tasks such as dose calculation, organ delineation, and radiomics analysis. In this study, we propose a learning-based method for enhancing the visual quality of CBCT images using a 2.5 D conditional diffusion model. By leveraging adjacent slices of the CBCT as a condition, the model can learn structural consistency and provide restored images that suppress noise and artifacts through the reverse diffusion process. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior image quality compared to existing 2D diffusion approaches, validating its clinical applicability for adaptive radiation therapy.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Penalty-Based Multi-Objective Optimization for Robust Data Splitting to Improve Consistency in Deep Learning Models.
abstract: The performance of deep learning models is dependent on the balanced partitioning of datasets into training, validation, and test sets, especially in preclinical longitudinal studies, where repeated scans, heterogeneous tumor types, imbalanced tumor sizes, and uneven sample counts can bias model evaluation. Random splitting often produces unbalanced splitting sets, contributes to data leakage, and results in reduced generalizability, potentially leading to inconsistent model performance. We present a penalty-based multi-objective optimization (MOO) framework that generates splits of data that are well-balanced, thereby contributing to the high consistency and generalizability of the model. Using a pancreatic tumor ultrasound dataset, we demonstrate that MOO splits effectively eliminate significant class, size, and unique mouse distribution imbalances compared to random splits. We then show that, although the mean Dice score was similar in both splits, the variance in the scores was significantly lower in the MOO splits.

verified_metadata.title: Penalty-Based Multi-Objective Optimization for Robust Data Splitting to Improve Consistency in Deep Learning Models
verified_metadata.conference_title: 2026 IEEE 23rd International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
verified_metadata.abstract: The performance of deep learning models is dependent on the balanced partitioning of datasets into training, validation, and test sets, especially in preclinical longitudinal studies, where repeated scans, heterogeneous tumor types, imbalanced tumor sizes, and uneven sample counts can bias model evaluation. Random splitting often produces unbalanced splitting sets, contributes to data leakage, and results in reduced generalizability, potentially leading to inconsistent model performance. We present a penalty-based multi-objective optimization (MOO) framework that generates splits of data that are well-balanced, thereby contributing to the high consistency and generalizability of the model. Using a pancreatic tumor ultrasound dataset, we demonstrate that MOO splits effectively eliminate significant class, size, and unique mouse distribution imbalances compared to random splits. We then show that, although the mean Dice score was similar in both splits, the variance in the scores was significantly lower in the MOO splits.

title: A Unified Transformer Architecture for 3D MSI-H&E Fusion.
abstract: Mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) enables unlabeled, untargeted mapping of biomolecular distributions in tissue but is limited by low spatial resolution and high data complexity. We address these challenges with a generative model for MSI peak learning that produces compact, chemically meaningful embeddings, and a transformer-based framework for multimodal fusion of low-resolution MSI with high-resolution H&E microscopy across serial sections. The model tokenizes MSI and H&E patches and employs deformable cross-attention to transfer histological structure while preserving MSI chemistry, yielding slice-consistent high-resolution 3D reconstructions. Experiments on 3D DESI Orbitrap MSI/H&E data from human colorectal adenocarcinoma demonstrate anatomically accurate and chemically faithful reconstruction without manual intervention. Code is available at https://github.com/H-deep/TransUniFERE-3D.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

verified_metadata.conference_title: 2026 IEEE 23rd International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
verified_metadata.abstract:
Fairness in medical artificial intelligence (AI) tools is essential, as biased model behaviour can lead to unequal diagnostic outcomes and raise serious ethical concerns, ultimately reducing clinical trust. Although Vision Language Models (VLMs) show strong performance in medical imaging, they still exhibit demographic biases, particularly across gender, race, and other sensitive attributes.
Addressing these disparities is difficult due to the utility-fairness trade off, where improving equity often reduces diagnostic accuracy. To overcome these challenges, we propose the Max Deviation Penalty, a lightweight regularization objective that integrates seamlessly into parameter efficient finetuning schemes.
Experiments across diverse medical and general domain benchmarks demonstrate that our method consistently achieves state of the art performance in balancing fairness and utility, surpassing existing baselines enabling fair, reliable VLM adaptation.

title: CephRes-MHNet: A Multi-Head Residual Network for Accurate and Robust Cephalometric Landmark Detection.
abstract: Accurate localization of cephalometric landmarks from 2D lateral skull X-rays is vital for orthodontic diagnosis and treatment. Manual annotation is time-consuming and error-prone, whereas automated approaches often struggle with low contrast and anatomical complexity. This paper introduces CephRes-MHNet, a multi-head residual convolutional network for robust and efficient cephalometric landmark detection. The architecture integrates residual encoding, dual-attention mechanisms, and multi-head decoders to enhance contextual reasoning and anatomical precision. Trained on the Aariz Cephalometric dataset of 1,000 radiographs, CephResMHNet achieved a mean radial error (MRE) of 1.23 mm and a success detection rate (SDR) @ 2.0 mm of 85.5 %, outperforming all evaluated models. In particular, it exceeded the strongest baseline, the attention-driven AFPF-Net (MRE$=1.25 ~\text{mm}$, SDR @$2.0 ~\text{mm}= 84.1 \%$), while using less than 25 % of its parameters. These results demonstrate that CephRes-MHNet attains state-of-the-art accuracy through architectural efficiency, providing a practical solution for real-world orthodontic analysis.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Swin-DDPM: A Transformer-Enhanced Diffusion Model for Multi-Organ Low Dose CT Denoising.
abstract: Minimizing radiation exposure in computed tomography (CT) is essential, yet dose reduction often introduces severe noise and structural degradation. We propose Swin-DDPM, a transformer-enhanced diffusion framework for efficient and high-quality denoising of low-dose CT (LDCT) scans across multiple anatomical regions. The model embeds a hierarchical Swin Transformer within an accelerated denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM) paradigm, enabling ten-step training and inference while preserving fine anatomical details. A task-specific noise scheduler adapts the diffusion process to organ-dependent noise patterns, enhancing generalization across chest, abdominal, and cranial datasets. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Swin-DDPM outperforms CNN, GAN, and prior diffusion-based methods in both quantitative and visual metrics, achieving over$100 \times$faster inference. The framework provides a scalable foundation for next-generation LDCT reconstruction and clinically reliable image restoration.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Curriculum-Guided Myocardial Scar Segmentation for Ischemic and Non-Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
abstract: Identification and quantification of myocardial scar is important for diagnosis and prognosis of cardiovascular diseases. However, reliable scar segmentation from Late Gadolinium Enhancement Cardiac Magnetic Resonance (LGE-CMR) images remains a challenge due to variations in contrast enhancement across patients, suboptimal imaging conditions such as post-contrast washout, and inconsistencies in ground-truth annotations on diffuse scars caused by inter-observer variability. In this work, we propose a curriculum learning-based framework designed to improve segmentation performance under these challenging conditions. The method introduces a progressive training strategy that guides the model from high-confidence, clearly defined scar regions to low-confidence or visually ambiguous samples with limited scar burden. By structuring the learning process in this manner, the network develops robustness to uncertain labels and subtle scar appearances that are often underrepresented in conventional training pipelines. Experimental results show that the proposed approach enhances segmentation accuracy and consistency, particularly for cases with minimal or diffuse scar, outperforming standard training baselines. This strategy provides a principled way to leverage imperfect data for improved myocardial scar quantification in clinical applications. Our code is publicly available on Github.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Conditional Diffusion Model Optimization for Real-Time Point-of-Care Image-Quality Enhancement on Nvidia Jetson Orin Nano.
abstract: High-resolution optical coherence tomography (OCT) is often inaccessible in low-resource settings. While diffusion models can enhance low-cost OCT scans, their computational cost prohibits embedded deployment. We solve this problem by presenting the first real-time deployment of a diffusion-based OCT enhancement model on an Nvidia Jetson Orin Nano. Our systematic pipeline achieves a 33 ms inference time by first pruning the model from 224 M (million) to 42.9 M parameters (80.8% reduction) with minimal fidelity loss (no statistically significant difference in quality ($p>0.3$) ). We then apply a novel hybrid INT8 quantization approach, strategically offloading unstable Softmax operations to a lightweight custom CUDA kernel. Expert evaluation shows that downstream diagnostic utility of the resulting images is also not impacted. This work provides a concrete blueprint for translating large generative models into practical, affordable medical diagnostic tools.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Shape-Guided Self-Supervised Learning for Intracranial Aneurysm Segmentation.
abstract: Intracranial aneurysm (IA) is a localized dilation of a cerebral artery that can rupture and cause life-threatening subarachnoid hemorrhage. Accurate segmentation of aneurysms is essential for quantitative morphological assessment and clinical decision-making. IA segmentation remains challenging due to class imbalance, scarce annotations, and high shape variability. Traditional shape-based methods lack shape adaptability, while deep learning approaches often ignore explicit shape priors and are limited by small datasets. To address these issues, we propose a clinically inspired, shape-guided self-supervised learning framework that uses a synthetic deformation engine to generate pseudoaneurysmal geometries, enabling robust learning of aneurysm shape representations without dense labels. Experiments show consistent performance gains (up to +3.0% in aneurysm IoU) across multiple point-based architectures, demonstrating the generality and effectiveness of the proposed approach. https://github.com/moyamung/SG-SSL
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
