title: Rethinking Glaucoma Calibration: Voting-Based Binocular and Metadata Integration.
abstract: Glaucoma is a major cause of irreversible blindness, with significant diagnostic subjectivity. This inherent uncertainty, combined with the overconfidence of models optimized solely for accuracy can lead to fatal issues such as overdiagnosis or missing critical diseases. To ensure clinical trust, model calibration is essential for reliable predictions, yet study in this field remains limited. Existing calibration study have overlooked glaucoma's systemic associations and high diagnostic subjectivity. To overcome these limitations, we propose VViT (Voting-based ViT), a framework that enhances calibration by integrating a patient's binocular information and metadata. Furthermore, to mitigate diagnostic subjectivity, V-ViT utilizes an iterative dropout-based Voting System to maximize calibration performance. The proposed framework achieved state-of-the-art performance across all metrics, including the primary calibration metrics. Our results demonstrate that V-ViT effectively resolves the issue of overconfidence in predictions in glaucoma diagnosis, providing highly reliable predictions for clinical use. Our source code is available at https://github.com/starforTJ/V-ViT.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Transfer Learning from Imagenet for Meg-Based Decoding of Imagined Speech.
abstract: Non-invasive decoding of imagined speech remains challenging due to weak, distributed signals and limited labeled data. Our paper introduces an image-based approach that transforms magnetoencephalography (MEG) signals into time-frequency representations compatible with pretrained vision models. MEG data from 21 participants performing imagined speech tasks were projected into three spatial scalogram mixtures via a learnable sensor-space convolution, producing compact image-like inputs for ImageNetpretrained vision architectures. These models outperformed classical and non-pretrained models, achieving up to 90.4 % balanced accuracy for imagery vs. silence, 81.0 % vs. silent reading, and 60.6 % for vowel decoding. Cross-subject evaluation confirmed that pretrained models capture shared neural representations, and temporal analyses localized discriminative information to imagery-locked intervals. These findings show that pretrained vision models applied to image-based MEG representations can effectively capture the structure of imagined speech in non-invasive neural signals.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Resmscam-FFT Net: Residual Multi-Scale Channel Attention Module with Fast Fourier Transform Network for Cardiac Segmentation.
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global mortality, underscoring the critical need for accurate and timely diagnosis. Echocardiography has been established as the primary non-invasive diagnostic tool, but its reliance on operator expertise leads to significant variability and limits access to timely care. To address these challenges, we introduce ResMSCAM-FFT Net, a deep learning model for precise semantic segmentations and measurements of cardiac chambers in 2D echocardiogram videos. Rooted in the U-Net structure, ResMSCAM-FFT Net incorporates Pyramid Vision Transformer v2 (PVT v2) encoder for efficient multi-scale feature extraction, Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) Block to enforce global topological consistency and mitigate ultrasound artifacts, and Residual Multi-Scale Convolutional Attention Module (ResMSCAM) for content-aware local boundary refinement. Compared with other deep learning-based models, our proposed network achieves state-of-the-art performance in generating robust and highly accurate segmentation masks for automated cardiac function assessment.

verified_metadata.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global mortality, underscoring the critical need for accurate and timely diagnosis. Echocardiography has been established as the primary non-invasive diagnostic tool, but its reliance on operator expertise leads to significant variability and limits access to timely care. To address these challenges, we introduce ResMSCAM-FFT Net, a deep learning model for precise semantic segmentations and measurements of cardiac chambers in 2D echocardiogram videos. Rooted in the U-Net structure, ResMSCAM-FFT Net incorporates Pyramid Vision Transformer v2 (PVT v2) encoder for efficient multi-scale feature extraction, Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) Block to enforce global topological consistency and mitigate ultrasound artifacts, and Residual Multi-Scale Convolutional Attention Module (ResMSCAM) for content-aware local boundary refinement. Compared with other deep learning-based models, our proposed network achieves state-of-the-art performance in generating robust and highly accurate segmentation masks for automated cardiac function assessment.

title: Unsupervised X-Ray-to-DRR Translation with Structural Enhancement for Efficient X-Ray-to-CT Registration.
abstract: Artifacts and geometric distortions arising from modality differences are major sources of mismatch between conventional CT-based digitally reconstructed radiographs (DRRs) and real X-ray images. We propose an unsupervised crossmodal image translation framework that maps X-ray images to DRRs, enhancing structural features in the frequency domain while constraining geometric deformations in the spatial domain. Specifically, an edge-based spatial branch is introduced to guide the generator with richer structural information, while a Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT)-based frequency enhancement module separates high-frequency details from low-frequency components to better preserve anatomical structures and improve cross-domain translation. Experiments on a public cadaveric pelvis dataset demonstrate state-of-the-art translation performance across multiple metrics. Moreover, when integrated into several advanced 2D-3D registration pipelines, the proposed method substantially improves registration accuracy and sub-millimeter success rates. The code is available at https://github.com/pj-jiang/unsupervised-x-ray-to-drr-images-translation.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Learnable Hierarchical Visual Contexts for Tumor Segmentation in Computed Tomography Images.
abstract: Despite advances in deep learning (DL), automated tumor segmentation on computed tomography (CT) scans remains challenging for radiotherapy applications due to due to large variability in tumor shapes, appearance, and diffuse boundaries. We present LeVal-learnable visual query contexts that refines attention towards tumor-relevant regions for improved segmentation. LeVal combines task-agnostic learnable tokens called semantic contexts with task-specific query tokens. Semantic contexts cross attend to multi-scale features of a 3D Swin transformer encoder, which are jointly subject to 2-stage pretraining: (a) self-supervised learning (SSL) using 14,000 unlabeled CTs and (b), supervised pretraining for multi-organ segmentation use pseudo-contours generated by bespoke methods. Task queries are refined through cross-attention with semantic contexts, which then modulate the decoder output to generate segmentation. LeVal was evaluated across four public datasets involving pancreas, colon, adrenal, and head-and-neck cancers. It consistently outperformed existing methods. Leval also demonstrated stronger embedding separation between tumor and surrounding healthy tissues, indicating better discriminability. Code and model checkpoints will be made available through GitHub upon manuscript acceptance.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: LUMEN: Longitudinal Multi-Modal Radiology Model for Prognosis and Diagnosis.
abstract: Large vision-language models (VLMs) have evolved from general-purpose applications to specialized use cases such as in the clinical domain, demonstrating potential for decision support in radiology. One promising application is assisting radiologists in decision-making by the analysis of radiology imaging data such as chest X-rays (CXR) via a visual and natural language question-answering (VQA) interface. When longitudinal imaging is available, radiologists analyze temporal changes, which are essential for accurate diagnosis and prognosis. The manual longitudinal analysis is a time-consuming process, motivating the development of a training framework that can provide prognostic capabilities. We introduce a novel training framework LUMEN that is optimized for longitudinal CXR interpretation, leveraging multi-image and multi-task instruction fine-tuning to enhance prognostic and diagnostic performance. We conduct experiments on the publicly available MIMIC-CXR and its associated Medical-Diff-VQA datasets. We further formulate and construct a novel instruction-following dataset incorporating longitudinal studies, enabling the development of a prognostic VQA task. Our method demonstrates significant improvements over baseline models in diagnostic VQA tasks, and more importantly, shows promising potential for prognostic capabilities. These results underscore the value of well-designed, instruction-tuned VLMs in enabling more accurate and clinically meaningful radiological interpretation of longitudinal radiological imaging data.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Safm-Cta: Segmentation-Augmented Foundation Model for CT-to-CTA Translation.
abstract: Computed Tomography Angiography (CTA) synthesis from non-contrast Computed Tomography (CT) scans offers a contrast-free alternative for vascular assessment, particularly benefiting patients at risk from iodinated contrast agents. However, existing generative models such as GANs or diffusion networks often fail to maintain vascular continuity and anatomical realism. In this study, we propose SAFM-CTA, a Segmentation-Augmented Foundation Model for high-fidelity CT-to-CTA translation. SAFM-CTA integrates a pretrained 3D Vision Transformer encoder that captures global anatomical priors with a multitask decoder jointly trained for CTA synthesis and vascular segmentation. Through segmentation-guided optimization and vessel-weighted content loss, the model enforces explicit anatomical consistency during generation. Evaluated on 1,886 paired CT-CTA scans, SAFM-CTA surpasses state-of-the-art methods (PSNR: 29.37, SSIM: 0.915), yielding superior vessel integrity. These results highlight the potential of SAFM-CTA as a clinically applicable foundation model enabling contrastfree angiographic imaging with strong structural coherence and perceptual fidelity.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Hyper-DSCNet: Integrating Radiographic Details and Syndromic Context with Hypergraph Learning for Chest X-Ray Detection.
abstract: Chest X-ray imaging plays a crucial role in thoracic disease screening, yet faces challenges in detecting complex lesions ranging from micro-nodules to interconnected syndromes like heart failure. Current deep learning models exhibit limitations in local detail perception and multi-lesion semantic relationship modeling. Based on this, we propose Hyper-DSCNet, a Hypergraph learning method that integrates three core modules: a Radiographic Detail Enhancement(RDE) module for small lesions, a Syndromic Context Modeling (SCM) module for capturing high-order associations, and a Multi-finding Adaptive Fusion (MFA) module for dynamic feature integration. Evaluation on the ChestX-Det dataset shows 3.0% AP50 and 6.8% AP-s improvements over baselines, demonstrating strong performance and clinical potential.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Disease Progression and Subtype Modeling for Combined Discrete and Continuous Input Data.
abstract: Disease progression modeling provides a robust framework to identify long-term disease trajectories from short-term biomarker data. It is a valuable tool to gain a deeper understanding of diseases with a long disease trajectory, such as Alzheimer's disease. A key limitation of most disease progression models is that they are specific to a single data type (e.g., continuous data), thereby limiting their applicability to heterogeneous, real-world datasets. To address this limitation, we propose the Mixed Events model, a novel disease progression model that handles both discrete and continuous data types. This model is implemented within the Subtype and Stage Inference (SuStaIn) framework, resulting in Mixed-SuStaIn, enabling subtype and progression modeling. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Mixed-SuStaIn through simulation experiments and realworld data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, showing that it performs well on mixed datasets. The code is available at: https://github.com/ucl-pond/pySuStaIn.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Optical Flow-Guided Echocardiography Label Augmentation for the Segment Anything Model.
abstract: Echocardiography plays a crucial role in evaluating cardiac function; however, conventional segmentation techniques often struggle with limited annotations and domain shifts arising from variations in patient and device environments. In this study, we propose the Echo Flow Labeling (EFL) framework, a pseudo-label augmentation strategy driven by optical flow, designed to extend sparse end-diastolic and end-systolic annotations to intermediate frames. Our method leverages unsupervised optical flow estimation, a novel pointbased label refinement, and an occlusion-aware weighting scheme to enhance segmentation consistency and boundary accuracy in SAM-based models. Extensive experiments on publicly available CAMUS and EchoNet-Dynamic datasets show that the EFL framework consistently improves segmentation performance even under sparse frame annotations scenarios. These results indicate that integrating annotationdriven learning with an occlusion-aware weighting strategy can meaningfully improve the performance of large-scale pretrained models on task-specific echocardiography datasets.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Preserving Anatomical Continuity: Three-Stage Pipeline for Colon Segmentation in 3D Abdominal CT Scans.
abstract: Accurate colon segmentation from CT images is essential for colorectal disease analysis, yet deep learning based methods often produce disconnected predictions due to complex anatomy. This study introduces a three-stage, topologypreserving segmentation pipeline to address this issue. The first stage performs initial deep learning-based segmentation, followed by centreline bridging to reconnect disjoint regions and a reconstruction stage to refine continuity. Evaluations on TotalSegmentator and RAOS datasets using overlap, distance and topology-based metrics demonstrate improved structural consistency while maintaining segmentation accuracy. The proposed method enhances topological integrity, enabling more reliable colon segmentation for clinical and research applications.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Riva Cytology Classification and Detection: A Lesson on How "None of Us is as Smart as All of Us".
abstract: Early and accurate computer-aided detection of abnormal cervical cells in Papanicolaou smear images is essential for preventing cervical cancer, in particular for centers with limited access to expert cytotechnologists. The RIVA Cytology Challenge provides a large-scale, expert-annotated collection of high-resolution Papanicolaou smear images from Hospital Rivadavia, offering the unique opportunity to develop a highly accurate classification and detection model for automated cervical cancer screening. In this work, we describe our solution for the challenge in Track A, which involves both the classification and detection tasks. Our proposed solution achieved the mean Average Precision (mAP@0.50:0.95) score of 0.14183, and demonstrate many strategies, which were found to be successful in progressively improving the test scores, as well as those which failed to do so.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Modeling Structure-Function Discordance in Glaucoma Visual Field Analysis.
abstract: The Humphrey Visual Field (HVF) test is essential for assessing functional vision loss in glaucoma, but artifacts and patient variability can reduce test reliability. This work models and aims to predict two types of structure-function discordance between HVF sensitivity and retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness from optical coherence tomography (OCT): (i) functional loss with normal structure (FLD) and (ii) structural loss with normal function (SLD). Groundtruth labels were derived by combining HVF pattern deviations with OCT RNFL classifications, while predictions relied solely on HVF data. We evaluated three methods: (i) neighbor-based rules, (ii) zone-majority classification, and (iii) a lightweight convolutional neural architecture with dual outputs each specialized for FLD or SLD. The CNN outperformed rule-based baselines, demonstrating that HVF-based models can predict structure-function discordance, providing a potential signal for test reliability. This approach may support clinicians in identifying questionable test regions and deciding whether repeat testing is warranted.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Radiomics LUS Transformer for Liver Tumour Segmentation.
abstract: Accurately segmenting liver tumours in laparoscopic ultrasonography (LUS) is critical for computer-assisted intervention guidance with augmented reality (AR). However, LUS images are often degraded by speckle noise, low contrast, and acoustic artifacts, while the liver's complex anatomy and tumour heterogeneity further complicate segmentation. These challenges are exacerbated by the probe's limited field of view and restricted manoeuvrability, which frequently produce partial or inconsistent tumour appearances across frames. Moreover, isoechoic tumours exhibit echogenicity similar to the surrounding liver tissue, rendering them nearly invisible in individual frames. To address these limitations, we propose RadioLUS, a hybrid deep-learning framework that operates on sequences of LUS frames. It integrates hierarchical visual features from a Swin-UNet backbone with handcrafted radiomics descriptors that capture speckle, texture, and shape characteristics. By aggregating temporal information across frames, the framework enhances weak tumour boundaries and improves the detection of subtle tissue variations. Experimental results demonstrate that RadioLUS outperforms the state-of-the-art under challenging LUS imaging conditions.

verified_metadata.title: Radiomics LUS Transformer for Liver Tumour Segmentation
verified_metadata.conference_title: 2026 IEEE 23rd International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
verified_metadata.abstract: Accurately segmenting liver tumours in laparoscopic ultrasonography (LUS) is critical for computer-assisted intervention guidance with augmented reality (AR). However, LUS images are often degraded by speckle noise, low contrast, and acoustic artifacts, while the liver's complex anatomy and tumour heterogeneity further complicate segmentation. These challenges are exacerbated by the probe's limited field of view and restricted manoeuvrability, which frequently produce partial or inconsistent tumour appearances across frames. Moreover, isoechoic tumours exhibit echogenicity similar to the surrounding liver tissue, rendering them nearly invisible in individual frames. To address these limitations, we propose RadioLUS, a hybrid deep-learning framework that operates on sequences of LUS frames. It integrates hierarchical visual features from a Swin-UNet backbone with handcrafted radiomics descriptors that capture speckle, texture, and shape characteristics. By aggregating temporal information across frames, the framework enhances weak tumour boundaries and improves the detection of subtle tissue variations. Experimental results demonstrate that RadioLUS outperforms the state-of-the-art under challenging LUS imaging conditions.

title: Aurora: Adaptive Unified Representation for Robust Ultrasound Analysis.
authors: L. D. M. S. S. Teja
abstract: Ultrasound images can vary widely across scanners, operators, and anatomical targets, so models trained in one setting often generalize poorly to new hospitals and clinical conditions. The Foundation Model Challenge for Ultrasound Image Analysis (FMC-UIA) reflects this scenario by requiring a single model to handle multiple tasks like segmentation, detection, classification, and landmark regression across diverse organs and datasets. We propose a unified multi-task framework based on a transformer visual encoder from the Qwen3-VL family. Intermediate token features are projected into spatial feature maps and fused using a lightweight multiscale feature pyramid, enabling both pixel-level predictions and global reasoning within a shared representation. Each task is addressed with a small task-specific prediction head, while training uses task-aware sampling and selective loss balancing to manage heterogeneous supervision and reduce task imbalance. Our method is designed to be straightforward to optimize and adaptable across a wide range of ultrasound analysis tasks. The score improved from$\mathbf{6 7 \%}$to$\mathbf{8 5 \%}$on validation and reached$\mathbf{8 1. 8 4 \%}$average on the official test set across all tasks. The code is publicly available at Github.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: F2FD-TTT: Test-Time Training with Self-Supervised Fourier-to-Fourier Denoising for Membrane Segmentation in Cryo-ET Tomograms.
abstract: Cryogenic electron tomography (cryo-ET) is a technique for imaging biological structures in their native environments. An important step in downstream analysis of cellular cryo-ET data is segmenting membranes within tomograms, which facilitates the study of cellular architectures. Numerous supervised deep learning-based membrane segmentation approaches were introduced. However, supervised deep segmentation networks often struggle with generalization due to domain shifts caused by factors such as biological variability and different imaging and post-processing conditions. In this work, we propose F2FD-TTT, a cryo-ET-specific approach for test-time training that incorporates self-supervised Fourier-to-Fourier denoising to facilitate generalization of deep neural networks for membrane segmentation. We evaluate F2FD-TTT on a recent dataset consisting of tomograms from diverse sources and demonstrate that F2FD-TTT can improve cross-domain generalization without requiring supervised fine-tuning.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Oculomix: Hierarchical Sampling for Retinal-Based Systemic Disease Prediction.
abstract: Oculomics — the concept of predicting systemic diseases, such as cardiovascular disease and dementia, through retinal imaging — has advanced rapidly due to the data efficiency of transformer-based foundation models like RETFound. Image-level mixed sample data augmentations, such as CutMix and MixUp, are frequently used for training transformers, yet these techniques perturb patient-specific attributes, such as medical comorbidity and clinical factors, since they only account for images and labels. To address this limitation, we propose a hierarchical sampling strategy, Oculomix, for mixed sample augmentations. Our method is based on two clinical priors. First (exam level), images acquired from the same patient at the same time point share the same attributes. Second (patient level), images acquired from the same patient at different time points have a soft temporal trend, as morbidity generally increases over time. Guided by these priors, our method constrains the mixing space to the patient and exam levels to better preserve patient-specific characteristics and leverages their hierarchical relationships. The proposed method is validated using ViT models on a five-year prediction of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in a large ethnically diverse population (Alzeye). We show that Oculomix consistently outperforms image-level CutMix and MixUp by up to 3% in AUROC, demonstrating the necessity and value of the proposed method in oculomics.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Weakly Supervised Counterfactual Spatio-Temporal Multiple Instance Learning for Inflammation Detection in Endoscopic Inflammatory Bowel Disease Assessment.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) significantly impacts patients' quality of life, and accurate endoscopic assessment is critical for effective management. Conventional deep learning methods require frame-level annotations, which are labor-intensive and impractical for large video datasets. We propose a weakly supervised counterfactual spatio-temporal attention multiple instance learning (CFSpatioMIL) framework that captures spatial and temporal dependencies using only video-level labels. To enhance robustness and interpretability, we introduce a top-$k$instance loss to encourage attention on multiple discriminative frames, and a counterfactual consistency mechanism that enforces stable predictions when highly attended frames are removed or replaced. We evaluate our approach on two multi-center IBD video datasets, training on one and externally validating on the other. CFSpatioMIL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art MIL baselines in F1 score and AUC, demonstrating its potential as a scalable approach for standardized inflammation assessment.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Center-Aware Detection with Swin-Based Co-DETR Framework for Cervical Cytology.
abstract: Automated analysis of Pap smear images is critical for cervical cancer screening but remains challenging due to dense cell distribution and complex morphology. In this paper, we present our winning solution for the RIVA Cervical Cytology Challenge, achieving 1st place in Track B and 2nd place in Track A. Our approach leverages a powerful baseline, integrating the Co-DINO framework with a Swin-Large backbone for robust multi-scale feature extraction. To address the dataset's unique fixed-size bounding box annotations, we formulate the detection task as a center-point prediction problem. Tailoring our approach to this formulation, we introduce a center-preserving data augmentation strategy and an analytical geometric box optimization to effectively absorb localization jitter. Finally, we apply track-specific loss tuning to adapt the loss weights for each task. Experiments demonstrate that our targeted optimizations improve detection performance, providing an effective pipeline for cytology image analysis. Our code is available at https://github.com/YanKong0408/Center-DETR.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: NOA: A Versatile, Extensible Tool for AI-Based Organoid Analysis.
abstract: AI tools can greatly enhance the analysis of organoid microscopy images, from detection and segmentation to feature extraction and classification. However, their limited accessibility to biologists without programming experience remains a major barrier, resulting in labor-intensive and largely manual workflows. Although a few AI models for organoid analysis have been developed, most existing tools remain narrowly focused on specific tasks. In this work, we introduce the Napari Organoid Analyzer (NOA), a general purpose graphical user interface to simplify AI-based organoid analysis. NOA integrates modules for detection, segmentation, tracking, feature extraction, custom feature annotation and ML-based feature prediction. It interfaces multiple state-of-the-art algorithms and is implemented as an open-source napari plugin for maximal flexibility and extensibility. We demonstrate the versatility of NOA through three case studies, involving the quantification of morphological changes during organoid differentiation, assessment of phototoxicity effects, and prediction of organoid viability and differentiation state. Together, these examples illustrate how NOA enables comprehensive, AI-driven organoid image analysis within an accessible and extensible framework.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Crestomics: Analyzing Carotid Plaques in the Crest-2 Trial with a New Additive Classification Model.
abstract: Accurate characterization of carotid plaques is critical for stroke prevention in patients with carotid stenosis. We analyze 500 plaques from CREST-2, a multi-center clinical trial, to identify radiomics-based markers from B-mode ultrasound images linked with high-risk. We propose a new kernel-based additive model, combining coherence loss with group-sparse regularization for nonlinear classification. Group-wise additive effects of each feature group are visualized using partial dependence plots. Results indicate our method accurately and interpretably assesses plaques, revealing a strong association between plaque texture and clinical risk.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Effectiveness of SAM for Conjunctiva Segmentation.
abstract: We propose an end-to-end framework for anemia detection from eye conjunctiva images, integrating a LoRA fine-tuned Segment Anything Model (SAM) for segmentation with machine learning models for hemoglobin estimation and classification. The LoRA-based SAM achieved mean IoU scores of 83.4 % on the Eye-Defy dataset and 76.1 % on the Eye Conjunctiva Segmentation Dataset, outperforming zero-shot SAM variants. Handcrafted RGB and CIE-Lab features extracted from the segmented conjunctiva enabled Random Forest regression to achieve an$R^{2}$of 0.52 (MAE$1.23 ~\mathrm{g} / \text{dL})$, closely matching results using ground-truth masks. For binary anemia classification, Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM achieved accuracies up to 90 %, exceeding prior literature. These results highlight the effectiveness of SAM in producing high-quality conjunctiva segmentation without manual annotation, enabling scalable and automated anemia screening. Code is available online.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Automatic Vertebrae Segmentation From Intraoperative 3D Point Clouds for Scoliosis Spine Surgery.
abstract: Accurate, real-time assessment of spinal alignment is essential in Posterior Spinal Fusion Surgery (PSFS) for scoliosis correction. Image-guided surgery systems rely on the registration of a preoperative spine model to intraoperative images. In this work, we tackle the segmentation of vertebrae from textured 3D point clouds acquired during the surgery without any radiation. We trained a Point Transformer v3 for vertebra segmentation, demonstrating a 14.2 % improvement over prior U-Net-based architectures on the cadaveric SpineDepth benchmark. To overcome the critical scarcity of real intraoperative data, we establish a semi-synthetic training paradigm incorporating the SpineDepth data with an augmented dataset derived from 49 real scoliosis cases, featuring synthesized surgical texture. On top of that, we demonstrate the clinical feasibility of this approach through a pilot evaluation on a real intraoperative PSFS case, where our integrated method achieves promising segmentation results. This work marks a significant step toward eliminating reliance on intraoperative radiation for spinal assessment.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Identifying Optimal nnU-Net Configuration for Cerebral Microbleed Segmentation.
abstract: The nnU-Net has become the de facto standard in medical image segmentation. While the generalizability of nnUNet has widely been studied across various domains, we question the optimality of the automated nnU-Net configuration specifically for cerebral microbleed (CMB) segmentation. We identified that the standard nnU-Net setup, particularly the recommended input patch size, is primarily optimized for the heterogeneous nature of multi-organ segmentation, resulting in suboptimal performance for CMB segmentation. To address this limitation, we propose a patch selection algorithm based on a local minima search that fully leverages the imaging characteristics of CMB lesions. Experiments on two independent cohorts demonstrate that our approach improves the overall performance without altering the segmentation backbone, highlighting the important role of preprocessing. Our code is available at https://github.com/junmokwon/CMBPreprocessing
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Introduction of a Learned Prior to Passive Cavitation Imaging.
abstract: High-intensity focused ultrasound can induce cavitation, enabling therapeutic applications, such as sonoporation, targeted drug delivery, or histotripsy, which require accurate monitoring. Passive acoustic mapping, known as passive delay-and-sum (DAS), is a common cavitation monitoring technique but suffers from limited axial resolution. Recently, a regularized inverse approach, cross-spectral matrix fitting (CMF), incorporating prior knowledge into the reconstruction process, such as the group sparse characteristics of cavitation power maps (CMF-spTV), was proposed. While this approach improves axial resolution, it may fail to reconstruct cavitation clouds under specific conditions, e.g., elongated in the lateral direction. Herein, we propose a plug-andplay framework using a deep denoiser learned within a deep equilibrium framework. The proposed method improves the F1-score by 2 percentage points compared to CMF-spTV and by 32 points compared to DAS, with visibly better reconstructions, especially of laterally elongated cavitation clouds.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Resource-Efficient Automatic Refinement of Segmentations via Weak Supervision from Light Feedback.
abstract: Delineating anatomical regions is a key task in medical image analysis. Manual segmentation achieves high accuracy but is labor-intensive and prone to variability, thus prompting the development of automated approaches. Recently, a breadth of foundation models has enabled automated segmentations across diverse anatomies and imaging modalities, but these may not always meet the clinical accuracy standards. While segmentation refinement strategies can improve performance, current methods depend on heavy user interactions or require fully supervised segmentations for training. Here, we present SCORE (Segmentation COrrection from Regional Evaluations), a weakly supervised framework that learns to refine mask predictions only using light feedback during training. Specifically, instead of relying on dense training image annotations, SCORE introduces a novel loss that leverages region-wise quality scores and over/under-segmentation error labels. We demonstrate SCORE on humerus CT scans, where it considerably improves initial predictions from TotalSegmentator, and achieves performance on par with existing refinement methods, while greatly reducing their supervision requirements and annotation time. Our code is available at: https://gitlab.inria.fr/adelangl/SCORE.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: The Retinal-Glycemic Link: Using Retinal Imaging to Explore Glycemic Variability.
abstract: Retinal vasculature provides insight into systemic body health. In this work, we characterize and illustrate the potential for early detection of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) images. Using the AI-READI cohort ($\mathrm{N}=1062$), we extract vascular metrics from OCTA images and correlate them with diabetic state (based on hemoglobin$\mathrm{A} 1 \mathrm{c}, \text{HbA} 1 \mathrm{c}$) as well as continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) variables. Our results show that OCTA features of foveal avascular zone area, roundness of vessels, and degree of branching are most highly-correlated with HbA 1 c and CGM variables. We also explore the ability of multimodal deep learning (DL) models trained on OCTA metrics and additional retinal imaging to classify high vs. low glycemic variability, which has been shown to be an early biomarker of glycemic dysregulation and insulin resistance. We find that combining fundus images with OCTA metrics moderately improves DL classification performance compared to unimodal inputs. These findings highlight the potential of multimodal retinal imaging as a widely deployable tool for early metabolic screening.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Robust White Blood Cell Classification With Stain-Normalized Decoupled Learning and Ensembling.
abstract: White blood cell (WBC) classification is fundamental for hematology applications such as infection assessment, leukemia screening, and treatment monitoring. However, real-world WBC datasets present substantial appearance variations caused by staining and scanning conditions, as well as severe class imbalance in which common cell types dominate while rare but clinically important categories are underrepresented. To address these challenges, we propose a stainnormalized, decoupled training framework that first learns transferable representations using instance-balanced sampling, and then rebalances the classifier with class-aware sampling and a hybrid loss combining effective-number weighting and focal modulation. In the inference stage, we further enhance robustness by ensembling multiple trained backbones with test-time augmentation. Our approach achieved the top rank on the leaderboard of the WBCBench 2026: Robust White Blood Cell Classification Challenge at ISBI 2026. Our code implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/luulecmg/WBCBench2026
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Otoscopy AI: Deeply Supervised Attention for Otoscopic Image Segmentation.
abstract: Automatic segmentation of otoscopic images is a prevalent challenge and a focus of active research. Recent works in the field adopt convolutional neural networks (CNNs) because of their performance compared to traditional methods. In this paper, we introduce a novel deeply supervised attention (DSA) approach that integrates a deep supervision mechanism with a convolutional block attention module (CBAM) to enhance the model using high-level features from small and uncertain objects. The proposed approach improves the segmentation of 11 otoscopic features, including the tympanic membrane, the cerumen, and abnormalities. Our method is the first architecture to provide segmentation for such abnormalities, reaching 0.80 mAP on average, demonstrating$10-20 \%$superior performance over existing state-of-the-art methods. To ensure robustness and generalization in real world settings, additional evaluations were performed on a clinical test dataset and a published benchmark.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Predicting Post-Stenting Outcomes Using Self-Supervised 3D Vision Transformers in Intravascular OCT.
abstract: Intravascular optical coherence tomography (IVOCT) has emerged as a powerful imaging modality for guiding percutaneous coronary intervention. This study aimed to develop a fully automated deep learning framework to predict post-stenting outcomes from pre-stenting IVOCT images. A total of 263,504 images from 1,263 patients who underwent IVOCT-guided PCI were analyzed. For each case, a 3D volume of interest comprising the target frame and ± 15 adjacent frames was constructed as input to the network. The proposed framework integrated self-supervised pretraining and supervised fine-tuning using a vision transformer to predict post-stenting lumen area. The model achieved strong agreement with the ground truth, with an R2of 0.863, root mean square error of 0.903 m m2, and concordance correlation coefficient of 0.925. Furthermore, our model accurately identified stent under-expansion, yielding a sensitivity of 89.6% and specificity of 87.7%. These findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed approach to support data-driven clinical decision-making.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Quality Control for Medical Image Segmentation Under Domain Shift with Heteroscedastic Regression.
abstract: Trustworthy medical image segmentation systems require robust quality control mechanisms so that inadequately segmented cases can be excluded from downstream processing. This need becomes particularly acute when inputs deviate from the training distribution, such as images from unseen pathologies or novel scanner types. We propose heteroscedastic regression as a new approach for this, explicitly modeling both the expected accuracy and the uncertainty in our estimate. This framework provides flexibility to perform failure detection with varying thresholds for segmentation quality and confidence. Moreover, it can be combined with a recently proposed adversarial training strategy to achieve OOD generalization. Our approach permits computationally efficient inference and more reliably filters out low-quality segmentations than score agreement, while retaining substantially more high-quality results than predictive entropy or anomaly detection based approaches. Code is available from https://github.com/MedVisBonn/isbi26-implementation
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: ST-SAM: A Spatio-Temporal Enhanced Segment Anything Model for Echocardiogram Video Segmentation.
abstract: Echocardiogram video segmentation is crucial for enabling rapid, objective, and reproducible quantification of cardiac structures, which is the key for the diagnosis and treatment of cardiovascular diseases. Although recent SAM-based methods have achieved promising results, they often struggle to effectively capture spatio-temporal features in echocardiogram videos, resulting in limited performance for multi-structure segmentation. To this end, we propose the Spatio-Temporal Segment Anything Model (ST-SAM)—a novel framework comprising a Spatial Topology Module (STM) and a Temporal Graph Enhanced Module (TGEM) that jointly enhance spatial topological relationships and temporal consistency in echocardiogram videos. Experimental results demonstrate that ST-SAM outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods by an average of 3.0% Dice across four-chamber segmentation tasks. The source code can be found at https://github.com/xmed-lab/ST-SAM.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Evidence-Grounded Temporal Reasoning in Operating Room Long Video Understanding.
abstract: Operating rooms (OR) are complex, high-risk environments that demand long-horizon video understanding for intelligent surgical assistance and quality assurance. Existing domainspecific OR models and datasets mainly address short-clip or frame-level analysis, lacking the ability to reason across extended temporal contexts. In contrast, general long-video multimodal large language models (MLLMs) exhibit strong temporal reasoning but fail to capture the structured interactions and clinical semantics unique to surgical workflows. To bridge this gap, we introduce OR-LongVQA, a benchmark for long-video understanding in operating rooms, covering diverse factors and causality-centered questions. We further propose a reasoning retrieval framework based on temporal scene graph and evidence-grounded reasoning modules that retrieve relevant subgraphs and perform interpretable step-by-step inference. We compare the proposed reasoning framework with existing state-of-the-art methods on the OR-LongVQA benchmark. Our approach outperforms prior methods by achieving significant improvements in longhorizon reasoning accuracy and interpretability, demonstrating its effectiveness and reliability for clinically-oriented, structured operating room video understanding.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Frequency-Aware Spatiotemporal Modeling With Cross-Frequency Attention for Echocardiography Left Ventricle Segmentation.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of the left ventricle (LV) in echocardiography videos is essential for cardiac function assessment but remains challenging due to complex motion patterns, temporal dependencies, and noisy artifacts. In this work, we propose a novel frequency-aware spatiotemporal modeling network that captures both video-level and frame-level frequency characteristics for robust LV segmentation. At the video level, the extracted spatiotemporal feature tensor is decomposed into low-frequency components that capture periodic cardiac dynamics and high-frequency components that retain fine structural details. A cross-frequency attention mechanism enables high-frequency queries and values to interact with low-frequency keys, enhancing boundary learning under the guidance of global motion consistency. At the frame level, we utilize joint spatial-frequency feature extraction in the encoder and adaptively fuse high- and low-frequency components through skip connections in the decoder, enhancing segmentation precision and structural fidelity for each frame. Experiments on the CAMUS dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, effectively leveraging both temporal coherence and frame-level detail for accurate LV segmentation.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Efficient Statistical Shape Analysis of 3D Cell Surface with Deep Functional Map and Elastic Shape Flow.
abstract: Quantifying cell shapes in three-dimensional (3D) space is a fundamental readout of cellular state and function, and intricately linked to a multitude of biological processes. Currently, existing 3D cell shape analysis methods mainly use over-simplified features, which are difficult scaled up to large-scale datasets and lack statistical rigor. To address these problems, we propose an efficient statistical shape analysis framework tailored for 3D cell shape. Technically, we adopt the state-of-the-art deep learning-based shape matching method that enables efficient and accurate correspondences of cell shapes. Then we apply the non-Euclidean statistical shape analysis with elastic shape metric to model the complicated morphologism with necessary statistical rigors at population level. Experiments on public 3D cell datasets compared with existing methods demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: MEA-YOLO: Medical Enhanced Attention YOLO for Simultaneous Polyp and Lumen Detection in Robotic Colonoscopy.
abstract: Robotic colonoscopy requires accurate simultaneous detection of polyps and lumens for autonomous navigation. However, existing object detectors lack medical domain-specific designs. We present MEA-YOLO (Medical Enhanced Attention YOLO), a unified framework for simultaneous polyp and lumen detection that integrates domain-specific attention mechanisms tailored for colonoscopy imaging. Our novel C2f-MEA module combines efficient multi-scale attention with specialized edge and lumen enhancement branches, addressing the unique visual characteristics of colonoscopic images. Evaluated on the Extended-LDPolyp dataset (37,947 images with dual annotations, video-level split), MEA-YOLO achieves 74.52% mAP@0.5, outperforming YOLOv8n by 2.58% and Faster R-CNN by 41.65%. Task-specific evaluation shows 72.52% AP for polyp detection and 76.52% AP for lumen detection, with consistent improvements in both precision and recall. Ablation studies confirm that medical-specific enhancements are crucial-while generic attention mechanisms degrade performance, our domain-aware design contributes 2.58% mAP improvement. Despite adding only 6.25% parameters overhead, MEA-YOLO maintains real-time performance at 111.5 FPS, demonstrating that architectural innovations guided by clinical insight can achieve superior accuracy without sacrificing efficiency for robotic colonoscopy deployment.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: BASSL-MI: Batch-Agnostic Self-Supervised Learning Uncovers Clinically Relevant Tumor Niches in Multiplexed Imaging.
abstract: ABSTRACT Multiplexed imaging enables rich, high-resolution characterization of the tumor microenvironment but relies on labor-intensive and error-prone cell segmentation and phenotyping pipelines. We present BASSL-MI, a batch-agnostic, self-supervised framework for discovering tissue niches directly from multiplexed imaging data. BASSL-MI operates directly on image patches, eliminating the need for explicit cell segmentation while mitigating image-, sample-, or batch-specific artifacts. Built on a modified contrastive block disentanglement architecture, BASSL-MI learns dual latent representations that separate biologically informative features from batch-dependent factors through spatially guided augmentations and batch-invariance objectives. Applied to a 56-marker colorectal cancer CODEX dataset, BASSL-MI-trained embeddings markedly reduce image-specific variability and recover biologically interpretable spatial niches. Notably, it uncovers CD20–rich follicular regions associated with improved survival, outperforming published findings from cell segmentation-driven clustering. This work demonstrates that self-supervised, patch-based learning can capture clinically relevant spatial organization within tumor microenvironments, advancing toward automated, non-cell-based analysis of multiplexed imaging data.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: A Unified Multi-Task Learning Framework for Ultrasound Image Analysis.
abstract: Ultrasound imaging involves diverse anatomical targets and variable acquisition settings, which complicates the creation of broadly applicable analytical tools. Conventional deep learning approaches are often narrowly tailored to individual tasks, which restricts their potential to serve as versatile foundation models in clinical contexts. In response, the Foundation Model Challenge for Ultrasound Image Analysis (FMC_UIA) 2026 establishes a comprehensive benchmark aggregating 27 distinct tasks-including segmentation, classification, detection, and regression. This paper describes our proposed solution for FMC_UIA 2026, which adopts a unified Multi-Head Multi-Task Learning (MH-MTL) architecture with hard parameter sharing. A MiT-B5 backbone pre-trained on ImageNet provides rich feature representations. For different tasks, we use multiple task heads for prediction, and we use a routing mechanism to control the task heads. Training proceeds in two phases-initial multitask joint learning, followed by targeted fine-tuning per task group. The experimental results have confirmed the feasibility and stability of this unified method. Finally, our total score on the test set was 0.9215, and we ranked third. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/linghs/ISBI-FMC-UIA-Challenge.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Dual-Domain Diffusion Priors and Image Fusion-Based Model for Metal Artifact Reduction in Clinical Dental CBCT Images.
abstract: The presence of metal artifacts in dental cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images significantly impedes accurate diagnosis, driving the need for more effective metal artifact reduction (MAR) methods. In this study, we propose a novel unsupervised model, the Dual-domain Diffusion Priors and Image Fusion-based Model (DDPIFM), for MAR in clinical dental CBCT images. This approach utilizes two Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM) to learn the metal-free data distribution priors in both the image and projection domains, respectively, and applies these priors to remove metal artifacts in both domains. During the sampling process, information from both domains is fused into the generated image, progressively eliminating artifacts and enhancing image quality. Experimental results demonstrate that our DDPIFM outperforms traditional method and other unsupervised diffusion model in both quantitative analysis of simulated cases and qualitative analysis of clinical case.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: YOLO-US: A Unified Multi-Task Foundation Framework for Generalist Ultrasound Image Analysis.
abstract: The inherent heterogeneity of Ultrasound (US) imaging impedes the development of generalizable medical models, whereas the clinical translation of Generalist Medical AI demands unified foundation models rather than task or organ-specific approaches. This study proposes YOLOUS, the official baseline for the FMC_UIA 2026 challenge, which enhances the YOLOv11 architecture with a custom C3_MViTBv3 backbone and lightweight MBTransformer blocks, achieving a balance between local texture extraction, global long-range dependency modeling, and computational efficiency. Shared multi-scale representations are dynamically routed to four decoupled, task-specific heads, which are optimized for segmentation, classification, detection, and biometric regression. Comprehensive evaluation across a heterogeneous benchmark consisting of 27 subtasks demonstrates state-of-the-art robustness, with a normalized IoU of 0.7955 for precise detetction and a normalized MRE of 40.63 for biometric measurement. Furthermore, in-depth analysis of segmentation performance under severe domain distribution shifts yields critical insights into the “heterogeneity gap,” validating YOLO-US as a scalable, mobile-friendly baseline for future ultrasound foundation models. The code will be available at https://github.com/LwpZoe/YOLO-US.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Leveraging Fourier Domain for Unsupervised Removal of Structured Noise in Fluorescence Microscopy Imaging.
abstract: Due to the practical limitations such as phototoxicity, fluorescence microscopy images are generally with faint signals corrupted by severe and complex noise, necessitating the denoising step to improve image quality for more accurate biological analysis. Recently, unsupervised deep learning techniques have attracted widespread attentions owing to their powerful capability of removing noise without the reliance of collecting clean images. Although existing unsupervised denoising methods such as blind spot networks are effective in suppressing spatially independent noise, developing unsupervised strategies for structured noise is still underexplored. Based on the observation that noise correlated in the spatial domain can exhibit independence in the Fourier domain, this work develops a Fourier-based blind spot strategy to enable effective unsupervised structured noise removal for multi-frame fluorescence microscopy imaging. The evaluation on publicly available real-world microscopy datasets validates its effectiveness in removing structured noise.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: DiGMa: A Dual-Domain Collaborative Framework for Efficient Temporal MPI Reconstruction.
abstract: Magnetic particle imaging (MPI) is a novel imaging technique offering radiation-free and fast imaging with promise for temporal imaging studies (e.g., vascular and functional imaging). However, MPI temporal reconstruction is challenged by per-frame noise and the cost of joint spacetemporal modeling. In this study, we first propose a dualdomain collaborative framework for efficient temporal MPI reconstruction, named DiGMa, to address the two main challenges. DiGMa performs signal-domain denoising via GCN-based inter-frame modeling, and image-domain enhancement via Mamba that efficiently captures long-range dependencies. The proposed method was evaluated on both simulation and measured data, demonstrating superior performance over traditional approaches. Besides, qualitative results indicate fewer artifacts and superior image quality, while the computational load of the model is also reduced. DiGMa thus achieves a favorable balance between reconstruction quality and computational efficiency for temporal MPI.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Semantic-Aware 3D Polyp Segmentation in Dynamic Endoscopy Scenes.
abstract: This paper proposes the first 3D polyp segmentation method based on Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) for dynamic endoscopy scenes. A two-staged training approach, SAPolyp-NeRF (Segment Anything Polyp in NeRFs), is introduced. The first stage is to reconstruct the dynamic implicit field of soft tissue. Then, a multi-view self-prompt mechanism is employed to automatically predict 2D polyp masks for the rendered views generated by the dynamic implicit field. The second stage is a 2D-to-3D segmentation module, in which a view-alternating weak supervision strategy is introduced to train SAPolypNeRF for the second time using 2D polyp masks supervision aggregated from multiple training views to produce a dynamic 3D mask implicit field for 3D polyp segmentation. The experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves higher-quality comprehensive reconstruction and accurate segmentation of the lesion region than the state-of-the-art 3D segmentation methods, resulting in the best overall performance.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Unsupervised Adaptation from FDG to PSMA PET/CT for 3D Lesion Detection Under Label Shift.
abstract: In this work, we propose an unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) framework for 3D volumetric lesion detection that adapts a detector trained on labeled FDG PET/CT to unlabeled PSMA PET/CT. Beyond covariate shift, cross tracer adaptation also exhibits label shift in both lesion size composition and the number of lesions per subject. We introduce self-training with two mechanisms that explicitly model and compensate for this label shift. First, we adaptively adjust the detection anchor shapes by re-estimating target domain box scales from selected pseudo labels and updating anchors with an exponential moving average. This increases positive anchor coverage for small PSMA lesions and stabilizes box regression. Second, instead of a fixed confidence threshold for pseudo-label selection, we allocate size bin-wise quotas according to the estimated target domain histogram over lesion volumes. The self-training alternates between supervised learning with prior-guided pseudo labeling on PSMA and supervised learning on labeled FDG. On AutoPET 2024, adapting from 501 labeled FDG studies to 36918F-PSMA studies, the proposed method improves both AP and FROC over the source-only baseline and conventional self-training without label-shift mitigation, indicating that modeling target lesion prevalence and size composition is an effective path to robust cross-tracer detection.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Deepsrs: Enhancing Stimulated Raman Scattering Imaging Through Multi-Stage Deep Learning for Super-Resolution and Denoising.
abstract: DeepSRS is a multi-stage deep learning framework designed to enhance Stimulated Raman Scattering (SRS) microscopy images by addressing both denoising and super-resolution challenges. The pipeline combines an autoencoder-based spectral denoiser with fine-tuned generative models—namely GAN and diffusion architectures—to achieve rapid, high-fidelity reconstruction. DeepSRS attains up to fourfold lateral superresolution, markedly improving signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), structural similarity, and perceptual quality metrics. This integrated approach expands the analytical capabilities of nonlinear optical imaging and opens new avenues for biochemical visualization, histological interpretation, and quantitative microscopy in both research and clinical settings.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Unsupervised Fixed Point Networks for Improved MRF Reconstruction.
abstract: Magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF) is a powerful quantitative imaging technique that simultaneously estimates multiple tissue parameters from a single acquisition. However, severe undersampling in MRF often introduces artifacts and noise, compromising reconstruction accuracy and reliability. To address this, we propose UFP-MRF, a novel unsupervised fixed-point network for MRF reconstruction. The framework integrates the physical acquisition model with learnable regularization components, ensuring strong convergence through contractive mapping design. Leveraging a deep equilibrium (DEQ) formulation, UFP-MRF efficiently computes fixedpoint solutions that implicitly capture infinite-depth network behavior, achieving high-quality reconstructions at equilibrium. Trained via a data-consistency loss without fully sampled ground truth, UFP-MRF rapidly converges to a stable solution and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both reconstruction accuracy and robustness.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Intelligent Diagnosis of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease by Integrating CT Segmentation and Multi-Dimensional Representations.
abstract: CT scans of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) show spatial heterogeneity, making precise characterization difficult with traditional methods. This study proposes a deep learning model with a “segmentation first, then diagnosis” cascade framework for intelligent COPD risk stratification. In the segmentation stage, an Attention-Spectral Dual-Module (ASDM) is introduced to integrate frequency and spatial domain features, combined with a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to optimize skip connections and enhance key feature extraction. A region-adaptive composite loss function is designed to improve lung parenchyma segmentation accuracy. In the diagnosis stage, a cross-dimensional feature fusion architecture is used, with 2D CNNs extracting local texture features and 3D CNNs capturing short-range spatiotemporal context. A Transformer module models longrange dependencies across slices. Experimental results show excellent performance in lung parenchyma segmentation, with a Dice coefficient of 0.973. The model also achieves an accuracy of 95.8% in COPD diagnosis, demonstrating strong potential for clinical application.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: From Intensity to Anatomy: Optimizing nnU-Net for MR-to-CT Translation on SynthRAD2025.
abstract: Magnetic resonance (MR) to computed tomography (CT) translation enables a non-ionizing alternative for radiotherapy planning and longitudinal disease monitoring. The SynthRAD2025 dataset provides a large-scale benchmark to evaluate cross-modality synthesis methods across anatomical regions. Building upon the nnU-Net framework, this work revisits its design for image synthesis and proposes key optimizations to establish a strong new baseline. We integrate architectural refinements, a two-stage fine-tuning strategy, and an optimized Anatomical Feature-Prioritized (AFP) loss that leverages pre-trained segmentation features to enhance anatomical fidelity. Best practices for AFP supervision are detailed, including segmentation model configuration and layer selection. Evaluation on SynthRAD2025 combines intensity and segmentation-based metrics, showing that our optimized model ranks first on segmentation performance while maintaining competitive intensity fidelity. These findings demonstrate that anatomy-aware supervision within general-purpose architectures substantially improves clinical relevance without compromising visual quality. Our code is publicly available at github.com/Phyrise/nnUNet_translation.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Unified PET Image Enhancement for Diverse Degradation Levels with Mixture-Of-Experts and Dynamic Prompts.
abstract: Positron Emission Tomography (PET) images often suffer from suboptimal quality due to physical constraints and clinical trade-offs, such as radiation dose and scanning time. Thus, PET image enhancement using deep learning is of great importance. However, most existing methods are designed to handle a single degradation level and lack the flexibility to adapt to varying degrees of image degradation. Recently, the all-in-one image restoration paradigm has emerged, aiming to handle multiple types of degradation within a single model. Inspired by this direction, this paper proposes a unified model for enhancing PET images under various degradation conditions, including varying doses and scanning times. Specifically, we introduce a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) mechanism into the encoder of the Restormer network. This allows the model to adaptively select specialized experts for different degradations. We also employ dynamic and adaptive prompts in the decoder to guide the recovery process. The proposed method is validated on a dataset comprising 430 subjects with multiple scanning times. Experimental results show that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches. It works effectively on PET images acquired under various scanning conditions.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Scale-Aware Curriculum Learning for Data-Efficient Lung Nodule Detection with YOLOV11.
abstract: Lung nodule detection in chest CT is crucial for early lung cancer diagnosis, yet existing deep learning approaches face challenges when deployed in clinical settings with limited annotated data. While curriculum learning has shown promise in improving model training, traditional static curriculum strategies fail in data-scarce scenarios. We propose Scale-Adaptive Curriculum Learning (SACL), a novel training strategy that dynamically adjusts curriculum design based on available data scale. SACL introduces three key mechanisms: (1) adaptive epoch scheduling, (2) hard sample injection, and (3) scale-aware optimization. We evaluate SACL on the LUNA25 dataset using YOLOv11 as the base detector. Experimental results demonstrate that while SACL achieves comparable performance to static curriculum learning on the full dataset in$\text{mAP}_{50}$, it shows significant advantages under data-limited conditions with$4.6 \%, 3.5 \%$, and 2.0% improvements over baseline at$10 \%, 20 \%$, and 50% of training data respectively. By enabling robust training across varying data scales without architectural modifications, SACL provides a practical solution for healthcare institutions to develop effective lung nodule detection systems despite limited annotation resources.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: XBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Visual-Language Explanations in Chest Radiography.
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have recently shown remarkable zero-shot performance in medical image understanding, yet their grounding ability, the extent to which textual concepts align with visual evidence, remains underexplored. In the medical domain, however, reliable grounding is essential for interpretability and clinical trustworthiness. In this work, we present the first systematic benchmark for evaluating cross-modal interpretability in chest X-rays across seven CLIP-style VLM variants. We generate visual explanations using cross-attention and similarity-based grounding maps, and quantitatively assess their alignment with radiologist-annotated regions across 36 types of pathologies. Our analysis reveals that: (1) while all VLM variants demonstrate reasonable grounding maps for large and welldefined pathologies, their grounding performance substantially degrades for small or diffuse lesions; (2) models that are pretrained on chest X-ray-specific datasets exhibit improved alignment compared to those trained on general-domain data. (3) The overall classification performance and grounding performance of the model are strongly correlated. These findings underscore that current VLMs, despite their strong classification performance, still fall short in clinically reliable grounding, highlighting the need for targeted interpretability benchmarks before deployment in medical practice. XBench code is available at https://github.com/Roypic/Benchmarkingattention.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: DPANet: Dual-Path Prior-Guided Attention Network for Few-Shot Intravascular Ultrasound Segmentation.
abstract: Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) is a key modality for early detection of coronary artery disease, enabling the assessment of vessel morphology and plaque burden by delineating the lumen and the external elastic membrane (EEM). However, low contrast, blurred boundaries between lumen and EEM, and scarce expert annotations make accurate IVUS segmentation difficult. We propose DPANet, a Dual-Path Prior-guided Attention Network for Few-Shot IVUS Segmentation. DPANet combines (1) a prior-guided difference reconstruction path that independently segments the lumen and lumen+EEM regions, then recovers the EEM via set difference to sharpen boundaries in low-contrast areas; and (2) an Iterative Prototype Refinement (IPR) module whose Cross-Attention Aggregation Module (CAAM) dynamically aligns prototypes with spatial features, improving generalisation under few-shot supervision. Experiments on a private IVUS cohort demonstrate that DPANet improves the average Dice score by approximately 3% over strong baselines, while maintaining high accuracy and robustness under severe artifact interference, and offering a practical solution for clinical vessel segmentation.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: End-to-End Mandibular Reconstruction with Integrated Repositioning and Completion Networks.
abstract: Patients with mandibular defects require mandibular reconstruction surgery to restore both physiological function and facial morphology. Accurate preoperative planning relies on a complete mandible in its correct anatomical position. However, existing methods primarily focus on morphological completion, without considering anatomical repositioning, which can result in significant issues if the defective mandible is left in a compensatory malposition. This paper presents a novel end-to-end framework that jointly performs mandible repositioning and morphological completion. In the repositioning stage, we predict rigid transformations to restore the displaced mandible to its anatomically correct location. The completion stage then restores the repositioned mandible to its complete morphology. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method surpasses state-of-the-art approaches, showing strong potential for clinical applications in computer-assisted craniofacial reconstruction.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Improving Gradient Flow Methods for Instance Segmentation of Crossing Objects.
abstract: In this paper we propose a novel flow tracking method for instance segmentation, that can handle crossing cells or objects. Current gradient-flow approaches (e.g. Cellpose, Omnipose) assign a single vector to each pixel; when flow tracks from different instances intersect, the vectors collapse onto a common trajectory, causing inseparable merges. Our new approach can infer multiple gradient-flow vectors at the same spatial location. By encoding the image into a latent embedding and decoding flow vectors conditioned on both the current pixel and its source position, the model can disambiguate intersecting flow lines and recover distinct instance masks even in scenes with many crossing instances. Evaluations on public microscopy benchmarks containing overlapping and elongated objects show that our multi-flow representation improves instance segmentation without sacrificing computational efficiency.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: DBCoreset: A Density-Based Coreset Algorithm for Computationally Efficient Chest X-Ray Diagnosis.
abstract: Coreset generation is a data reduction method that facilitates efficient deep learning training. A good coreset can achieve comparable performance using a much smaller number of training samples. However, traditional coreset methods exhibit density bias. This bias leads to poor representation of subregions that are sparsely populated by data points within a class. To solve this, we propose a novel Density-based Coreset Generation algorithm to facilitate computationally efficient chest x-ray diagnosis. We first partition the feature space into fine-grained, clinically-relevant miniclusters utilizing density. We then introduce a scoring-based selection mechanism. It helps in finding out the representative datapoints to eventually train a classifier model. Furthermore, we enforce a minimum inclusion criterion for every minicluster. This step aims to mitigate density bias so that coverage of all pathological patterns may be possible. Training the downstream classifier on the curated coreset demonstrates improved performance and balance. On the publicly available dataset, we used only about one-third of the training data and achieved a 40% reduction in computational resources. Even with this reduction, we have achieved as close as$83.01 \% \pm 0.36$with our method compared to$83.37 \% \pm 0.78$on the full dataset. We also outperform other coreset-based methods. Our method also reduces skewness in the classwise data distribution. The code is available at https://github.com/mahawar2/DbCoreset.git.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Automatic Correction of Generative AI Chest X-Ray Radiology Reports.
abstract: The factual correctness of generative AI-derived radiology reports needs to be improved before they can be used in clinical workflows. In this paper, we propose an automatic report correction method that uses both image and textual information in automated radiology reports to identity errors in identity and location in findings through fact-checking models. Prompts for a pre-trained large language model are then generated from the error analysis to produce corrected sentences by selectively modifying target findings described in the automated report sentences. We show that this method of report correction, on the average, improves the report quality between 17-30% across various SOTA report generators over multi-institutional chest X-ray datasets.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Unified Ultrasound Intelligence Toward an End-to-End Agentic System.
abstract: Clinical ultrasound analysis demands models that generalize across heterogeneous organs, views, and devices, while supporting interpretable workflow-level analysis. Existing methods often rely on task-wise adaptation, and joint learning may be unstable due to cross-task interference, making it hard to deliver workflow-level outputs in practice. To address these challenges, we present USTri, a tri-stage ultrasound intelligence pipeline for unified multi-organ, multi-task analysis. Stage I trains a universal generalist USGen on different domains to learn broad, transferable priors that are robust to device and protocol variability. To better handle domain shifts and reach task-aligned performance while preserving ultrasound shared knowledge, Stage II builds USpec by keeping USGen frozen and finetuning dataset-specific heads. Stage III introduces USAgent, which mimics clinician workflows by orchestrating USpec specialists for multi-step inference and deterministic structured reports. On the FMC_UIA validation set, our model achieves the best overall performance across 4 task types and 27 datasets, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, qualitative results show that USAgent produces clinically structured reports with high accuracy and interpretability. Our study suggests a scalable path to ultrasound intelligence that generalizes across heterogeneous ultrasound tasks and supports consistent end-to-end clinical workflows.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Visualization Guided Retinal Fluid Segmentation of Optical Coherence Tomography B-Scans.
abstract: Vision loss remains a critical global health issue, with conditions such as diabetic macular edema and age-related macular degeneration often detected only after substantial retinal damage. Early retinal fluid accumulation is a key biomarker, and Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) provides noninvasive, high-resolution retinal imaging essential for diagnosis. Accurate segmentation of retinal structures is crucial, yet recent conventional deep learning approaches often do not provide satisfactory performance because fluid regions occupy a small portion of the image, leading to inefficient computation and reduced accuracy. We propose CLAVIS, a novel plug-and-play pipeline that leverages CLAssification outputs to generate VIsualizations and guide Segmentation, generating more precise maps of the fluid regions. We leverage visualization techniques to target image regions that influenced the classification outcome. Experimental results demonstrate that this guidance strategy improves Dice score by$\mathbf{+ 0. 1 4}$on the average and up to$\mathbf{+ 0. 1 8}$for some pathologies.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

verified_metadata.title: Reconstruction Algorithm Based on Multi-Harmonic Feature Fusion and Enhanced U-Net for Low-Concentration Magnetic Particle Imaging
verified_metadata.conference_title: 2026 IEEE 23rd International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
verified_metadata.abstract: To address weak signals and severe background artifacts in low-concentration magnetic particle imaging, this paper proposes a noise-resilient reconstruction algorithm based on multi-harmonic feature fusion and an enhanced U-Net(MH-U-Net). Our algorithm introduces enhancements in both the signal and image domains to improve the reconstruction quality. In the signal domain, the algorithm performs a weighted fusion of the imaginary parts of the 3rd and 5th harmonics, utilizes filtered back projection to preserve highfrequency edges, and employs a grid search to determine the optimal weights. In the image domain, an optimized U-Net architecture driven by a joint loss function is employed for precise denoising. Experimental results demonstrate that our algorithm achieves high structural similarity on the training set, demonstrating a substantial performance improvement compared to the baseline algorithm provided by the official challenge dataset. It realizes MPI image reconstruction under low tracer concentrations, facilitating the biomedical applications of MPI.
